May Agni the Omniscient go forth against our foes, burning back their curses and their malice; may he confound the army of our adversaries and render them weaponless — Jātavedas, the Knower of creatures.
You are fierce for such a deed, O Maruts — advance, show mercy, prevail together; the Vasus have shown mercy to those who sought their aid. For Agni, knowing all, shall go forth against their foes.
O Maghavan, against the hostile army of those who make themselves our enemies — both of you, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, and Agni, burn them back in retaliation.
Urged forward, Indra with his two tawny steeds goes downhill; your thunderbolt goes forth crushing the foes; strike those who face you, those alongside, those who flee — make all destruction a truth and reality for them.
O Indra, bring about confusion of the army against our foes; with the rushing blast of Agni and of Wind scatter them in all directions and destroy them.
May Indra confound their army; may the Maruts strike them down with might; may Agni seize their eyes — may the enemy host return defeated.
One hundred and one viṣkandhas are spread throughout the earth. Of all of them, let this be the viṣkandha-nullifier.
Of Karṣapha, of Viśapha — Dyauṣpitā (Sky-Father) is the father, Earth the mother. Just as the gods have acted against them, so act ye against them again likewise.
The sputum-free ones (the seers) upheld it; thus was it made by Manu. I render the viṣkandha castrate (vadhri), even as one strips the scrotum from the bulls of the herd.
In the tawny cord, the knot (khṛgala) which the wise ones bind — let those who tie knots render the renowned power of kābava castrate (vadhri).

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
By which (cord) you move about in pursuit of glory, as the gods with their asura-māyā — even as an ape (kapi) is the corrupter of dogs, so are the cord-tyers the corrupters of kābava.
For ruin indeed I shall shatter you, having defiled the kābava. Like swift chariots (driven off the field), you shall career away by means of my imprecations.
From Yama's realm you have arisen, O wise one, eager to yoke mortals to intoxicated women (pramadās). You journey alone on the same chariot, O Svapna, knowing (your nature), measuring out the womb of the Asura.
Bamba first saw you everywhere, before the night, at the birth of a certain day. From that time onward you arose over this (world), O Svapna, concealing yourself in an all-pervading form.
The great pressing-stone (bṛhan grāvā) turned from the Asuras toward the gods, desiring greatness. To that Svapna the thirty-three (gods), having won their way to heaven, granted lordship.
Neither the Pitṛs nor the gods know this babblement (jalpi) that wanders here in the midst. The Āptya-men placed Svapna in Trita Āptya; the Ādityans, instructed by Varuṇa.
Let the cruel deeds of the evildoer depart from him; let the doer of good live a holy life free from evil dream. You make heaven drunk with your highest kinsman; you are born from the tormented mind of one who suffers.
We know all your kindred from of old; we know, O Svapna, who here is your overlord. Protect our glory with glory here; go far away, depart to a distance from those who hate us.
O Mothers (Ambās), fair-faced ones, release (the waters) with their creatures; release what is truly to be known. I send forth messengers to slay this poison. The potent water (vār) — the sap-drained poison, the serpent-born (āheya) — the poison sap-drained, rendered non-poisonous.
I invoke Indra here, the soma-drinker, vigorous on both sides (ubhayāvin), to slay this poison. The potent water — the sap-drained poison, the serpent-born — the poison sap-drained, rendered non-poisonous.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
I invoke fierce Varuṇa here together with the royal lords (rājanyās), to slay this poison. The potent water — the sap-drained poison, the serpent-born — the poison sap-drained, rendered non-poisonous.
I invoke Aditi here, daughter of the sun (sūraputrī), the maiden (kanīnikā), to slay this poison. The potent water — the sap-drained poison, the serpent-born — the poison sap-drained, rendered non-poisonous.
I invoke Bṛhaspati here, who is the purohita (domestic priest) of the gods, to slay this poison. The potent water — the sap-drained poison, the serpent-born — the poison sap-drained, rendered non-poisonous.
The āṇas, the cāṇas, and the caṇḍāmarkas — (I invoke them) to slay this poison. The potent water — the sap-drained poison, the serpent-born — the poison sap-drained, rendered non-poisonous.
Of the nine, of the ninety, of the festering poisons — of all of them I have seized the name. The poison whose sap has utterly departed: gone, removed, sap-drained is the poison.
Death is one, Yama is one, Śarva is one, the arrow-hurler is Bhava — may they fashion healing for us, away from the divine hosts.
May Yama restore us together with the Fathers; may Mitra and Varuṇa, Vāyu and Agni restore us; may the slayer of evil, the proclaimer of evil, restore us; may the goddess Nirṛti restore us once more.
The arrow that has flown dispatched by the gods, or that which has been released toward heat or toward the great power — may Soma the knowing drive it away from us, or the Fathers invoked by the gods, who behold mankind.
May the thousand-eyed immortal one, of manifold forms, protect here. In your friendship, O fierce one, may I come to no harm — you who are companion to the cow and companion to man.
The fury of yours, O Thousand-eyed one, that is poured round with poison — with that same fury be gracious to us; come to us as benign, as Śambhu.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
May no world of mine fall under your wrath, O Thousand-eyed one, in your blazing fury. Go to him who hates us; strike down him whom we hate.
Those gods who stand in the eastern quarter, named Hetayas — their arrows are Agni. May they show us mercy, may they speak on our behalf. Homage to them; svāhā to them.
Those gods who stand in the southern quarter, named Aviṣyavaḥ — their arrows are the Waters. May they show us mercy, may they speak on our behalf. Homage to them; svāhā to them.
Those gods who stand in the western quarter, named Virājaḥ — their arrows are Kāma. May they show us mercy, may they speak on our behalf. Homage to them; svāhā to them.
Those gods who stand in the northern quarter, named Pravidhyantaḥ — their arrows are Vāyu. May they show us mercy, may they speak on our behalf. Homage to them; svāhā to them.
Those gods who stand in the fixed (nadir) quarter, named Vilimpāḥ — their arrows are Food. May they show us mercy, may they speak on our behalf. Homage to them; svāhā to them.
Those gods who stand in the upper quarter, named Aviṣyantaḥ — their arrows are Rain. May they show us mercy, may they speak on our behalf. Homage to them; svāhā to them.
He who dwells within the Waters, he who dwells within Vṛtra, he who is in man, he who is in the stone — he who has entered into the herbs and into the trees of the forest: may this oblation be offered to those fires.
He who dwells within Soma, he who dwells within cattle, he who has entered into birds and into wild beasts — he who has entered into two-footed creatures and into four-footed ones: may this oblation be offered to those fires.
He who shares a chariot with Indra, Vaiśvānara the all-consuming one — him I invoke with repeated calls, the one who ever conquers in battles: may this oblation be offered to those fires.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
That god whom they call the all-devourer, whom they call Kāma, whom they call the giver and the receiver — he the wise, the mighty, the encompassing, the undeceivable: may this oblation be offered to those fires.
Thee whom thirteen world-beings and five human ones recognized in mind as the hotar-priest — for the bearing of vital luster, for glory, for the one rich in true speech: may this oblation be offered to those fires.
To him whose food is the bull, whose food is the cow, who bears Soma upon his back, the wise ordainer — to the eldest forms of Vaiśvānara: may this oblation be offered to those fires.
Those who move in succession through heaven, earth, and atmosphere, those who pursue the lightning — those who dwell within the quarters and those who dwell within the wind: may this oblation be offered to those fires.
Bṛhaspati, Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni, the golden-handed Savitṛ, Indra — all the gods and the Aṅgirasas we invoke: may they appease this flesh-devouring fire.
Appeased is the flesh-devouring fire, and also the man-seeking one. And that which is the all-devourer — that flesh-eating fire I have wholly pacified.
Here has come the parṇa-amulet, powerful, crushing rivals by its might; the vigour of the gods, the sap of plants — may it invigorate sovereignty in me without faltering.
In me hold sovereignty, O parṇa-amulet; in me establish splendour; may I, in the overlordship of the realm, be allied with you and be supreme.
The prize, the dear hidden treasure, that the gods deposited in a forest tree — may Indra bestow that amulet upon me together with long life, to be worn.
The leaf of Soma has come hither with powerful force, given by Indra, in friendship by Varuṇa; I wear it, shining brilliantly in many ways, for long life, for a hundred autumns.
May the parṇa-amulet cling fast to me for my complete uninjuredness, so that I may be supreme over the human accumulation of riches.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
May vital power return to me, may the self, wealth, and the brahman return; may the dhiṣṇya fires arrange themselves back in their proper stations, right here.
The carpenters, the chariot-makers, the blacksmiths, and the wise counsellors — subdue them all, O Parṇa; make my people into submissive attendants.
Let there be a submissive attendant whether Vaiśya, or Śūdra, or noble Ārya — subdue them all, O Parṇa; make my people into submissive attendants.
That by which you became a barren woman — that we destroy; this very thing we lay away far from you, elsewhere, at a distance.
May an embryo enter your womb, a male, like an arrow into a quiver; may a hero be born here — your son at ten months.
Bear a male child, a son; after him may another male be born; may you become a mother of sons — of those already born and those yet to be born.
With the good seeds that bulls engender, find a son for yourself with those; be a prolific cow, a milch-cow.
I make for you the Prajāpati rite; may the embryo enter your womb; find a son, O woman — one who shall be a blessing to you, and you in turn shall be a blessing to him.
Those divine plants whose father was Parjanya and whose mother was the Earth — may they, the goddesses, help you toward the finding of a son.
That bull who shall stir your womb together with his seed — may he pour into you offspring of long life, lasting a hundred autumns.
The plant that the great bull with the moist navel, Vāta, enclosed — from it I bring up for you the all-sustaining poison-neutralizer.
The plant that the boar rooted up in a single lotus-pond — from it I bring up for you the all-sustaining poison-neutralizer.
The plant that Aditi sowed as seed-sower upon a lotus-pond — from it I bring up for you the all-sustaining poison-neutralizer.
She whose nest is within the waters in the great ocean — from it I bring up for you the all-sustaining poison-neutralizer.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
I bring up for you from the highest; from the lowest I bring up for you; from the middle-ones the middle one — I bring up that poison-neutralizer.
I seized, together I seized, both ends together I seized; I bring up the poison-neutralizer of heaven and earth.
The serpent was not as an embryo; the serpent struck the stone-cloud and rendered its venom impotent. By the brahman of the poison it came into being — from that, alive, you shall not escape.
The serpent is scorched, the serpent is utterly scorched, rendered juiceless, made powerless. By the brahman of the poison it came into being — from that, alive, you shall not escape.
I give back your venom to you — you have indeed reached your former step. You think yourself one who has bitten me; bitten by me, you shall not escape.
One hundred and one are the remedies; of them you are the mother, O herb. You flow down to the ocean, established upon the earth.
In her I know the remedy: the ten-headed, ten-tongued one. He who first gathered you — may he fare well, O herb; and he to whom the heroic physician gave you — may he be well.
May sight return again, may breath return again, may life's span return again to us. I have extracted you by the counter-rite; by the counter-rite I have extracted you.
I release you from the bond of the curse, and also from that which belongs to Varuṇa; and from the foot-fetter of Yama, from every transgression against the gods.
Well joined are the skull-plates of your head and of your heart — those who know them. The rising sun, Āditya, has caused the body's radiance to shine forth.
Flow forth from Himavat; your confluence is in the Sindhu. Let all those waters, gathering together, bestow sight and breath upon us.
May the elephant-splendour spread wide, the great glory that arose from the body of Aditi. All of that — this which is Savitṛ's — let all the gods together with Aditi grant to me.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Let Mitra and Varuṇa, and Indra and Rudra fashion it. Let the gods, sustainers of all, anoint me with that splendour.
That great radiance of yours, O Jātavedas, which blazes up when you are invoked — with that radiance today, O Agni, make me full of splendour.
By that splendour whereby the elephant came into being, whereby the king stands foremost among men, whereby the gods ascended heaven with their light — with that splendour, O Agni, unite me here.
As great as is the splendour of the sun and of the mighty elephant — that much splendour, O you two Aśvins garlanded with lotus-wreaths, create for me.
As far as the four cardinal directions, as far as the eye reaches in its range — let that vital power, that elephant-splendour, gather itself entirely within me.
Sharpened is this brahman-power of mine, sharpened my heroic might; sharpened is my conquering kṣatra-force — of those for whom I am the purohita.
I sharpen for them the kingdom, I sharpen vigor, heroic might, and strength; I hew off the arms of the enemies, and I sharpen my own men.
Sharper than the edge of Agni's axe, and sharper still — sharper than the vajra of Indra are those for whom I am the purohita.
May they fall down, may they be brought low, those who assail Indra the bountiful overlord. I wound the enemies with brahman-power; I raise up my own men.
I sharpen the weapons of these men; I make their kingdom flourish with good heroes. May their kṣatra-power be ageless and conquering; may all the gods win over their fierce resolve.
Go forward, conquer, urged onward! I sharpen your weapons, O men. You of sharp arrows and powerful bows — strike down the weaklings; you of fierce weapons and mighty arms!
Right here I set firm the house, that it may stand in peace, sprinkled with ghee. O house, may we approach you — all heroes, good heroes, heroes unharmed.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Stand firm right here, O house — you who possess horses, who possess cattle, who possess pleasant speech; full of vigor, full of ghee, full of milk — rise up for great good fortune!
You are a support, O house, of great meter, storing good grain. May the calf low toward you, may the young child, may the milk-cows come streaming in at evening.
May Savitṛ, Vāyu, Agni, Tvaṣṭṛ, the hotar — knowing it — firmly establish this house. May the Maruts sprinkle it from their udder with ghee; may Bhaga, our king, extend our tillage.
O wife of Māna, sheltering and pleasant goddess — you were first established by the gods. Clothed in grass, benevolent, may you be; bestow on us, O auspicious one, wealth rich in good heroes.
Into you may the young boy come, and the calf together with the herd; into you may the jar of fermented grain and the pot of curds flow in.
Magnify this kṣatriya of mine, O Indra; make him the sole bull of the clans. Drive away all his enemies; subdue them for him in the coming contests.
May he be the lord of lords of wealth; may he be king, the lord of the clans. Place great splendors in him, O Indra; render his enemy devoid of splendor.
Allot to him a share in the village, in horses, in cattle; cut off from his share whoever is his enemy. May he be the highest king among the kṣatra-powers; O Indra, subdue all the foes for him.
May Heaven and Earth milk out abundant treasure for him, like a milk-cow yielding warm milk. May this king be dear to Indra, dear to the cows, to the plants, and to the waters.
I yoke for you Indra, who brings victory — by whom they conquer and are never conquered — who shall make you the sole bull of the peoples and the highest of human kings, O king.
May you be supreme; may all the others be lower — whoever, O king, are your adversaries. As sole bull, as the companion of Indra, as the victor, trample upon the great deeds of those who would be your enemies.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
O horn-faced one, of Āṅgirasa descent, born of the gods, all-perceiving — born of heaven and earth, O Thousand-eyed one, be here for us.
O thousand-eyed herb, thou who seest beyond the snare — ever flame-armed, slayer of demons, be here as our all-perceiving one.
Those who steal away the freshly pressed libation and the abundance of milk, O herb — seize thou them, O Thousand-eyed one, O thou of proven might.
Those who deliver the afflicted one into ruin and the wounded man who is exposed — seize thou them, O Thousand-eyed one, O thou of proven might.
As the four-eyed horse sees through the night in darkness, so dost thou, O Thousand-eyed one, look forward upon him who approaches.
Purchased with cows, with horses, with riches art thou, O herb. With the eye of the dark horse, look upon the demons, the Kimīdins.
Come together, drink together; let your food be sweet and shared. Let all your vows be unanimously the same; let your minds be of one accord.
Be of one mind; let Indra be your common guide; let this Agni, the carrier downward, bring peace to you. Whatever hostility, whatever terror there was — may all the gods wash that away.
May Bṛhaspati be well-being for you; may both heaven and earth be well-being; may the atmosphere too, and the Marutvān, be well-being for you; may Aditi, mother of gods, be well-being for you.
May heaven and earth be well-ordered; may the waters and the plants be well-ordered; may all the fires, together in their shared vow, be well-ordered for this pre-eminence.
I unite your hearts; let your minds be united; let your bodies be united; let your breath of life be united.
I unite the hearts of your cattle; I unite those of your sons and of your daughters; I unite the minds of your wives in harmony with their minds; I unite even the sight of your husbands.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The eastern quarter — Agni is its overlord, Asita its guardian, the Ādityas its arrows. Homage to those overlords, homage to those guardians, homage to those arrows, homage be to you. He who hates us, he whom we hate — him we place in your jaws; let the breath of life abandon him.
The southern quarter — Indra is its overlord, Tiraścirājī its guardian, the Vasus its arrows. Homage to those overlords, homage to those guardians, homage to those arrows, homage be to you. He who hates us, he whom we hate — him we place in your jaws; let the breath of life abandon him.
The western quarter — Varuṇa is its overlord, Pṛdākū its guardian, Mitra its arrows. Homage to those overlords, homage to those guardians, homage to those arrows, homage be to you. He who hates us, he whom we hate — him we place in your jaws; let the breath of life abandon him.
The northern quarter — Soma is its overlord, Svaja its guardian, Vāta its arrows. Homage to those overlords, homage to those guardians, homage to those arrows, homage be to you. He who hates us, he whom we hate — him we place in your jaws; let the breath of life abandon him.
The fixed (nadir) quarter — Viṣṇu is its overlord, Kalmāṣagrīva its guardian, the plants its arrows. Homage to those overlords, homage to those guardians, homage to those arrows, homage be to you. He who hates us, he whom we hate — him we place in your jaws; let the breath of life abandon him.
The upward quarter — Bṛhaspati is its overlord, Citra its guardian, the thunderbolt its arrows. Homage to those overlords, homage to those guardians, homage to those arrows, homage be to you. He who hates us, he whom we hate — him we place in your jaws; let the breath of life abandon him.
The bull (anaḍvān) upholds the earth and yonder sky; the bull upholds the wide midspace. The bull upholds the six broad quarters; the bull has entered into this entire world.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The bull is milked for the realm of good deeds; may Pavamāna swell him from the east. Parjanya is the stream, the Maruts are his udder; sacrifice is the milk, the sacrificial fee is the milking.
The bull — he is Indra — surveys the beasts; he measures out the threefold path. Yielding milk of what has been and what shall be, bearing all the ordinances of the gods, he moves about.
Of him neither the lord of sacrifice holds power, nor does sacrifice itself; neither the giver nor the receiver rules over him. He who bears all, who fashions all — tell us of the gharma vessel: which of the four-footed ones is he?
This one is Indra; among human beings the heated gharma moves, blazing bright. He who, knowing it, would not eat of the bull's flesh shall not be stirred in his generous bounty — he shall be rich in offspring.
By that by which the gods ascended to heaven, having left the body — the abode of immortality — by that may we attain the realm of good deeds: by the vow of the gharma, by glory, by fervent austerity.
These twelve nights they call the observance nights of Prajāpati. Therein also is the vow of brahman; therein also is the strength of the bull.
Those twelve observance nights of Prajāpati that they speak of — he who knows the brahman therein knows verily the strength of the bull.
The bull is milked at evening, milked at dawn, milked by day. Those milkings of his that come together — we know them from his followers.
He who knows the seven milkings of the bull through his devotees — he attains offspring and the heavenly realm; so indeed the seven ṛṣis know.
This is the middle part of the bull where his yoke-bar is set. His forward part extends as far as his hinder part is gathered in.
Treading the ploughshare down with his hooves, churning up the soil with his shanks — by toil the bull and the ploughman together approach the sweet drink of refreshment.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
This one is called the bull among human beings; he is Indra. May his hooves not be harmed, nor any of his leg joints.
By strength thou art Indra, by vow thou art Parameṣṭhin; by that whereby the cow exists, thou art Vaiśvadeva. Him who hates us, whom we hate — crush together his vital breaths, tear asunder his vital breaths.
I approach the houses rejoicing in my mind, bearing vigor, intent on wealth, of keen intelligence. Beholding the milk of the houses with a benign, friendly eye, I rise up.
These houses are sources of joy, full of vigor, full of milk, standing laden with good things — may they recognize us as those who know them.
Rich in pleasant words, blessed, food-abounding, glad with laughter — O houses free from hunger and thirst, be not afraid of us.
The houses to which one returns when traveling abroad, in which there is great goodwill — those houses we invite; may they know us as we arrive.
As cattle are called home, as goats and sheep are called home — so too may the sweet drink of food be called home into our houses.
Called in are friends of great wealth and sweet delight; unharmed and with all their folk, may our houses be so always.
May this one be a slayer, irresistible in attack — Indra who has prevailed, standing firm in battles. Prajāpati has bestowed upon him great vigor, the great oblation, growing strong through the offered oblation.
O Prajāpati, with the growth-conferring oblation thou hast made Indra a slayer, impossible to strike down. Before him the clans created by the gods bow down; for he verily is the smiter, he verily has become the one worthy of oblation.
O Prajāpati, lead us toward better fortune, to a wide cattle-pasture, O overcomer of assailants — strengthening Indra for great battle, the god with the god-strengthening oblation.
As thou shalt conquer all battle arrays, as thou shalt prevail overwhelming enemies, as thou shalt be sovereign, a great sovereign — even so may Indra make thee irresistible in smiting.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
May this hero smite enemies without check; all you gods, clear away his adversaries. Do not injure his offspring nor his heroes — may Indra make him irresistible in smiting.
Strike the enemies, make them subject to thee — Agni is thy guardian, the most excellent overlord. May King Varuṇa grant thee shelter — even so may Indra make thee irresistible in smiting.
May you two touch each other with your bodies, may you touch each other with your faces, with your very selves; Bṛhaspati and Soma bring you two into mutual contact.
I fix his name upon him with my speech — he shall not be released from it; let me seize hold of him in longing, as one seizes a dark one in a muddy pit.
The love-charm that was in the beloved one, bestowed by tawny Soma — from that charm, renowned above all others, his mind has been fixed upon me.
Whatever man you desire, in whomsoever you wish to find your good fortune — in him we place a heart-burning, so that he shall pine away after you.
Just as his heart shall wither — like a string freshly severed — let his gaze grow terrible, sky-wide, and let him weep aloud, unable to see me.
That supreme maker-of-love, brought here by the honey-licker — you indeed are possessed of radiance, and you indeed are truly auspicious; moreover, among all plants you are called the maker-of-love.
You, O herb, face Soma; you face likewise the sun; you face all the gods — so too we address you directly.
I dig up this herb that spreads wide, that stretches along the ground — that which greets the one who comes, and turns back the one who departs.
Of yonder man, as he departs and as he comes, I have seized the mind; I have seized the mind that resides in his hand, and also the mind that dwells in his heart.
Upon me your mind is fixed, upon me your thought, upon me your vow; in my intention may you be, and together let us dwell in my heart.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Let me speak — not you; in the assembly, you shall not speak; let you be mine alone, and do not praise any other woman.
Whether you be beyond the folk, or whether you be beyond the rivers — let this herb bring you back to me, as if binding you and leading you home.
Kings have gone to union, debts have gone to union, skin-diseases have gone to union, clans have gone to union; toward us let good dreams be gathered together — we drive the ill dream away to the one who hates us.
O Embryo of the wives of the gods, O instrument of Yama — whatever dream is auspicious, that is mine; whatever is evil, that we dispatch to the one who hates us.
Tṛṣṇāman is your name; you are the face of the dark bird, the face of Nirṛti — thus we know you, O Dream, for what you are.
You, O Dream, carry off the bodiless one as a horse carries a load; like a horse you have dragged us in the night — carry off the god-reviler, the slanderer, who is not ours.
Whatever ill dream there is among us, whatever among our cattle, and whatever in our house — the god-reviler and slanderer who is not ours: let him be released with that, as one releases a necklace-amulet.
Measuring off nine cubits away from our bodies — all ill dream, all ill omen, we consign to the one who hates us.
O gods, O Maruts born of Pṛśni, grant the waters, cleave the deep reservoir — from broad heaven, from earth, from the atmosphere — for this sovereignty, for the Brahmins through this sacred word, for the offspring, for these, for the herbs: svāhā!
O gods — Agni, Indra, Sūrya — grant the waters, cleave the deep reservoir [from broad heaven, from earth, from the atmosphere — for this sovereignty, for the Brahmins through this sacred word, for the offspring, for these, for the herbs: svāhā!]
O gods yoked together — Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman — grant the waters [cleave the deep reservoir, from broad heaven, from earth, from the atmosphere — for this sovereignty, for the Brahmins through this sacred word, for the offspring, for these, for the herbs: svāhā!]

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
O gods, O Fathers, the near descendants of Āyu who consume the raw offering — grant the waters [cleave the deep reservoir, from broad heaven, from earth, from the atmosphere — for this sovereignty, for the Brahmins through this sacred word, for the offspring, for these, for the herbs: svāhā!]
O gods who dwell in the waters — Apāṃ Napāt, Tanūnapāt, Narāśaṃsa — grant the waters, cleave the deep reservoir [from broad heaven, from earth, from the atmosphere — for this sovereignty, for the Brahmins through this sacred word, for the offspring, for these, for the herbs: svāhā!]
O god Bṛhaspati, set forth the waters, cleave the ocean [from broad heaven, from earth, from the atmosphere — for this sovereignty, for the Brahmins through this sacred word, for the offspring, for these, for the herbs: svāhā!]
O god Prajāpati, set forth the waters, cleave the ocean [from broad heaven, from earth, from the atmosphere — for this sovereignty, for the Brahmins through this sacred word, for the offspring, for these, for the herbs: svāhā!]
O god Parameṣṭhin, set forth the waters, cleave the ocean — from broad heaven, from earth, from the atmosphere — for this sovereignty, for the Brahmins through this sacred word, for the offspring, for these, for the herbs: svāhā!
These creatures here that are being born and those already born from Prajāpati — make them known to this one; may the all-knowing approve and consent.
Those beasts — the four-footed ones over whom Paśupati holds sway, or those that are two-footed — once ransomed they go as sacrificial offerings to the sacred realm; may they accompany the sacrificer for the flourishing of wealth.
As they release it, O guardians of the world, O gods, bestow passage upon the sacrificer; that which stood prepared and laboring — may the dear path of the gods be attained.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Those who gazed upon it with contemplation as it was being bound, who watched it with mind and with eye — Agni first released them, the god who is in accord with Prajāpati together with his offspring.
Those whose vital breaths were bound in the tether of cattle, of beasts, and of men — Indra first released them, the god who is in accord with Prajāpati together with his offspring.
The wild forest beasts of all forms, and those of all forms as well as those of a single form — Vāyu first released them, the god who is in accord with Prajāpati together with his offspring.
May the gods, fully knowing, receive the vital breath moving about from limb to limb; go to heaven, stand firm with your bodies, travel to the celestial world by auspicious paths.
May the years, O Agni, may the seasons strengthen you; may the year and the seers who are truth itself augment you; blaze together with resplendent brightness; shine upon all four quarters.
Kindle yourself together, O Agni, and awaken him; stand up high for great good fortune; may the worshippers who approach you here not be harmed; may the Brahmins who tend you here be renowned and worthy of honor.
These Brahmins choose you, O Agni; be auspicious and propitious to us, O Agni; O Agni, be the slayer of rivals, the conqueror of adversaries; shine in your own abode without faltering.
Hold fast the wealth here, O Agni; may those who harbor ill intent, the deceivers with prior cunning, not beguile you; may sovereignty well-controlled belong to you, O Agni; may he who approaches you in worship grow, unvanquished.
Seize hold by your own sovereign power, O Agni; strive after friendship's due with the friend, O Agni; may you be chief among kinsmen, the pre-eminent one in their midst; among these kings, O Agni, blaze here as one worthy of invocation.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Beyond the snares, beyond the forces of dissolution, beyond hostilities, beyond those who hate — surpass all adversities, O Agni; then grant us wealth together with heroic offspring.
Invincible Jātavedas, unassailed, resplendent sovereign — blaze here, O Agni, with powers of dominion; releasing afflictions from human beings, guard us today on all sides with auspicious homesteads.
This is your ritual womb, O Agni, from which, having been born, you shone forth. Knowing it, mount it — then increase our wealth.
We invoke the bountiful one, Agni the fierce, for our aid — the pure one who is the mightiest slayer of Vṛtra.
O Agni, speak forth toward us here; be well-disposed, facing us. Grant us boons, O lord of clans — you are our wealth-giver.
Let Aryaman grant us, let Bhaga grant us, let Bṛhaspati grant us; let Pūṣan grant us — and may the divine Sūnṛtā bestow wealth upon us.
Rouse Aryaman, Bṛhaspati, and Indra to give; rouse Vāta, Viṣṇu, Sarasvatī, and Savitār, the prize-winner, to give.
We invoke King Soma for aid, and Agni with hymns; we invoke Āditya, Viṣṇu, Sūrya, and Brahmaṇaspati.
Indra-and-Vāyu and Bṛhaspati — we invoke them here as easy to call, so that at our assembly the whole world may be well-disposed toward us.
You, O Agni, augment our brahman-power and sacrifice with the fires; you, O god, impel wealth for us toward bestowal and giving.
At the impulsion of the prize-winner this came into being, and within it all these worlds — it compels even the reluctant to give, knowing; and may it bestow on us wealth rich in all heroes.
May the five directions milk for me, may the broad ones milk for me according to their strength; may I attain every intention with mind and heart.
May I rise with speech that wins cattle; do not cover me over with brilliance. May Vāyu surround me from all sides; may Tvaṣṭṛ be steadied for prosperity.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
From whatever we fear, O Indra, from that make us fearless; O Maghavan, be capable — with your aids sunder the enemies, shatter the foes.
We invoke Indra, the granter of success; may we prosper with bipeds and quadrupeds. Let no hostile armies encroach upon us; O Indra, destroy the treacheries scattering in all directions.
Indra is our protector, the slayer of Vṛtra, the guardian of our farthest boundary, the most excellent. May he be our protector from the outermost, from the middle, from behind, and from before.
Lead us, knowing, into a broad world — the celestial light, freedom from fear, well-being. O Indra, may we dwell under the shelter of your two mighty arms, the arms of the ancient one, the vast shelter.
The atmosphere makes us fearless, both heaven and earth make us fearless; fearlessness behind, fearlessness before — from above and from below, may there be fearlessness for us.
Fearlessness from the friend, fearlessness from the foe, fearlessness from the known, fearlessness before us; fearlessness by night, fearlessness by day for us — may all directions become my friend.
Go forward to victory, do not retreat; drive into the rivals' knowledge. Indra the terrible, slayer of rivals, has set victory altogether stirring for you.
You shall conquer; you shall not be conquered — in small battles, O Maghavan, and in great ones. We whet even you, the fierce one, for our aid; so, O Indra, be gracious to us in our invocations.
His two arms win cattle, matchless in resolve in battle, action after action; of a hundred aids, impetuous by nature — Indra has fashioned unparalleled might. So, O Indra, be gracious to us in our invocations.
I know the dear treasure of Indra, his secret name in the battle; that Maghavan indeed conquers when he is mine — may our warrior come to our invocation in the calling of war.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
May we conquer, yoked with you, O sustained one; raise up our share battle by battle. Make wide room and easy passage for us, O Indra; O Maghavan, crush the virile powers of the enemies.
You we invoke first among the gods; you have been the conqueror in battles. This singer of ours — eager, ardent, bursting forth — may you, O Indra, set his chariot foremost at the start.
Remember! You are Smara; you have been given by the gods — remember! Fix upon the mind of that man yonder; let it be just as I desire.
Burn his heart; go, O Kāma! Let the fever in his limbs blaze and torment of itself. Let his longings be consumed by obsessive thoughts — this woman alone shall be his direction; no other day, no other.
Joyless, causing swoons, confounders of the mind, leading astray, making one lose his purpose, roaming the wilderness — those ādhyaḥ that enter and possess, that spread and inflame: these very obsessive thoughts I send forth with the sacred formula.
Lacerators of the heart, timely ones, destroyers of village-food, severers of sleep, killers of the mighty, confounders of the mind — those ādhyaḥ that enter and possess, that spread and inflame: these very obsessive thoughts I send forth with the sacred formula.
Indra and Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa, both Heaven and Earth, Mātariśvan, the Aśvins, god Savitṛ, and Bhaga — let all of these smite his mind; let him find no repose here.
Let the thirty-three gods smite you; let the ādhyaḥ carry obsessive thoughts right into you. Let the incantations of Bharadvāja have dominion over you — drift away like a boat cut loose from its mooring!
These ādhyaḥ fly down like lightning-flashes of the rainy season. Become the receiver of them at evening, as cows return to their pen.
The ādhyaḥ cast down headlong — I lodge them within you. Let them attend upon you, goading you, rousing you without cease.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
These ādhyaḥ I send forth against you with the sacred formula — sated ones, with ill-fortune as their foremost cow. Let them wither you like a blade of grass, and let them make you weep bitterly.
The aja (goat; the unborn) was indeed born from Agni's grief; it beheld its progenitor at the first. By means of it the gods attained divinity in the beginning; by means of it the wise ones mounted upward upon the rungs.
Step upward by means of the fires toward the vault of heaven, holding the cooking-pot in your hands. Having gone to the back of the sky, to the solar light, mingle and ascend together with the gods.
O Agni, go forth first among those who seek the gods — eye of the gods and of mortals alike. May the sacrificers, striving and in fellowship with the Bhṛgus, go to the solar world in well-being.
Going to the solar light, they looked back no longer; let the generous ones ascend the sky. Those who, knowing well, stretched out the sacrifice that pours forth on every side.
I anoint the rice-porridge with strength and ghee — the divine ocean, the great milky expanse. By means of it may we reach the world of the well-doer, rising upward to the highest vault of heaven.
Your two ageless, winged pinions, O Odana, with which you drive away the demons — by means of those two may we fly to the world of the well-doer, where the ancient seers, the first-born of old, dwell.
From where you stand, O Odana, on the back of heaven, in the wide expanse above — the Brāhmaṇas who hold the eternal law followed you along together with their generous bounty.
From the surface of the earth I have ascended to the mid-region; from the mid-region I have ascended to the sky. From the back of the sky's vault I have gone to the solar light.
You are the aja (unborn/goat), O aja; you are heaven. By means of you the Aṅgirasas came to know the world. That world may we come to know in turn.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
By that with which you carry a thousand, or by that with which you carry all-wealth — by that carry this sacrifice of ours to the solar world, for us to go among the gods.
Cook the aja and the five rice-porridges. Having cooked the aja and the five rice-porridges, the gods fully attained the worlds.
The offspring-channel of yours that was stopped up of old by the Aśvins through the Dhruva (fixed peg) — that I now bring back for you. May Agni Vaiśvānara give it back to you again from the highest firmament.
You, O Agni, are her second auspicious husband — bestow upon her progeny reaching to old age. Release her from whatever bondage Nirṛti has seized her with. O Agni, grant offspring to this woman who desires offspring.
This woman who desires sons venerates you, O Agni the bull, with bent knee — she calls out to you. Mount her with benevolence; unite her with the progeny of Prajāpati.
For you, O Agni, this woman who desires sons pours an oblation of pure, clarified ghee. Leap upon her, exert your virility; you who hold the seed, O mighty one — unite her with progeny.
From the mountain, from the womb of heaven, drawn together limb by limb — the seed of the god of gods I have placed in the womb like a leaf upon a branch.
The navel-cord fell at the birth of Indra; one god, the eager one, caught hold of it. By means of you, O Agni, may we Brāhmaṇas who drink Soma prosper, and also she who does not give birth.
From the sharpener abandonment is born; from the arrow-shaft abandonment arises. He neither yearns nor grieves, O tejana, who carries you.
You are of ancient standing, O tejana; ancient is your shattering power. Ancient be that desire by which we desire yonder one.
As long as a burning arrow, speeding forth, creates fear among people — so long may you, O tejana, be a fiery force of abandonment here.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The waters have granted me the power of abandonment; the Maruts have granted me the power of abandonment; all the gods have granted me the power of abandonment; the Fathers have granted me the power of abandonment.
By that power I have surpassed the women of others, the rivals, from before. Before the haters I have surpassed; before midday too; before the evening I have surpassed — for in the tejana there is great power.
Heaven has stood firm; earth has stood firm; this entire universe has stood firm. Firm stands he from whom love was wrested away — may this desire of yours stand firm.
Hiraṇyagarbha came into being at the first; he arose as the single lord of all that exists. He upheld this earth and yonder heaven — to that god let us offer with oblation.
He who gives vital force and gives strength, he whose command all the gods attend — whose shadow is immortality, whose shadow is death — to that god let us offer with oblation.
He who became the sustainer and lord of all the moving world, of the breathing and the blinking — who is master of the two-footed and of the four-footed — to that god let us offer with oblation.
By whom the mighty heaven and the firm earth were fixed, by whom the celestial vault was propped, by whom the firmament — who measured out the vast atmosphere — to that god let us offer with oblation.
He who propped these two trembling heaven and earth and held them firm by his help — over whom the sun spreads forth its course — to that god let us offer with oblation.
He of whose greatness all the Himavat mountains declare the ocean together with Rasā — whose are the directions and the five divine quarters — to that god let us offer with oblation.
The waters that bear all life, the mothers who gave birth to the embryo — therein the god above the gods took his seat, within the one-pillared, measured, firm and mighty.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The waters, generating the embryo, brought forth the calf at the first. And as he was being born, his birth-membrane was of gold.
Golden was the birth-membrane of him who was born as the calf at the first. Great Diti beheld him as he came forth from the two wombs flowing apart.
The existent one pours nourishment into all existing beings; he has become the overlord of all beings. He who is Death performs the royal consecration — may that king approve this kingdom.
Advance, make yourself heroic — terrible perceiver, slayer of rivals! Stand firm, O increaser of allies; on your behalf the gods have spoken.
All beings have adorned him as he mounts; robed in glory he moves, self-luminous. Great is that name of the virile Asura — the all-formed one has stood firm in the immortal realms.
Embracing him as the tiger, they urge the lion on to great good fortune. Like a well-armed buffalo standing firm, they groom the leopard within the waters.
O tiger on the tiger-skin, stride forth across the great directions! May all the peoples come to you, and the heavenly milk-rich waters.
The heavenly waters that rejoice with milk, those of the atmosphere, and those of the earth — with the radiant power of all those waters together I anoint you.
I have anointed you with radiant splendor together with heavenly milk. May Savitṛ make you thus — one who increases allies.
O Kaśyapa, that which is brilliant, bright-shining, and full — that which is full, abundant and of wondrous radiance — in which the seven suns are together set — upon that let us place the king in sovereignty.
By those skills with which, knowing, you strengthened the widespread ones, by those with which you adorned the heaven, by those full and inexhaustible powers with which you adorned speech — with that splendor, O Agni, unite me here.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
By those banners by which the sun shines forth, by those by which Agni of wondrous radiance was beheld, by those by which the waters of moon-bright hue came alive — with that splendor, O Agni, unite me here.
May this one shine upon the five divine quarters; may he be first among the people, like Indra. Place in him fullness and wondrous radiance; may this one fill the lap of the two realms.
May Indra protect you in accord, may Bṛhaspati protect you in accord, may Soma have protected you in accord, and Agni in accord. May all the gods protect you in accord — the seven kings who are consecrated from above.
May Mitra and Varuṇa protect you in accord here, may Heaven and Earth protect you in accord with their plants. May the sun protect you in accord with its days; may the moon protect you with the stars in accord.
May Heaven and Earth, both all-knowing, carry you — the brilliant, the vast, the south. May Soma and Agni, attentive, be aware; may Pūṣan protect you, Savitṛ with his impulsion.
O Agni, bring hither the yātudhāna who is chanting praise, the kimīdin — for thou hast indeed become the slayer of the dasyu, most favored of the gods.
O Parameṣṭhin of the oblation, O Jātavedas, O master of thy body — O Agni, having partaken of the tula-offering, cause the yātudhānas to cry out in distress.
Let the yātudhānas wail — those ravenous devourers who are kimīdins — and do thou, O Agni, and Indra, find delight in this our oblation.
Let Agni seize him from the front; let the mighty-armed Indra drive him on — let every sorcerer come forward declaring, 'Here I am!'
I behold thy powers, O Jātavedas; declare to us the yātudhānas, O thou who seest men. Scorched by thee on every side, let them come forward openly proclaiming themselves — hither to this place.
Seize them, O Jātavedas; subdue them for the desire of the heart. Arise as our messenger, O Agni; bring the yātudhānas hither.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Do thou, O Agni, bring the yātudhānas here in bonds — then let Indra with his vajra split open their skulls.
May this oblation carry away the yātudhānas as a river carries foam. Whoever — whether woman or man — has done this deed, let that person come hither and give praise.
O Soma-drinker, strike down the offspring of the yātudhāna and lead them away; of the one who is chanting, strike out the upper eye and also the lower.
This chanting one has come — recognize him, take pleasure in seizing him. O Bṛhaspati, bring him under control; O Agni and Soma, pierce him through.
Thee whom the Gandharva dug up for Varuṇa, for the nurturing of the dead — thee, that herb which arouses the phallus, we now dig up.
Bulls are thy diggers; a bull art thou, O herb. Thou art virile, endowed with virility — for the sake of the virile one we dig thee up.
Up rises the Dawn, up rises the Sun, up rises the vigorous power of the herbs — Prajāpati, the bull, stirs with potent, prize-winning force.
Make this one erect upward — just as when two growing shoots bend low as if scorched by heat — let this herb make thee more vigorous than that.
Thou art the sap of the waters, of the herbs, and of the forest trees; thou art moreover the brother of Soma — thou art the virile power belonging to the ṛṣi's lineage.
The vigour of the horse, of the spotted deer, of the he-goat, and of the man — even the prize-winning force of the bull — bestow that upon him, O herb.
Gather together the prize-forces of the bulls, gather the vigors of the herbs — gather the virility of males, O Indra; bestow upon him bodily strength.
Today, O Agni; today, O Savitṛ; today, O divine Sarasvatī; today, O Brahmaṇaspati — stretch my membrum like a bowstring.
Upright stand the mountains; upward the winds blow; upright shall this one of mine stand upon the earth like a post.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Rise up, O fierce one; shake thyself; let thy channels swell up. Untired, like a horse-guard keeping watch over a ship, let there be no weakness upon the testicles.
The golden-horned bull who arose from the ocean — with him, with that mighty one, we lull all these people to sleep.
The wind does not blow past the earth; the sun does not scorch beyond it — lull to sleep all the people and the dogs as well, O friend of Indra, as thou movest about.
The women who sleep in carriages, who sleep on couches, those who lie on beds — the women who are of fragrant perfume — all of them we lull to sleep.
Quivering and quivering, I have seized the sight; I have seized the breath. I have seized all the limbs in the deepest darkness of the nights.
He who sits, and he who moves about, and he who stands gazing about — we close the eyes of all of them, just as this house is closed.
Let the mother sleep; let the father sleep; let the dog sleep; let the lord of the house sleep — let all the kinsmen sleep; lull all the people to sleep.
O Sleep, with thy sleep-inducing power lull all the people to sleep. Put the others to sleep until after sunrise — let me move about till dawn, unharmed and uninjured, like Indra.
From your eyes and from your nostrils, from your ears and from your mouth — the head-lodged yakṣman from the brain, from the forehead we tear it out.
From your neck-vertebrae and from your cervical joints, from your backbone, from your spine — the yakṣman of the upper arm, from the shoulders, from the chest we tear it out.
From your lungs and from your cardiac region, from the diaphragm, from your flanks — the yakṣman from the kidneys, from your spleen, from your liver we tear it out.
From your intestines and from your rectum, from the vaniṣṭhū, from the belly — the yakṣman from the hands, from the fingers, from the nails we tear it out.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
From your bones and from your flesh, from your sinews, from your veins — the yakṣman from the ribs, from the marrows, from the navel we tear it out.
From your thighs and from your knee-joints, from your heels, from the balls of your feet — the yakṣman of the pudenda, from the hips, from the buttocks we tear it out.
Lodged limb by limb, hair by hair, bound joint by joint — the yakṣman of the skin, we tear it out from you entirely in all directions.
From each and every limb of yours, joint by joint throughout — by the extraction-spell of Kaśyapa we tear out the yakṣman from you.
Agni, the two demon-slayers — sharp, sharp-horned, the seer of seers, the poet most poetic — let them thrust away the evil-sayer, overwhelm hostility; back with the counter-stroke: upon the one who works harm, harm we hurl back.
Indra, the demon-slayer [sharp, sharp-horned, the seer of seers, the poet most poetic — let him thrust away the evil-sayer, overwhelm hostility; back with the counter-stroke: upon the one who works harm, harm we hurl back].
Soma, the demon-slayer [sharp, sharp-horned, the seer of seers, the poet most poetic — let him thrust away the evil-sayer, overwhelm hostility; back with the counter-stroke: upon the one who works harm, harm we hurl back].
Varuṇa, the demon-slayer [sharp, sharp-horned, the seer of seers, the poet most poetic — let him thrust away the evil-sayer, overwhelm hostility; back with the counter-stroke: upon the one who works harm, harm we hurl back].
Vāyu, the demon-slayer [sharp, sharp-horned, the seer of seers, the poet most poetic — let him thrust away the evil-sayer, overwhelm hostility; back with the counter-stroke: upon the one who works harm, harm we hurl back].
Tvaṣṭā, the demon-slayer [sharp, sharp-horned, the seer of seers, the poet most poetic — let him thrust away the evil-sayer, overwhelm hostility; back with the counter-stroke: upon the one who works harm, harm we hurl back].

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Dhātā, the demon-slayer [sharp, sharp-horned, the seer of seers, the poet most poetic — let him thrust away the evil-sayer, overwhelm hostility; back with the counter-stroke: upon the one who works harm, harm we hurl back].
Savitā, the demon-slayer [sharp, sharp-horned, the seer of seers, the poet most poetic — let him thrust away the evil-sayer, overwhelm hostility; back with the counter-stroke: upon the one who works harm, harm we hurl back].
Sūrya, the demon-slayer [sharp, sharp-horned, the seer of seers, the poet most poetic — let him thrust away the evil-sayer, overwhelm hostility; back with the counter-stroke: upon the one who works harm, harm we hurl back].
Candramā, the demon-slayer [sharp, sharp-horned, the seer of seers, the poet most poetic — let him thrust away the evil-sayer, overwhelm hostility; back with the counter-stroke: upon the one who works harm, harm we hurl back].
Bṛhaspati, the demon-slayer [sharp, sharp-horned, the seer of seers, the poet most poetic — let him thrust away the evil-sayer, overwhelm hostility; back with the counter-stroke: upon the one who works harm, harm we hurl back].
Prajāpati, the demon-slayer [sharp, sharp-horned, the seer of seers, the poet most poetic — let him thrust away the evil-sayer, overwhelm hostility; back with the counter-stroke: upon the one who works harm, harm we hurl back].
Parameṣṭhin, the demon-slayer — sharp, sharp-horned, the seer of seers, the poet most poetic — let him thrust away the evil-sayer, overwhelm hostility; back with the counter-stroke: upon the one who works harm, harm we hurl back.
"All-dwellers" — such is your name; fierce-eyed are you, O dice, who bear up the realm. To that one, O Indu, we would do homage with an oblation; may we become lords of riches.
This is for the fierce brown one who is self-sovereign among the dice. I would learn to propitiate Kali with ghee; may he show mercy to us in such a situation as this.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
O Agni, carry ghee to the Apsarasas; carry dust to the dice, sand and water too. May the gods, delighting in the gift of oblations according to their proper share, rejoice in both the oblatory offerings.
The god who pointed out this wealth to us, who presides over the seizing and remaining of dice — may he, delighting in this oblation, protect us; together with the Gandharvas may we make merry in shared exultation.
Those Apsarasas who exult in shared revelry in the space between the oblation-cart and the sun — may they join our hands together with skill; may they subdue for us the rival gambler.
Because I invoke the gods as one in need, because we have practiced brahmacarya — because I take hold of the brown dice, may they be gracious to us in such a plight as this.
[Colophon:] "Beginning with ādinavam" — thus one verse.
May Bhaga lead thee hence, taking thee by the hand; may Bṛhaspati be thy forerunner. May the god Savitā, whose laws are true, make thee worthy of homage, worthy of approach.
With that sweet whip which the Aśvins, the gods, fashioned at the beginning — with that we entwine thee, suffused with sweetness, into thy husband's love.
Be thou above thy mother-in-law; instruct thy husband's sister. We make thee glorious before thy husband; be thou beloved among the brothers-in-law.
Adorning thy person with the waters, enter the house — thou art the chief queen. There the gods have appointed thee to the householder's fire, that thou mayest be rich in offspring, reaching old age.
Ascending ever higher, scattering those who assail thee — thou hast stood upon the head of thy enemy; be a sovereign queen, accompanied by sons.
Over the mothers-in-law, over the fathers-in-law, over the household and its prosperity — reign supreme; among husband, brothers-in-law, and kinsmen of thine own birth, be a sovereign queen.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Whatever honey there is in the mountains and highlands, in the cattle and in the horses — with that wherewith the dice were anointed, therewith I anoint the head of this woman.
Whatever splendour is in the auspicious cow, or in the grass of a good pasture — with the splendour of this unguent I anoint her with splendour.
With that oblation offered with a united heart, wherewith Uśanā Kāvya moved of old, knowing the rites and knowing the deities — I pour libation; may your minds be in full accord, may they be mighty.
Great is the truth, great is the oblation, great is Uśanā Kāvya. The hearts of the mighty gods, of the righteous ones — these I have joined together.
I walk yoked with truth as my companion; I have full knowledge of the divine Anumati. May Indra be the heart of the gods for you; may your minds be in full accord, may they be mighty.
Tvaṣṭā, Vāyu, Kaśyapa, Indra, and Agni — they followed with their minds the footprint of the oblation; they found the mighty one who had entered into the atmosphere. May your minds be in full accord, may they be mighty.
With that by which these two, Heaven-and-Earth, were propped apart, by which the atmosphere and the sunlit realm came into being — knowing with the mind, I pour libation with the oblation; may your minds be in full accord, may they be mighty.
Heaven-and-Earth brought forth the heart by which the wise Tvaṣṭā fashions all this world. Of that heart Uśanā, conversant with the rites, found knowledge — the thought that had entered into the mind.
This thought and this intent — by means of which the gods achieved their aims — with faith in truth the seven seers pour this as oblation.
O Manyu, exulting and exhilarated, mounting the same chariot with thee, their weapons whetted to sharpness, with arrows keen — may the men, of fiery form, advance forward.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Like fire, O Manyu, overwhelm with fury; invoked, be our battle-leader, O conqueror. Knowing how to conquer the foes, divide the spoil; measuring out strength, drive away the hostile hosts.
Overwhelm, O Manyu, hostility against us; come, crushing, smashing, annihilating the foes. Thy fierce host has now been held back; thou who art self-born, subdue the submissive to thy will.
Thou art one invoked by many, O Manyu; sharpen for battle beast after beast. Unwounded, yoked with thee as ally, we raise a brilliant war-cry to win the victory.
Maker of victory, like Indra, never faltering — be our protector here, O Manyu. We proclaim thy beloved name, O conqueror; we know that fountain from which thou hast arisen.
With might, with the power of a thunderbolt, O arrow-hurler, thou bearest strength, ever supreme over those who confront thee. With purpose, O Manyu, be united with us; be invoked by many, lead us into the midst of great wealth.
The wealth assembled on both sides, gathered together — may Varuṇa and Manyu grant it to us. The foes, bearing fear in their hearts, defeated, shall go to the uttermost distance.
Auspicious to us be the goddess Pṛśniparṇī; let her bring ill-fortune to Nirṛti. For she is fierce, the devourer of kaṇva-demons — her, the powerful one, I have fetched for you.
Pṛśniparṇī was born first as one who ever pursues and strikes down. With her I sever the head of kaṇva as one severs the head of a bird.
She who bears vigor, who bears life-breath, and who is the refresher of living beings — may Pṛśniparṇī drive all those kaṇvas to destruction away from here.
Rounding them up, drive them out as a sharp-horned bull drives out its herd — the greedy kaṇva, the sinful one, O mighty Pṛśniparṇī.
You, fierce Pṛśniparṇī, come burning like fire; the kaṇvas have been brought near to the end of life. Drive them into the mountain, into the darkness whither they depart — cast those evil ones down there.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The greedy blood-drinker, and the one who desires to steal away prosperity, and the womb-devouring kaṇva — destroy them, O mighty Pṛśniparṇī.
Those kaṇvas who carry off our cattle, who carry off our homes, who carry off our prosperity — those, O fierce Pṛśniparṇī, drive to destruction away from here.
That in which a spell is implanted — here is that śalya (splinter/shaft), the reed, the wrapping, and the point. As a son hears and comes to his mother, so hear: this is your very self — be thus dislodged.
If, having split the bone, you have fallen into the marrow, or if you are lodged in one who is dear to a woman — come back across the broad cow-pasture ground, following in the track of the rays of the risen sun.
Mātariśvan, the purifying wind, blowing along you; the sun shining brightly so the body may be seen — from the smell of blood, from the festering, dislodge yourself; free yourself from the wound that is there in you.
Dislodge yourself from there, come back this way; we know your many purposes, those that are outside. These are your sisters, this indeed is your father, this is your mother — come here to this kinsman.
Whether you were shot by enemies or by friends, or sent forth and released by gods or by a goddess — having pierced and left the horn in the man, O arrow, let the horn and point be conjoined and depart from here.
If you are lodged among the tips, or lodged at the front, or lodged in the flesh of a man — like one who looses a noose and sets free the fetter, let the splinter from the eye make its way for departure.
Carried from hand to hand, the metal may see you out by the power of healing plants; cleansed with waters, anointed as one lying down, placed harmless in the sheath of the kinswomen.
For the sixty-fold śalya an enclosure of sixty nights has been made. Today we dislodge it from its station away from here for you.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Let marrow be joined with marrow; let joint be united with joint for you. Let that which has been scattered of your bodily frame come together; let sinew and let joint be joined for you.
Let marrow be laid together with marrow; let bone grow upon bone. We bind your sinew together with sinew; let skin grow upon skin.
Let hair be joined together with hair; let skin knit itself together with skin. Let your blood grow upon bone; let flesh grow upon flesh.
Rohiṇī is the fully healing one, Rohiṇī of broken bone. Born on the day of Rohiṇī (the lunar asterism), you are Rohiṇī, O herb.
If the bone is broken, if it is shattered, the grinding agent against your own body — may Dhātṛ (the Divine Ordainer) set all that right, joining joint to joint.
If a thunderbolt was hurled against you, or if it fell and pierced into the cut, or if you were shattered; or if you fell from a tree — O ten-headed, O Ṛbhu, I join your joints together as craftsmen join together the parts of a chariot.
Rise up, go forward — your joint has been set in place; may Dhātṛ set together the broken part of your body. As a well-wheeled, well-felly'd, smooth, well-hubbed chariot rolls along — stand firm just so.
Rising, may Āditya slay the woodworms; setting, may Sūrya slay them with his rays. So long has he been marshalled against us.
The Apsarā dug out the root; the Gandharva recited it round about. By that very means may Sūrya, slayer of Vṛtra, crush you woodworms and strip you of immortality.
Let her coming slay the woodworms; let her going slay the woodworms. Let her striking slay the woodworms; let her who grinds grind the woodworms to dust.
Woodworms, let there be nothing of yours here; you have been detected, like thieves caught at nightfall.
Among the woodworms, the eldest, and likewise the youngest and the middle one — slain are all your kindred, slain is the mother, slain is the father.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Just as foam, seen upon the water, is swept away, so we with one utterance drive out all the woodworms together.
The cows have settled in the stall; the wild beasts have retreated. You, O Āditya, with your rays have driven all the woodworms down.
Rising, stretch forth your rays; dispatch them like arrows. You, O Āditya, scorch all the woodworms with your terrible body.
You who are curved and bent back, chipping away like a piece of wood — Śarkoṭa is indeed your name. Whence have you come to possess venom?
You who strike with both — with your tail and with your mouth — even in your mouth there is no venom; whence should venom reside in the track of your tail?
You are the grandson of the Dānava Vidutsura. His venom was rendered powerless at the start; therefore your venom too is powerless.
I have made you utterly powerless, impotent — a castrate I have made you. The immortal gods made you, the demonic one, a castrate.
Such a tiny, little creature — I split that creature with a peg. Thereupon I poured away the venom in the southern direction along the year.
These seven peahens to the west, sisters, unmarried virgins — they drew out your venom, as water-bearers draw water from a well, as those who own pitchers draw it.
"Of the nine nineties" — thus the one verse.
I drive away the troop of the wing-clipped ones, the troop of the baldheads, and also the troop of the shaven-headed ones, even as crows are chased away.
The prattler, the infatuator, Drowsiness, Languor, and Fever-of-the-third-day — all of them we burn up with the fire of the jaṅgiḍa plant.
Protect us, O Jaṅgiḍa, from the unclean ones, and from the Rakṣases. From the Yātudhāna and the Kimīdin — from these protect us, O Jaṅgiḍa.
From Apsarases, from Gandharvas, from gods, from Asuras, and moreover from all evil — from these protect us, O Jaṅgiḍa.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The divine Agni burns down your enemies, drives away hostility, folly, and the Yātudhānas. Come forth, destroyer of enemies and misfortune; protect us, O Jaṅgiḍa, from a hundred diseases.
Attach yourself to the divine Agni, its overlord, with divine power — the one who does the work. May the powerful Jaṅgiḍa guard us with power, so that we may be victorious in battles.
True is Agni, true are the Waters, true to me are Heaven and Earth, the two that bring welfare to all. True shall be this sacred formula of ours that is made. The jaṅgiḍa that Uśanas bound for Indra — that same I bind upon you.
The little śakuntikā bird has eaten your poison along with her companion. Let me not die, nor let yonder man die. He shall not die; let us not die. Far from him be its operation — the green plant shall make you sweet, the honey-sweet one shall render you honey.
Into the sun I release the poison, into the wineskin in the house of the soma-presser. [Remainder fragmentary.]
The thrice-seven sparkling ones have destroyed the blossom of the poison. [Remainder fragmentary.]
The poison of the ālvantaruṭa plant is sapless venom; vidārī and karambha render the poison devoid of sap. [Remainder fragmentary.]
The fierce, sapless poison of water — and Agni, the all-beholding — [neutralize it]. [Remainder fragmentary.]
The śakuntikā bird spoke to me — she who sucks the flower of the poison: [she declared it harmless]. [Remainder fragmentary.]
It does not fester, it does not intoxicate, the poison does not slay the man. Let me not die, nor let yonder man die. He shall not die; let us not die. Far from him be its operation — the green plant shall make you sweet, the honey-sweet one shall render you honey.
Of the ninety-nine, this is one.
Honey-sweet am I to my husband; yet sweeter than honey to my lover. Moreover, my vulva is honeyed; I am honey at the moment of union.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
With honey I blend myself, as one blends fermented grain with māsara-liquor. This speech of mine is commingled with honey; my two eyes are honey-radiant in their gaze.
Honey is the sky, honey the earth, honey is Indra, honey is the sun. The women who were born honey — from all of them I am yet more honey-sweet.
Honey-sweet are the plants, and honey-sweet are the waters too. The cows that were born as honey — from all of them I am yet more honey-sweet.
Born of honey, producing honey — the most powerful among plants — with him I make an impression in the heart of every man.
Just as a horse stalled in the tether rushes toward the mare, so do you, O potent herb, bring that man to me, neighing as he comes.
How like delight his very breath, how like delight his very breast! Desiring other women, intent on surpassing them — yet your mind followed after me, as a shadow follows one who walks.
The Dāsas with sapless arms dig you up on the dark side of the mother. You are a slave-woman, you are a bought-thing, you are uprooted — a sapless, impotent poison.
The kakkaṭa crabs eat you; the kuruṅga deer eat you on the ridges. You are a wicked thing whose seeds have been eaten; dug up with a spade, you have caused no further harm.
As the string is let down from the bow, so I unstring your virulence, O poison. Let its festering shoots fall down, as the sun makes the earlier dawns fall away.
The Sindhu is spread behind, the rising-place of the sun is in front. Whatever forest lies between those two — all of that is the bane of poison.
May the honey-maker render you honey; may the food-maker render you food — both for sitting down to drink and for standing upright.
Lomakarṇa devoured you and sank you into the Paruṣṇī river. The Bhaimīs fashioned garlands from that — all the poison is food for the great buffalo.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
By the wide, the far-striding, the swift, and by that of the afflicted — for the earth has seized its name. Let the poison be warded off, let the poison be made impotent.
I have brought hither the herb that is Indra's mother, Indra's strength, Indra's sister — the herb that speaks under Indra's patronage — the poison-destroyer.
Whatever moves on feet, whatever has hooves, whatever has a stalk, whatever has blossoms, whatever Prajāpati causes to stir — all that is a poison-neutralizer.
The Sindhu river stands as support behind; the rising of the sun stands ahead — the poison that lies between those two, that we corrupt with our utterance.
As far as the sun blazes, as far as it looks out upon all — over that whole extent we chant forth the corruption of poison.
My tongue flows with sweetness; my tongue speaks sweetness. O tongue, become possessed of brilliance — let not this man of mine come to harm.
Hā! Hai! O auspicious, blessed, healthy Pṛśniparṇī — lead this man of mine today toward long life!
Those by whom the rains rain down, those by whom the inviolable cows live — Savitṛ has illumined those as my poison-corrupters.
Prajāpati first bound you, the unvanquished one, for valor. I bind that one upon you for life, for brilliance, for might, and for strength. May the unvanquished one protect you on all sides.
Stand upright, guarding alertly, O unvanquished one. Let not the Paṇis, let not the Yātudhānas deceive you. Shake off the assailants as Indra shakes off the Dasyus; overpower all enemies who would fight you. May the unvanquished one protect you on all sides.
Even a hundred striking and smiting him could not exhaust him. Upon him Indra has bestowed sight, breath, and strength. May the unvanquished one protect you on all sides.
We clothe you about with the armor of Indra, who became the high king of the gods. May all the gods lead you forward. May the unvanquished one protect you on all sides.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
In this amulet reside one hundred heroic powers; in this unvanquished one a thousand life-breaths. Stand over all enemies like a tiger — whoever would fight you, let him be the lower one. May the unvanquished one protect you on all sides.
Anointed with ghee, sweet, full of nourishment, possessing a thousand life-breaths, having a hundred birthplaces, bestowing vigor — both benevolent and bliss-giving, both vigorous and rich in sap. May the unvanquished one protect you on all sides.
As you shall be the highest, without a rival, the slayer of rivals, the master of those born together — so may Savitṛ make you. May the unvanquished one protect you on all sides.
The watery kind and the spotted kind, the burning kind and the steaming kind; the painful kind and the severe kind, the tertian kind and the ever-recurring kind — O fever demons, vanish from here!
I know your name, O Takman — you are named Fire. We lead you away from here as a gentle fever.
You are the burning heat of Vṛtra; you are the offspring of the cloud. May Heaven and Earth destroy the fever from here.
Your mother is named Pañcapsinī; and you yourself are called Ekapsinī. I know your name — therefore, O Takman, run away from here!
And you are named Audumbara; and you are named Priyātithi. We destroy you hence with powerful sacred utterance.
The chattering kind and the babbling kind, the dampening kind and the burning kind; the tertian kind and the Mauñjigala kind — O fever demons, vanish from here!
O Vikilīda, O Vilohita, O Vikāśa, O Kraṃdarajjana — go to the mountain, O Dhūmaketu! Let homages be made to you in the forest.
O Agni, the mighty one, slay the lowest demon, cast down the middling one, crush the highest. May Agni, whose face is light, be benevolent to us; may Heaven and Earth be benevolent to us without fail.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Like a mother, like a father — protect him, release him from distress on all sides.
Born from the wind, from the atmosphere, from the lightning, from the light — may that golden-born conch-shell, the kṛśana-gem, guard us from distress.
You are the chief among golden things; you were born from Soma. You are the radiant one in the chariot, luminous in the quiver.
You who, radiant in the front, were born from the ocean — by means of the conch-shell, having struck down the rākṣasas and the devourers, we overpower them.
Those who are devourers, the sorcerers, the rākṣasas, those who are kimīdins — all of them, O conch-shell, by means of you we overpower in every direction.
With the conch-shell we drive away disease and wretchedness; with the conch-shell we also drive away the ever-gnawing ones. The conch-shell, the universal remedy, the kṛśana-gem — may it guard us from distress.
Born in heaven, brought from the ocean, fetched from the river — that golden-born conch-shell, the jewel that extends life, shall be ours.
The kṛśana became the bone of the gods; endowed with vital essence it moves amid the waters. I bind it upon you for life, for radiance, for vigor, and for strength — may the kṛśana-gem guard you on all sides.
A maiden, going to fetch water, found Soma flowing beside it. While carrying it homeward she spoke: "For Indra I press you; for Śakra I press you."
O you hero who goes about, peering into house after house — drink this Soma pressed by Jambha's mouth, accompanied by parched grain and gruel, with cakes, worthy of the uktha-hymn.
Will he perhaps be able? Will he perhaps act? Will he perhaps make us more prosperous? Will those women who hate their husbands come to unite with Indra?
We do not even seek to cure you; we do not even press you hard. Gently, gently — O Indu, flow around for Indra.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
These three expanses, O Indra, cause to grow apart — the head of that man, the field, and this here upon my belly.
That which is our field, and this body of mine, and the head of that spread-out one — make all of those hairy and abundant.
Through the hole of the chariot, through the hole of the wagon, through the hole of the yoke, O Śatakratu — Apālā, O Indra, you purified three times, you made her sun-skinned.
On the back of heaven, fifty honey-mixing suparṇas, guardians of the world — fierce, they protect rank by rank, those who stirred up Indra to heroic valor.
The supreme chaplain Bṛhaspati made the abhīvardha-amulet for him for sovereignty. By means of it, lay your rivals low; having multiplied your cattle abundantly in peace, may your chariot-vehicle go forth to victory.
Those who are your peers, all of them together steadfastly brought along your share of cattle. Grow in power over your rivals, over those who make war on you.
Crush down all the injurers, be as the abhīvardha — the grower-in-superiority, the overcomer, the one with the overwhelming host. May all the clans come to you, may the heavenly, milk-laden waters come to you.
Grow in power with offspring, waxing strong; may you prevail with armies and with cattle. Waxing strong with brāhmaṇas, rājanya warriors, and vaiśyas, with śūdras — overcome with your assembly those who make war on you.
Grow in power with fields; spread wide with offspring; grow in power with heroes; become abundant with cattle. With glory and with tribute — whoever strives against you, let him, having been overcome, stand before you bringing tribute.
For aid we invoke Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Agni, the Marut host, and Aditi. O Vasus, liberal givers, as [one frees] a chariot from a difficult pass, deliver us wholly from every distress.
Come, O Ādityas, for our complete welfare; be gods who bestow bliss in the victories against Vṛtra. [Deliver us wholly from every distress.]

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
May the Fathers, whose invocation is auspicious, protect us; and also the two divine daughters of the gods, fosterers of the cosmic order. [Deliver us wholly from every distress.]
With hymns of praise we entreat Narāśaṃsa, the vigorous one who bestows vigor, Pūṣan the lord of heroes, with his favors. [Deliver us wholly from every distress.]
O Bṛhaspati, make our path forever easy; that which of thine is ordained by Manu for well-being and bliss, that we implore. [Deliver us wholly from every distress.]
In the tight pass the seer Kutsa called upon Indra, the Vṛtra-slayer, the lord of mighty deeds, for aid. O Vasus, liberal givers, as [one frees] a chariot from a difficult pass, deliver us wholly from every distress.
Together with the gods, may divine Aditi protect us; may the divine protector shield us without ceasing. May Mitra and Varuṇa be gracious to us, and Aditi, Sindhu, Pṛthivī, and Dyaus.
Burn away from us the sin that blazes. O Agni, blaze bright — bring us wealth.
Burn away from us the sin that blazes. We sacrifice for good fields, for easy passage, and for the gaining of riches.
Burn away from us the sin that blazes. So that their wise men, and ours too, may prosper most gloriously.
Burn away from us the sin that blazes. So that we may be born of thy wise men, O Agni; so that we may prosper through thee.
Burn away from us the sin that blazes. When the rays of Agni the mighty one go forth on every side.
Burn away from us the sin that blazes. For thou, O thou of face turned everywhere, art he who encompasses all from every side.
