These prayers Bṛhaddiva, the foremost, the sun-seeker, proclaims as might for Indra; the self-sovereign dwells in the great enclosure and has opened wide all his own doors.
Thus did Bṛhaddiva Atharvan, the great one, declare Indra himself to be his own body; the sisterly winds of Mātariśvan, stainless, both urge him on and increase him with strength.
Prospering, of exhilarating origin, radiant in manifestation, with immortal breath, nobly born, growing; with breath undeceived, shining — like a serpent Trita has upheld the three.
He who first settled in the ordinance — from thence he fashions manifold forms; the nourishing one first entered the womb, he who has heeded the unuttered word.
He whose heat poured forth from thy body, dripping gold, pure, following their own nature — here thou dost hold the immortal names; the robes, O master, are set in motion for us.
When these have proclaimed the ancient foremost thing, standing seat by seat on that which ages not — the Sage, as the two Mothers of vitality lick him, has measured the kinsman-bride's form as counterpart.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
That great and broad ruling power — the Sage has fashioned it with his wisdom, O Yama, in reverence; when the converging ones press toward the earth, then the great wheel of obstruction has grown.
The seven sages have fashioned the seven bounds; towards one of them the sinful one has gone; yet thou who art immortal in breath, encompassed, advancing, O Asura, attained, goest along by thine own power.
The eldest life sets down its treasures, or the Sage, the giver, is attended by vigour; or when a son urges the kingly power against his parents, calling the eldest bound with blessing.
Look now upon those, O Varuṇa, who have turned back again at thy sacrifice; thou dost fashion forms — thou fillest one half with the other's power, and with half thou increasest thy vigour, O Unwildering.
We have magnified the powerful friend, Varuṇa the vigorous son of Aditi; we have spoken for him the words proclaimed by the Sage, to the two Worlds truthful in speech.
Who drove you forth from behind? Who dug out the paths in front, when you, the Waters urged on by Varuṇa, came hurrying?
Prajāpati released you; he dug out the paths in front; and he in turn released us from behind — released by him, we flow.
The purifying Waters flow in many ways, through all these worlds and through all the regions; may they purify us from sin and blame; may they release us from the lap of death and dissolution.
May the Waters, our mothers, refine us; may the clarified-butter purifiers purify us with ghee; for the divine ones carry away all defilement — from them indeed I come forth pure, cleansed.
The divine Waters, our mothers, intent on refining, dripping with ghee, have mingled together with honey; may those bright ones, the divine ones, bestow on us the whole span of life by night and by day.
Most watery of waters, most wealthy of the wealthy ones — may the Waters purify; may they purify us.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
You, O Waters, hold the glory of heroes; you refine the pure ones; your great directions, the sub-regions separate, flow in motion.
You are the womb of Mitra and Varuṇa; you are the sweetest milk-cows of Soma; the god Indu takes up his dwelling in you, O divine ones; O Waters, gladden the brahman power and the kṣatra power.
Continually prevailing through these, we go pursuing the appeasers; the Waters are the refiners of all — those which the gods gave to Manu.
When they flow, the Waters purify; when they stand still, they become purely clean; I have found no blame in them, no defilement — from of old they have been mingled together with honey.
Golden-hued, pure, purifying, the Waters have strode forward, having cast away blame; a hundred of you, O divine ones, and a thousand purifying filters purify at the outpourings.
Such as they are, life-bestowing, they refine the brahman whose toes they touch, worthy of praise; those who make everything pure, who do not pass away — like cows, well-born, you stand with milk.
Release us from all defilements, O rivers, from whatever sins we have committed with our bodies; directed by Indra, urged on by Varuṇa, pour in honey, O Waters, into the ocean.
Night is your mother, the Sky your father, Aryamā is your grandfather. Śilācī indeed is your name; you are the sister of the gods.
Whoever drinks you lives; you protect the man. You are the upholder of the eternal ones, and the binder of the eternal ones.
Whatever has been done by a staff, or by an arrow, or by a wound with burning heat — for that you are the healer; Niṣkṛti indeed is your name.
Auspiciously you abide on the plakṣa, on the aśvattha, on the khadira, on the dhava; auspiciously on the nyagrodha tree. Come to us, O Arundhatī!
Tree by tree you climb, like a maiden in her ardour. Victorious, standing firm against all, Saṃjayā indeed is your name.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
O golden-hued young one, vigorous, with a hairy flank — O Lākṣā, you are the sister of the waters; the wind has become your very breath.
O golden-armed, blessed one, of the sun's colour, most beautiful in form — the expiation goes where it must go; expiate this man here.
Ghṛtācī by name is the illegitimate child; Ajababhru is your father. You are the blood of that dark horse of Yama — so are you infused.
Fallen together from the blood of the horse, she has clung to the leaf. You are a flowing, winged one; come to us, O Arundhatī!
O Ghṛtācikā, who rides the wind-chariot, whose wings are lightning, O Arundhatī — you go most readily to the afflicted; verily you shall carry him away from pain.
Whatever of you has been consumed by the Piśācas, let that swell up again for you. May Lākṣā, the all-healer, protect you together with the gods.
As Heaven and Earth do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.
As Wind and the Atmosphere do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.
As the Sun and the Moon do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.
As Day and Night do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.
As the cow and the bull do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.
As Mitra and Varuṇa do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.
As the brahman and the kṣatra do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.
As Indra and his sovereign power do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
As the hero and heroic might do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.
As the in-breath and the out-breath do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.
As Death and Immortality do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.
As Truth and Untruth do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.
As what has been and what shall be do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.
Honey-sweet is my going forth, honey-sweet is my going onward; may I speak with a honey-sweet voice; may my two eyes be honeyed in appearance.
He who stretches out toward me, who has fallen at my feet — and he who has come back again to me — may his two eyes wither with longing.
A barren cow is your mother, O Madhu-substance; a potent bull-ox is your father. You are born from a milch-cow; being a king, you are most laden with sweetness.
The bull-like one possessed of virile power, soma-backed, dwelling in the sky — Indrāṇī brought forward the honey-substance first of all, for the sake of good fortune.
The honey-substance that feeds on food, the one with a dry mouth — for the heart, indeed. May it anoint me with sweetness, so that I may obtain what I desire.
The honey-substance, born of the river, is led among people like a horse. May it anoint me with sweetness, so that I may obtain what I desire.
May sweet Sinīvālī sprinkle me together with sweetness. May she anoint me with sweetness, so that I may obtain what I desire.
Just as the bees anoint honey upon honey, so do I anoint your mind upon this body of mine.
Whatever of your mind has gone away, whatever is bound here or elsewhere — that I turn back to you; within me I bind your mind.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Kaśyapa and Suparṇa both stood in the Marīci; Suparṇa looked about and saw the earth enveloped in the ocean.
That earth which Suparṇa beheld sunken within the great flood — thee, O Sūkara, by thy wizardry thou didst lift up thrice from the ocean.
This earth which thou, O Sūkara, didst bring up from the ocean by thy wizardry — she is the corrupter of poison; let her be the remedy for this one.
She who, unshaken, stands upon the truth, clad in gold — from her, the all-sustaining, I draw forth the poison-destroyer.
She of whom one says: "whose nest is this" — [so is she named by one who knows].
She of whose earth the crickets make a home for themselves — from her, the all-sustaining, I draw forth the poison-destroyer.
He who found thee, O Earth; he who lifted thee up, O Earth — I have seized upon the names of those two, O thou of a thousand streams.
The names which Indra the Vṛtra-slayer made for thee, O Earth — those names of thine, O tawny one, we know them fully; be thou the destroyer of poison!
Those that the Maruts fashioned for thee, those that the seven seers know, that which all the Ādityāḥ know — that Earth is the destroyer of poison.
Overpower the yātudhānas, overpower the yātudhānīs; overpower all the rākṣasas — thou art the overpowering one, O herb.
O overpowering one, O ever-victorious one — vanquishing, I am the superior. Moreover I am the conqueror; I, together with the ever-following ones, have conquered you.
Thou who movest as the overpowering one, like a bull that has conquered — destroyer of sadānvāḥ, destroyer of rākṣasas: thou, O herb, art terrible.
O Khelā with drooping breasts — flee hence, fly away from here! A head with horns like a bull here has not missed thee.
O thou of no pressing, O thou of many sons, O thou with no entrails, O great-bellied one — depart quickly from us along the road, O gravel-devourer, roam on!

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Those misers who roam seeking the pressing of the fool — upon them, O Agni of the black track, sharp-horned, go goring!
That piece of wood which floats in the midst of the river, uninhabited by any person — grasp hold of that, O malevolent one, and go yonder beyond.
She whose birth-place the desired ones have traversed — the unseen worms, the scorching insects — to her, the consort of Balāsa, to the kuṣṭha-afflicting one, I make obeisance.
O daughter of Śarva, O wife of Bhava, O sister of the yātu-demons, O ever-following one — feed upon her sons and brothers there where we conduct thee.
This soma-stalk is pressed for the bull; for the bull it is taken up, fierce for the one who beholds men. The divine, manly one has cried aloud — great is the name of the bull, for such is his hump.
Be thou the equinox, O Viṣṇu — thou who art the lord of men for me. Moreover, even as Indra among the gods, let him proclaim himself among the peoples.
Let him proclaim himself among men, in concert with Indra the ally; and may Agni Vaiśvānara, the overcomer, confer upon thee the kingdom.
He whose share — this bull — is led around for Indra: let him smite enemies on the approach, and let him smite them on the departure.
Let him be the slayer of the enemy, the slayer of those who rage; let him be the leader of the clans, going at the fore among those who break forth.
Make this bull of Indra long-lived, full of brilliance, and also the overlord of the clans, the master of this earth.
He who is of fine horns, of fine hump, auspicious — he has seated himself upon the sacrificial grass; with the bull born of farmer-folk we offer worship.
Offering worship with the bull, as if with gentle ghee, we overcome with Indra all scorners and all battle-hosts.
The bull which the gods gave thee as thy exclusive share — with him strike down the Vṛtra-foes and smite the enemies in battle.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Smite the enemies, thrust aside the scorners — thou art arisen, endowed with virile power. We lead thee around as Indra's share; let our world be wide, free from adversaries.
O thou grown great with ghee, fed with ghee, of a thousand horns, well praised — O thou invoked with ghee, blaze forth!
Thou who, anointed with ghee, dost stand fierce for victory — do thou carry us through the straits and through the overpowering of battle-hosts.
The karkī cow, blessed and fortunate, wife of the bull, desirous of offspring, obedient, lowing — she who is in-calf and moves in season: a single donor gives her as one among a thousand.
She who bears the embryo and yields milk, she who, as the cow of all the gods (vaiśvadevī), is milked for the agnihotra — may that cow not harm us; she is the spouse of Varuṇa.
Toward the womb of the karkī cow the bulls move in one accord, eager to beget offspring. May she come to us as Aditi of all forms; the worlds cry out to her.
Sent forth by Prajāpati, full of seasonable vigor, the bulls resort to her for offspring. Let the virile bulls, bellowing, press upon her as she lows in desire — the seven-named lowing cow.
She was seen facing the dawn, golden in hue, clothed in the bright garment of Varuṇa, bringing the oblation as the cow of all gods — may the lord of cattle prosper the offspring for your giver.
Self-standing, O lowing cow, you stand firm for the bull, facing Soma, Sūrya, and Agni. Come to me without harm, O lowing one; may the lord of cattle prosper the livestock for your giver.
Prosperous shall the giver be — he who gives the radiant cow as Agni's share; the winning steeds shall stimulate you, O prize-bearing one, in your dear abode, the heart, sweet with Soma.
I render homage while receiving her — to that fire which dwells within the lowing cow, and to the manly greatness and might that has arisen in her. May she be pleasant and gracious to my person.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The lowing cow has come; we receive her — the cow of nourishment together with the troop of males. Bearing strength and yielding ghee, may she bring thousandfold prosperity for my giver.
Those first deeds which you performed without being reached — let them not harm our heroes here. That which is yours I place before you.
Those who were born beyond the ancient measure, possessed of renown, partakers of benevolence — the eyeless, the deaf have stumbled and laughed; the wicked do not cross the path of ṛta.
Toward the thousand-streamed one, the honey-tongued, the unwearied ones sang out together at the vault of heaven. His spies, the vigilant, never close their eyes; at every step let the snare-layers stand as a barrier.
Indeed, run forward all around for the winning of prizes; conquer on all sides the obstacles. You follow that ocean of the sky in its flow — you are called Sanisras, the thirteenth month.
You are Indra's house, you are Indra's shelter, you are Indra's armor, you are Indra's protection. Drive away with this, ward off with this, send away with this that adversary yonder — svāhā!
O Agni and Soma, of sharp weapons, of sharp missiles, most gracious — be kind to us here. Release us, who are seized, from blame; take pleasure in the sacrifice; bestow immortality upon us — svāhā!
You are the snare of the eye, the snare of the mind, the snare of brahman; you are anger-upon-anger. Let those who seek to injure us be without anger toward us — svāhā!
Whoever has assailed us with harmful intent — by eye, by mind, by speech, by design, by thought, by brahman-power — him, O Agni, turn into anger-upon-anger — svāhā!
Raise up life-force, raise up glory, raise up strength; raise up mental power, vital force, and manly might — bestow these upon us — svāhā!
You two are makers of life, you are full of life-force, possessed of svadhā; be my guardians, protect me. Abide in my self, be gracious to my person, do not harm me — svāhā!

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
You are Indra's house, you are Indra's shelter, you are Indra's armor, you are Indra's protection. Into you I enter — whole in every limb, whole in my entire self, completely uttered, fully a person — together with all that is mine.
I am he whose name is 'the Unscattered'; I surrender my self to Heaven and Earth. You are invoked for protection.
The divine thirteenth month, offspring of Prajāpati, bears the name 'the Unscattered.' Completely utterred, fully a person — I have gone forward to the divine citadels.
I have gone into the divine citadels — together with the community, for well-being — from the middle of the year, together with all my brothers.
I have gone forward to the divine citadels, being exactly who I am. Whoever assails me, let him reach Prajāpati.
You are stone, a watchful sentinel — guard me from injury, guard me from enmity. Guard me from divine imprecation; guard my person here.
Whoever has assailed us with harmful intent from the eastern quarter — let him meet this; may our armor of stone stand firm.
[Lacunose: parallel verse for the southern quarter — as above, 'Whoever has assailed us with harmful intent from the southern quarter — let him meet this; may our armor of stone stand firm.']
[Lacunose: parallel verse for the western quarter — as above, 'Whoever has assailed us with harmful intent from the western quarter — let him meet this; may our armor of stone stand firm.']
Whoever, bearing evil intent, should assail us from the upward direction — may he meet that; let the armour of stone be ours.
Svāhā to the eastern direction.
Svāhā to the southern direction.
Svāhā to the western direction.
Svāhā to the northern direction.
Svāhā to the fixed (nadir) direction.
Svāhā to the upward direction.
Svāhā to heaven.
Svāhā to the atmosphere.
Svāhā to the earth.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Svāhā to the earth.
Svāhā to the atmosphere.
Svāhā to heaven.
The great-throated one, born of dung, the belly-devourer, the unworshipped one; Oṣṭha, Kokamukha — these and whoever else they are, from here we drive them away.
Rāmadanta, Avadala, Prahāla, Ahināsika; Upavarta, Balāhaka, Khela, Gardabhanādina, the vulture-one, Hastyāyana — these [from here we drive away].
Pramṛśyādina, Abhyama, Bhīmahasta, Marīmṛśa; Trastākṣa, Mṛdvaṅguli, Nakhogra, Dantavīrya — these [from here we drive away].
Paryanya, Abhipāpada, the form-taking one who ever seeks to conquer; and also Śalalya, Śevala — these [from here we drive away].
Taṇḍa, Agretuṇḍika, Aliṃśa, and also Vatsapa; Dāmagranthi, Sanisrasa, the forest-dweller, the skin-dweller — these [from here we drive away].
This Jānukeśava, this demon that roams about — the āsura who seeks what has been sent forth — along with Aṃsū, Pāṃsyu, the hairy ones (Keśyāḥ), the stealers (Arāyāḥ), the dog-squeakers (Śvakiṣkiṇaḥ) — these from here we drive away.
The dāsa, the āsura, who devours the young children of people; Arāya, Keśin, Aghala — the one who strikes down and devours human beings — him from here we drive away.
The house-haunter named Hirākṣa, the slayer of the well-formed named Arāya — him from here we drive away.
Vitūla, Bhasva, Ākhida, Vanakrośa, Roruha; Āmāda, Prayutaiṣaṇa, Paryundāna, Paridrava, the downward-pulling one of the wolf, Gaṅgaṇa — these from here we drive away.
Whatever abundance is yours, whatever increase, whatever vital vigor, whatever essence — those, O Śakra, I take away; they are granted by you, O lord of Śacī.
From field to field I take away all increase, O lord of Śacī; what has been granted by you, O Vṛtrahan, I bring hither to my house.
The portion of the furrow that is in your field, the prosperity and what is scattered there; moreover, the residue that remains in your field — that I have pointed out to myself by the sacred word.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
What is on the threshing floor, what is in the granary, what is in the cattle pen, and what is in the treasure hoard; moreover, what lies in the storage jar — of that I take the essence from you.
The vigor of what has been winnowed out for you, the vigor of what has been threshed for you; the vigor of what is being ground for you — the vigor from your ground grain I take.
[The vigor] of what has been winnowed out for you, the vigor of what has been threshed for you; the vigor of what is being cooked for you — the vigor from your cooked [food I take].
The vigor of what has been bound up for you, the vigor of what has been churned for you; the vigor of what is being milked for you — the vigor from your milk I take.
I take from you the vigor of your cows; from your sheep I take the vigor; taking the vigor from your goats — from your single-hoofed animals I take it for myself.
The vigor that is in your people, the vigor in your acquired and known wealth; the vigor of all your households — that I bestow upon myself by the sacred word.
Now I will praise the drink, great in ordinance, mighty in strength — he at whose impelling power Trita, with his might, shattered Vṛtra joint from joint.
O sweet food, O honeyed food, we have chosen thee; be thou our protector.
Come to us, O food, auspicious with auspicious aids; be thou a fount of joy, free from enmity, a friend, most gracious — be such for us.
Thy flavors, O food, are spread abroad through the realms, abiding in heaven like the winds.
Thine are those who give, O food; thine are the sweetest, O food — they who are full of the sweetness of thy flavors rush forward like bulls with mighty necks.
In thee, O food, the mind of the great gods is set; by thine ensign a beautiful act was wrought — he smote the serpent in his lair.
When thou, O food, didst travel to yonder luminous realm of the mountains, there too, O honeyed food, do thou come rightly for our partaking.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
What of thee, O Soma, mixed with milk of cows, mixed with barley, we partake of — Vātāpa, be thou fat indeed.
Whatever remnant of waters and of herbs we eat of — [Vātāpa, be thou fat indeed].
O karambha-gruel, be a herb; be fat, O belly, freely moving — Vātāpa, be thou fat indeed.
Thee, O food, we have made to flow sweetly with our hymns as cows their oblation — thee for our communal joy, thee for the communal joy of the gods.
Toward that fair sacrifice thou art invoked for its keeping; come, O Agni, with the Maruts.
No god and no mortal surpasses the greatness of thy will — [come, O Agni, with the Maruts].
They who know the great realm of space, all the gods, free from deceit — [come, O Agni, with the Maruts].
They who are bright, of terrible form, of good dominion, devourers of the adversary — [come, O Agni, with the Maruts].
They who, fierce, have chanted the hymn, irresistible in their might — [come, O Agni, with the Maruts].
They who, divine, are seated in the shining vault upon the sky's surface — [come, O Agni, with the Maruts].
They who shake the mountains across the ocean with their might — [come, O Agni, with the Maruts].
They who stretch out with their rays across the billowing ocean — [come, O Agni, with the Maruts].
I release toward thee the Soma-sweet honey for the first drinking — [come, O Agni, with the Maruts].
Let the Maruts come in their troops, praised; let them bestow wealth upon us — [come, O Agni, with the Maruts].
The Kaṇvas have called to thee; they praise, O inspired one, thy thoughts — come, O Agni, with the Maruts.
May the Maruts pour together upon me, may Pūṣan, may Bṛhaspati; may this Agni pour together upon me with progeny and with wealth — may he make for me a long life-span.
May the Ādityas pour together, may the Agnis pour together upon me; may Indra pour together upon us — [with progeny and with wealth, may he make for me a long life-span].

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
May the ruddy ones pour together, and the hymns and whatsoever sages; may Pūṣan pour together — [with progeny and with wealth, may he make for me a long life-span].
May the Gandharvas and the Apsarasas pour together; may the divinities pour together upon me; may Bhaga pour together — [with progeny and with wealth, may he make for me a long life-span].
May the earths pour together; may those of heaven pour together upon me; may the atmosphere pour together — [with progeny and with wealth, may he make for me a long life-span].
May the intermediate quarters pour together; may the directions pour together upon me; may the expanse pour together — [with progeny and with wealth, may he make for me a long life-span].
May the rivers pour together; may the sindhu-streams pour together upon me; may the ocean pour together — [with progeny and with wealth, may he make for me a long life-span].
May the ploughed fields pour together; may the herbs pour together upon me; may Soma pour together — [with progeny and with wealth, may he make for me a long life-span].
May the waters pour together upon me; may the rains pour together upon me; may Sarasvatī pour together upon us with progeny and with wealth — may she make for me a long life-span.
May Bhaga pour lustre upon me, O Agni; may Viṣṇu pour nourishment. May Kṣatra drench us with progeny and wealth — may he make me long-lived.
May Virāj pour lustre upon me, O Agni; may Deṣṭrī pour nourishment. May Iḍā drench us with progeny and wealth — may she make me long-lived.
May Dhātā pour lustre upon me, O Agni; may Sikti pour nourishment. May the god Aryamā drench us with progeny and wealth — may he make me long-lived.
May Aṃśa pour lustre upon me, O Agni; may Vāyu pour nourishment. May Vāta drench us with progeny and wealth — may he make me long-lived.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
May the assembly-hall (Sabhā) pour lustre upon me, O Agni; may Surā pour nourishment. May Sūryā drench us with progeny and wealth — may she make me long-lived.
May Savitā pour lustre upon me, O Agni; may Sūrya pour nourishment. May the Moon (Candra) drench us with progeny and wealth — may he make me long-lived.
May the cattle pour lustre upon me, O Agni; may sacrifice pour nourishment. May the sacrificial fee (Dakṣiṇā) drench us with progeny and wealth — may she make me long-lived.
May wealth drench me; may vital power drench me. May radiance (tejas) drench us with progeny and wealth — may it make me long-lived.
May the lustres drench me; may the powers of being drench me. May Truth (Satya) drench us with progeny and wealth — may it make me long-lived.
O Night, the earthly dust has been filled by the father's abodes. O vast one, thou art spread across the seats of heaven; the thick darkness rolls on.
Of her whose farther shore is never seen, nor any who departs — all that stirs enters into her. Unharmed, O Night wide and dark, may we reach thy farther shore; O auspicious one, may we reach thy farther shore.
Those watchmen of thine, O Night, who look upon men — ninety and nine they are; eighty-eight, and further thy seventy-seven.
Sixty-six, O bountiful one; fifty-five, O gracious one; four and forty; and three and thirty, O vigorous one.
Two and twenty are thine, O Night; the lowest eleven — with these guardians of thine protect us today, O daughter of heaven.
Protect us! Let no evil-proclaimer hold sway over us; let no ill-intentioned one hold sway over us.
Let no thief of cattle hold sway over us today; let no wolf among the sheep hold sway. Let no robber of horses, O auspicious one, nor sorcerers among men hold sway.
Let the thief, the robber, run away by the farthest paths. Let the toothless rope flow beyond; let the evil-liver stream away beyond.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Make the serpent blind, O Night, stationary like smoke, and headless. Crush the jaws of the wolf; strike down the thief in a stumble.
In thee, O Night, we dwell; we shall sleep — keep watch! Grant us shelter for our cattle, for our horses, for our men.
And what we wear, and what thou encirclest within — all that we surrender to thee.
O Night, O mother, deliver us over to Dawn. May Dawn deliver us over to the Day; O Day, deliver thyself to her, O bright-shining Night.
Whatever flies here, whatever crawls here, whatever walks on feet or has a mouth — from that do thou, O Night, protect us.
She protects from behind; she protects from before; and from above and below. Guard us, O bright-shining one — we are thy praisers here.
Those who attend upon the Night and who keep vigil among living beings, who guard all the cattle — may they keep vigil in our own selves; may they keep vigil over our cattle.
I know thy name, O Night — Ghṛtācī is indeed thy name. Bharadvāja knows thee by that name; as such, watch over us, keep vigil in our possessions.
Brahman is its head, the Bṛhat-sāman its back, Vāmadevya is the belly of the odana-rice; the metres are its wings, truth is its face — the viṣṭārin oblation is born from austerity, a far-spreading sacrifice.
Boneless, pure, cleansed by the wind, radiant — they pass on to radiant worlds. Those who cook the viṣṭārin odana: Jātavedas shall not scorch their organ of generation.
Jātavedas shall not scorch their organ of generation; in the heavenly world abundant womanly pleasures shall be theirs. Yama shall not rob them of their seed.
He sits with Yama, he approaches the gods, he rejoices together with the Soma-intoxicated Gandharvas. Those who cook the viṣṭārin odana — adversity shall not cling to them from any quarter.
Becoming a charioteer, he travels onward in a chariot; becoming a bird, he ascends even to the sky. This sacrifice, spread wide, the most carrying of all — the viṣṭārin, once cooked, has reached heaven.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
He gives four jars fourfold, filled with milk, with water, with curds. May these channels flow toward you from every side, swelling with libation in the heavenly world.
Lakes of ghee, banks of honey, of good water, filled with milk, with water, with curds — may these channels flow to you forever, gladdening you with libation in the heavenly world.
The white lotus, the kumuda water-lily, the lotus-fibre, the śālūka water-root, the śaphaka and the mulālī — may the brimming lotus-pools, swelling with libation in the heavenly world, stand ready about me.
The odana I cook with faith — the viṣṭārin, the heaven-winning, the world-conquering — let it not be exhausted for me as it is ever being eaten; may it be for me an all-form wish-milking cow.
Being a bull, together with the sweet truth, milking immortality in the heavenly world — may those who are my sons and my fathers, all of them, sit near you, O viṣṭārin.
He who has spread out these sacrifices, for whose sake these worlds are anointed with libation — milk out immortalities for them, O viṣṭārin: my grandsons and my grandfathers.
Whether you have spread over the earth, or over the atmosphere, or over the sky, or over the divine realm — may my great-grandsons and my great-great-grandfathers recognize you here, O viṣṭārin.
In the heavenly world the Apsarases lie beside them, having become their wives — those who cook the viṣṭārin odana in this world, adorned with the sacrificial gift.
Drive her out, thrust her forth, beyond falling among her own kinsfolk. We make a falling-away for her — let that woman be sundered from her home.
Turn the husband away westward; lead the woman downward and away. Let her pass beyond ten mountains, let her pass beyond ten navigable rivers.
Toward the downward, the southward, toward the inauspicious direction — we make a falling-away for her; with that we burn her away.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Drive her out, drive her from the hole; from the hole make her enter the forest; from the forest make her a stranger among strangers. Set her chasing after wild beasts; make the wind the forelock of her hair.
Her heart and mind we blow into the fore-rush of the wind, into the snot. We make a falling-away for her — a scattering from her clinging to the household.
Let her float about following everything between both heaven and earth, as one unrestrained might wander, like a lock of rain-cloud cotton drifting overhead.
Let the wind blow ill upon her, let the sun scorch her with ill. And whatever food she eats, let that be more poisonous than poison to her.
"Let a lion be before your eyes" — thus the single verse.
This fire between you two — let it throw you both asunder, so that you shall not dwell together even in the furthest span of life.
Make them fly up asunder, O śimidā-plant; make them fly apart asunder, O śimidā — cleave these two householders apart as with a knife through cooked flesh.
Let her not delight in this husband of hers, nor in this her own marriage-bed. Let her abandon her own dwelling as a serpent abandons its worn-out skin.
As the dead and the living are without a common dwelling in this world, so let these two — husband and wife — be without a common dwelling in this world.
The eagle found you out; the boar dug you up with his snout. O herb that harms the harmer — you who would harm us — burn back the maker of the sorcery.
Burn back the sorcerers, burn back the maker of the sorcery. And whoever seeks to harm us — him, too, do you strike down, O herb.
O Agni, crusher of armies, overpower the armies. We carry the sorcery back to the sorcerer by means of this counter-charm.
Straight as an arrow may it fly. Heaven and Earth — let them press it out. May the sorcery, thus fashioned, pierce its maker as an arrow pierces a beast.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Let evil befall the evil-doer; let curses befall the curser. We send them back, forward and straight — let them find the one who fashioned them.
"He who has sorcery done to him" — this is the single verse.
Seizing the sorcery by the hand, carry it back again to the sorcerer. We place it full in his presence, that it may slay the sorcery's maker.
Go to him as a son to his father; cling and bite as a serpent coiled around its prey. Come unwinding like a thread, O sorcery fashioned — strike the sorcery's maker.
As a doe leaps up into the water, as a female deer leaps forth — so may the sorcery find its maker.
Measuring around like the hide of a spotted deer, encircling the skin — fasten the sorcery back around the necks of those with evil hearts who performed it.
Whether you, O sorcery, were fashioned by gods or were born of men — we send you back with this counter-formula directed against the source.
Whether a woman or a man performed the sorcery for the sake of harm — we lead it back to that one, as a mare-tether leads a horse.
Heaven and Earth have been invoked for me; the divine Sarasvatī has been invoked. Both Indra and Agni have been invoked for me — may they crush this worm.
O Indra, O Lord of Wealth, slay the worm of this boy. Slain are all adversaries by this utterance of mine.
The one that creeps around the eyes, the one that creeps around the nostrils, the one that goes into the middle of the teeth — that worm we crush.
Two of unlike form, two of like form, two black ones, two reddish ones; the tawny one and the tawny-eared one; vultures and crows — these are slain.
The worms that have white armpits, those that are black with white arms, and whatever they are of all various forms — those worms we crush.
The worm that is two-headed and four-eyed, the speckled one, the white one — I shatter its ribs and I cut off its head.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
That sun has risen, visible to all, the slayer of the unseen. Striking those that are seen and those unseen, crushing all worms altogether.
The yevāṣas, the kaṣkaṣas, the dhrūkṣṇas, the śipavitnus — let the worm that is seen be slain, and let the worm that is unseen be slain as well.
Slain is the yevāṣa, slain the śipavit, slain likewise the gaṅgaṇi. Slain are all adversaries by my fierce utterance.
Of all worms, male and female alike — I split the head with a stone, I burn the mouth with fire.
With your sharp flames, O Agni, with your bright blazing light, O god — carry away the raw-flesh eater; make him settle his mouth elsewhere.
With your blazing light and your flame, O Agni, burn out the evil-doer. Let the two of us forge a friendship, and may the raw-flesh eater be at peace — elsewhere.
We lead forth the raw-flesh eater, we lead forth the carrion eater from the houses. Those gods called the grain-eaters, O Agni — may they not harm you.
The raw-flesh eater and the carrion eater and the grain-eater — both kinds together — those who have made offspring their share, them we lead forth from here.
Those who take pleasure in raw things, who have not stooped to the cooked — let all of them gather together and go hence, the evil-doers, to another place.
He who is sinful, a doer of evil deeds, he whose success is made of transgression — may the gods worthy of sacrifice lead them back whence they have come.
Wash away the dust, wash away the impurity; cleanse the filth belonging to the elephant. May Dhātṛ lead us with good fortune; may he protect our offspring.
I make of Heaven and Earth my armor; may we be in the impulsion of Savitṛ. May Earth, our mother, with good fortune, and Heaven protect us from distress.
Whatever evil things belonging to the Asuras have approached us on those days — may the milk of the gods and these divine waters cleanse me.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
I come to your grace, O father of the Maruts; keep us not away from the sight of the Sun. May the hero prevail for us in the contests of steeds; may we propagate, O Rudra, with offspring.
He who slays the unborn, he who is within the womb, he who slays the man already born or yet to be born — may I prosper against him today with oblation; may he grant us offspring that lives to old age.
Indra's two arms — sturdy, bull-powerful, these two wondrous bulls that carry across — I shall yoke them first when the time of yoking arrives, those two by which the heavenly light of the asuras was won.
Swift, being whetted, terrible as a bull, crusher of crushers, shaker of the peoples — the Saṃkrandana, unwinking, sole hero: may Indra conquer a hundred armies together.
With the Saṃkrandana, with the unwinking, with the victorious, with the irresistible, with the hard-to-dislodge, with the bold — conquer through Indra; hold firm together, O men of battle, through the rain-bull who holds the arrow in hand.
He, the subduer, with arrow-wielders, with quiver-bearers, Indra who enters battle joined with his troop — victor in close combat, soma-drinker, bold-armed, bow-upraised: may he shoot with fitted arrows.
Distinguished by strength, ancient, foremost warrior, enduring, prize-winning, bearing-down, fierce — hero-against-hero, who overwhelms fighters, victor through might — mount the chariot for conquest, O Indra, the cow-finder.
Exult after this fierce hero; O battle-men, rally together after Indra — the village-conquerer, cattle-conquerer, bolt-armed, conquering in his onrush, crushing with might.
Plunging into the cattle-herds with force, taking them away unstopped, the fierce, hundred-thoughted Indra — hard to dislodge, battle-overwhelming, irresistible — may he protect our army, driving them forward in combat.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
O Bṛhaspati, wheel around with your chariot, repelling demons and foes — breaking enemies, crushing adversaries: be our protector of bodies.
Indra is their leader, Bṛhaspati the sacrificial fee, let the sacrifice go before, let Soma advance first — may the Maruts march in the midst of the divine armies that overwhelm, that are victorious.
Of Indra the bull, of Varuṇa the king, of the Ādityans, of the fierce host of the Maruts — of the great-minded, the world-shaking — the battle-roar of the gods has risen to victory.
Indra is ours at the clashing of banners; may our arrows be victorious; may our heroes be uppermost; may the gods protect us at our callings.
From Vaiśvānara there shone forth, newborn, the golden amulet. Bṛhaspati brought it, Kaśyapa brought it, for power indeed.
Bṛhaspati fashioned that amulet as Vaiśvānara's might. The Seven Seers, increasers of life, have bestowed you for strength.
All the gods and the Seven Seers have together bestowed your virile power. You were born as a golden amulet from Agni Vaiśvānara.
The aśvattha tree was born first, the dearest body of Agni — by the creative power of Vaiśvānara this amulet was made the neutralizer of kṛtyā.
I know you as kṛtyā-neutralizer; I carry you as kṛtyā-neutralizer; I make you the kṛtyā-neutralizer, the kṛtyā-neutralizer that sustains life.
The winged one, the feathered, the powerful kṛtyā-neutralizer, the rival-slayer — the broadly extended, all-healing, fierce, suddenly-striking amulet.
The winged one is for your strength; the broadly extended one for your healing. May the golden amulet, newborn, drive away the demons.
The divine amulet, rival-slayer, demon-killer, disease-chaser — of golden womb, full of rays: the might brought by Kaśyapa.
They call the Vaiśvānara one a sharpener, born from the womb of Agni together with the Moon — the prosperer of households, the one that carries across, the sustainer of life; you are a fierce kṛtyā-neutralizer, you who smash the valagaha.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Whoever's footprint is impressed upon this dusty earth — cleansing away whatever bodily taint is his, bathe upon his body.
We, deserving of the smiting, carry you at the impulsion of divine Savitṛ — for living, for our great unharmed state.
The cutting-through, the piercing-through, the scorcher of the enemy — this amulet: the enemy-conquering rival-slayer. May it drive away the one who hates.
The pillar of truth upheld the earth; through cosmic order the gods found immortality. With the firm oblation I uphold you — may Heaven and Earth acclaim that.
With those oblations by which Viśvakarman upheld this earth, our mother — with those oblations I uphold you here. May the oblations follow upon cosmic order and truth.
Be established here on the foundation of earth, in the lap of the willing, auspicious mother — undriven-away, rejoicing in greatness: in this dwelling may you be blessed with good offspring.
Blessed with good offspring, rejoicing in greatness, rest above on the summit of the earth. May the gods grant shelter to this house; may the earth fill it with streams.
May we, with unharmed heroes, approach together this house, the best of good things. May her roof-posts be firm; may the house-dwellers be steadfast and heroic.
May Savitṛ, Vāyu, Indra, Bṛhaspati wisely establish this house. May the Maruts sprinkle it with water and ghee; may Bhaga our king establish prosperity.
O wife of the house-master, take pleasure in the oblation, of him whose end is keen and whose middle is copious. May a young child cry out to you, may a boy cry out, may the milk-cows with their perpetual calves cry out.
May your posts be firm, firmly planted in the earth; may your roof-beams be firm, O divine house. Be one with steadfast heroes and no enemies; grant us shelter for two-footed and four-footed.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The divine house is fitted for the householder's fire; clothed in grass, well-pleasing to the world. O wife of the house-master, may the heroes approach you with steadfast limbs, steadfast people, and steadfast dwelling.
O Lord of the Dwelling, recognize us; be one of easy entry and free from sickness. What we pray to you for — take delight in that for us; let the four-footed and two-footed settle here.
Darbha, foremost of plants, was born with a hundred stalks; that one of a thousand powers shall guard us on every side.
Just as Darbha, being born, splits open the skin of the earth, so let that person be split asunder who plots evil against us.
We drive away the disease-carrier, we drive away the sorcery, we drive away the Rakṣas with the ever-flowing stream; we chase off all afflictions and all sorcerous fiends.
There is indeed a low-lying place and a high-lying place; not everything floats freely upon the stream. You, O Darbha, are the corrupter of that one who plots evil against us.
At evening round about, at morning round about, at midday round about — Darbha, whose golden hand strikes down the foe, shall guard us round on every side.
Born on the mountain, you have won the heavenly light together with the tawny Soma. Spare not the workers of evil; let no ignorant person come to harm.
With its root stretched down from heaven and set firm in the earth — Darbha of a thousand powers shall guard us on every side.
Thousand-stalked, mighty, sharp-twigged, withstanding poison — with Darbha we burn away all Rakṣases and all afflictions.
Burned away is the evil dream; burned away are the ill-wishers and all the sorcerous fiends.
Let the sorcerous fiends not afflict you; let not the tawny bird swoop down upon you. Darbha, the sea-born king, shall guard us on every side.
He who speaks an ill word against us, voicelessly muttering an evil utterance — that curse, unable to reach us, shall depart from us on every side.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Whatever a stranger curses upon us, whatever a rival curses, or a mother-in-law, or a father-in-law — we drive away those mighty curses with barley.
Whatever curses are heaped together, taking effect through speech that is unworthy of its season — you, bearing barley in your two arms, ward those off beforehand.
Straight-haired, tawny Yava, munificent one worthy of our joy — golden-bowed, let him approach and deal with the curses.
When Indra drank you, Śakra the Vāsava slew Vṛtra; he who bears poison like a bull — O Yava, overcome the curses.
Let the curses roam far away, held off from here; let all their tongues that have been uttered become powerless. From the naming of names, from the anger of speech, from the glance of the evil-eyed — we make shelter and armor for you.
Let the curses go backward, shot by that ill-intentioned person — he who would harm us, though we live by our own innocence.
May he guard me round from the curse, from untruth, and from wrong; may Yava guard me round from the declaration of the mighty one — let me not be harmed.
Neither to be brought low by curses nor to be pierced through — I release for you the great armor that is Yava.
As winged birds, as flying creatures, enter back into him — let the curses return to the one who cursed.
Grant to us, O Arāti; do not stand around us; do not guard from us the dakṣiṇā that we are begging. Let Savitṛ and the giver extend to us — we make obeisance to craving and to non-prosperity.
The person whom, O Arāti, you place in front as one who despoils all around — we make obeisance to you on his account; do not confound the acquisition belonging to me.
He whom today we harness with mind and with heart — O Arāti, do not thwart him for us, him who is willing to give, O all-despoiling one.
May the god-wrought acquisition prosper for us by day and by night. We follow after Arāti — obeisance be to Arāti.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
And you, naked and roaming as one who brings sleep, you pursue people — O Arāti, thwarting the mind and the intention of a person.
Go far away, O Non-prosperer; we deflect your weapon. Pursue him whom we hate — appear as a maiden, garlanded and wearing golden ornaments.
Obeisance be to you, O Non-prosperer; do not place me in front. I know you, O Arāti — winking, goading, denouncing mortals above other mortals.
Do not thwart our acquisition, do not thwart our speech; let the mighty pair Indra and Agni apportion goods to us. May all who are willing to give today be pleased to resist Arāti.
Going our way, we call upon Savitṛ, Anumati, and Bhaga. May I speak a well-beloved, honeyed speech in the divine invocations of the gods.
That which I beg with the tongue of the mongoose and with lips as its lid — may Śraddhā find that today, given by the tawny Soma.
Let the god Kuṣṭha, the protector, come hither from beyond the Himavat, destroying all fever and all sorcery-born afflictions.
Three are thy names, O Kuṣṭha: Naghamāra, Naghāriṣa, Naghāyus — may no man of this sort come to harm. On behalf of him for whom I proclaim thee, evening and morning, and also by day.
Jīvalā by name is thy mother, Jīvanta by name is thy father, Māriṣā by name is thy sister — [and so may no man perish].
Thou art the highest among plants, as the bull among cattle, as the tiger among beasts of prey — may no man of this sort come to harm, on behalf of him for whom I proclaim thee, evening and morning, and also by day.
Born thrice from the Śāmbu-spirits of the mountains, thrice from the Ādityas, thrice born from the Viśvedevas — that Kuṣṭha, the universal remedy, stands together with Soma, destroying all fever and all sorcery-born afflictions.
The aśvattha tree is the seat of the gods in the third heaven from here; there is the fount of the immortal nectar — from there Kuṣṭha was born. He [is the universal remedy].

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
A golden boat, bound with golden mooring-ropes, coursed through the sky [bearing Kuṣṭha thence].
Where the boat alights, where is the summit of the Himavat — there is the fount of the immortal nectar; from there Kuṣṭha was born. That Kuṣṭha, the universal remedy, stands together with Soma, destroying all fever and all sorcery-born afflictions.
Thee whom the ancient Aikṣvāka knew, thee whom the Kāśya knew, O Kuṣṭha, whom the Śāvasa knew, whom the Mātsya knew — by that [knowledge] thou art the universal remedy.
The headache, the tertian fever, the sadandir, and whatever is the annual fever — drive away downward the takman of every variety, of all-pervading power.
The mountains whose backs are Soma, the waters that lie spread open, the wind, Parjanya, and Agni — they have appeased the flesh-devouring demon.
That which strikes down whatever moves or is still, whatever is about to rise up, whatever creeps, and the ten-month embryo — that we drive away from here.
If the Apsarasas strike, if the Gandharvas of the household strike, the flesh-devourers, the foolish-deity-followers — those we drive away from here.
That which mounts thy thighs, lapping thy blood — the raw-flesh-eating, flesh-devouring enemies — those we drive away from here.
That which causes thy hips to fail, which lies between husband and wife at rest, that which licks within the womb — that we drive away from here.
That which, having bewildered thee with the darkness of sleep, falls upon thee, that which desires to devour thy progeny — that [we drive away from here].
That which, assuming the likeness of thy husband, falls upon thee as a lover — that niggard, that blind wretched sinner — that we drive away from here.
Ha, hai! O crooked one, O bald one, O hidden-eared one, O great-snouted one — with the sharp weapon of Indra we destroy thee.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Homage to Taṇḍa, homage to Kusuma, homage to Pratipāva, homage to Kaḥsvadhaya; homage to thee, O Nirṛti, all-desirable one — may she of all forms nourish this man to old age.
As far as the sky extends, as far as the earth, as far as the sun courses round — for that long, O fierce Gulgulu, guard me on all sides from every quarter.
We address the Pāṭā plant, sole queen, of single vow, dwelling in one place, of single mark — the expeller of rivals — for the sake of victory.
O Pāṭā, sole queen, of single vow, dwelling in one place, of single mark — neither the rival wife born of the mountain nor the one from outside has overcome thee.
I am higher than those above, I rise above those below; may my rival wife sink downward, lower than those who are lowest.
The sun does not wither the skin of the Saindhava flower; with thee, O Pāṭā, who dost not fade, I take the radiance from my rival wife.
Not merely Pāṭā art thou, O Pāṭā — thou art the maker of good fortune; place the boon of Bhaga upon us, O Pāṭā, and moreover make me the chief wife.
Inasmuch as thou, O Pāṭā, dost exalt thyself upon the tree, wave-borne by the wind, standing forward in victory, thy name is indeed Saṃjayā — the all-conquering one.
Speak forth with loud voice to the Pāṭā, whose leaves face upward, the auspicious, the overwhelming, the powerful — the expeller of rivals.
Indra spread out the Pāṭā for the purpose of smiting the Asuras; with her may I overcome my rival wife, as great Indra overcame the Dānavas.
Pāṭā bears a golden goad, hook-tipped; with it I strip away the radiance of my rival wife, so that it may be mine.
I dig up this plant, the most powerful of creeping herbs, by which one represses the rival wife and makes the husband hers alone.
Of those whose howling from afar we hear, moving separately like the wind — of those dog-companied ones, Indra has cut off the head.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Those who roam in front together with the rays of the sun — of those dog-companied ones, Indra has cut off the head.
Those who follow the wind through the mid-air below the sky — of those dog-companied ones, Indra has cut off the head.
Those whose golden swing is fastened in heaven, in the mid-air — of those dog-companied ones, Indra has cut off the head.
Those who dance along the golden couches in the mid-air — of those dog-companied ones, Indra has cut off the head.
Those who fly on wind-chariots, supine, striking with their feet — of those dog-companied ones, Indra has cut off the head.
Those who creep about a tree, with sidelong eyes, chattering and clamorous — of those dog-companied ones, Indra has cut off the head.
Those who assemble at the crossroads, disheveled, dwelling amid rags — of those dog-companied ones, Indra has cut off the head.
Those whose golden home is secretly hidden in sandbank pools — of those dog-companied ones, Indra has cut off the head.
Those who mount upon elevated places like kinswomen with lotus-flowers — of those dog-companied ones, Indra has cut off the head.
Those who plunge headlong into rivers, clinging together like maidens — of those dog-companied ones, Indra has cut off the head.
Those who wade into fords, hissing like inviolable cows — of those dog-companied ones, Indra has cut off the head.
Those who rise up out of the ocean, uttering loud cries, chattering and clamorous — of those dog-companied ones, Indra has cut off the head.
Those who go from person to person desiring many by the myriad — of those dog-companied ones, Indra has cut off the head.
Agni is long-lived; long-lived is he together with the forest-trees. May he make me long-lived and make this one long-lived.
Vāyu is long-lived; long-lived is he together with the mid-air. May he make me long-lived and make this one long-lived.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Sūrya is long-lived; long-lived is he together with the sky. May he make me long-lived and make this one long-lived.
Candra is long-lived; long-lived is he together with the asterisms. May he make me long-lived and make this one long-lived.
Soma is long-lived; long-lived is he together with the plants. May he make me long-lived and make this one long-lived.
The sacrifice is long-lived; long-lived is it together with the sacrificial fees. May it make me long-lived and make this one long-lived.
The ocean is long-lived; long-lived is it together with the rivers. May it make me long-lived and make this one long-lived.
Brahman is replete with long life; long-lived is it together with brahma-students. May it make me replete with long life and make this one long-lived.
Indra is long-lived; long-lived is he together with heroic power. May he make me long-lived and make this one long-lived.
The gods are long-lived; long-lived are they together with immortality. May they make me long-lived and make this one long-lived.
Prajāpati is long-lived; long-lived is he together with progeny. May he make me long-lived and make this one long-lived.
May the sacrificial gift (dakṣiṇā) protect me from the right; may the dakṣiṇā protect me from the left. May it protect me from behind, from whatever shaft the world may discharge.
O Paśupati, lord of cattle, having given two-footed and four-footed animals, giving the dakṣiṇā that possesses the very self, giving life-breath — breathe on!
The dakṣiṇā that you, with faith, give on behalf of a brahmin — may that carry you across from disease (yakṣman), from the scorching heat of fire, from the grief of divine affliction.
You give this dakṣiṇā; may it not be raw for you. We pluck out for you the sharp diseases, the yakṣman. Knocking down the ear-ache and all hostilities, may all diseases withdraw together.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
With food one wins life-breath; with clothing one wards off disease (yakṣman). One who gives gold, a horse, a cow makes of the dakṣiṇā an armor.
A turban given as dakṣiṇā — may it protect you from head-ailment; a garment — from bodily disease; a shining bright gold ornament given as dakṣiṇā — from blindness of the eye, from affliction of the ear, from deafness.
A pillow given as dakṣiṇā — may it protect you from neck-ailments; beads from the flesh-eating yakṣman; an ointment from disease of the limbs; food from internal intestinal disease.
Sandals given as dakṣiṇā — may they protect the ailing foot from disease of the foot from below the sole. A staff given as dakṣiṇā — may it protect you on all sides from the serpent, as you go forth to the south, on the right.
Presenting the dakṣiṇā with good-will, receiving together the dakṣiṇā as food and strength, we turn to the stream of Bhaga for our protection.
Of a thousand limbs, a hundred are the lights of this sacrifice; the dakṣiṇā is its fulfiller, immortal, celestial. May the all-formed dakṣiṇā come to us; we receive her as one who brings no harm.
May Agni with the Vasus guard me from the east. Upon that I step forward; upon that I rest; into that stronghold I enter. May he protect me, may he keep me safe; to him I surrender myself — svāhā!
May Vāyu together with the Atmosphere guard me from that direction. Upon that I step forward; upon that I rest; into that stronghold I enter. May he protect me, may he keep me safe; to him I surrender myself — svāhā!
May Soma with the Rudras guard me from the southern direction. Upon that I step forward; upon that I rest; into that stronghold I enter. May he protect me, may he keep me safe; to him I surrender myself — svāhā!
May Varuṇa with the Ādityas guard me from that direction. Upon that I step forward; upon that I rest; into that stronghold I enter. May he protect me, may he keep me safe; to him I surrender myself — svāhā!

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
May Sūrya together with Heaven-and-Earth guard me from the western direction. Upon that I step forward; upon that I rest; into that stronghold I enter. May he protect me, may he keep me safe; to him I surrender myself — svāhā!
May the Waters rich in healing herbs guard me from that direction. Upon them I step forward; upon them I rest; into that stronghold I enter. May they protect me, may they keep me safe; to them I surrender myself — svāhā!
May Viśvakarmā with the Seven Seers guard me from the northern direction. Upon that I step forward; upon that I rest; into that stronghold I enter. May he protect me, may he keep me safe; to him I surrender myself — svāhā!
May Indra, attended by the Maruts, guard me from that direction. Upon that I step forward; upon that I rest; into that stronghold I enter. May he protect me, may he keep me safe; to him I surrender myself — svāhā!
May Prajāpati, endowed with procreative power together with the steadfast ground, guard me from the fixed (nadir) direction. Upon that I step forward; upon that I rest; into that stronghold I enter. May he protect me, may he keep me safe; to him I surrender myself — svāhā!
May Bṛhaspati with all the gods guard me from the upward direction. Upon that I step forward; upon that I rest; into that stronghold I enter. May he protect me, may he keep me safe; to him I surrender myself — svāhā!
May those who are malicious towards you and would assail you from the eastern direction reach Agni together with the Vasus.
May those who are malicious towards you and would assail you from that direction reach Vāyu together with the Atmosphere.
May those who are malicious towards you and would assail you from the southern direction reach Soma together with the Rudras.
May those who are malicious towards you and would assail you from that direction reach Varuṇa together with the Ādityas.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
May those who are malicious towards you and would assail you from the western direction reach Sūrya together with Heaven-and-Earth.
May those who are malicious towards you and would assail you from that direction reach the Waters rich in healing herbs.
May those who are malicious towards you and would assail you from the northern direction reach Viśvakarman together with the Seven Seers.
May those who are malicious towards you and would assail you from that direction reach Indra together with the Maruts.
May those who are malicious towards you and would assail you from the fixed (nadir) direction reach Prajāpati endowed with procreative power.
May those who are malicious towards you and would assail you from the upward direction reach Bṛhaspati together with all the gods.
With vaikaṅkata wood as kindling, carry the clarified butter to the gods. O Agni, gladden them here; may they all come to my call.
O Indra, come to my call; hear what I am about to do. May these ati-sara charms consecrated to Indra bend their intentions toward me. Through them may we achieve heroic power, O Jātavedas, O master of bodies.
Whatever that impious one over there, O gods, is plotting to do — may Agni not carry his oblation; may the gods not go to his call. Come instead to my call alone.
Run forward, O ati-sara charms, you who are lords of all strength. Cut down that one's life-force, together with Indra as your ally.
Having surged forward, O ati-sara charms, strike him with Indra's might. Crush him as a wolf crushes a sheep. From that point let him not be released alive; bind tight the breath of this one.
Whatever counter-charms (pratisara) that man has made or may yet make — turn them back against himself, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, so that he may be crushed, that man.
That brahmin whom those men have installed in front for their own support — him I deliver beneath the foot of Indra for Death; let the flesh-eating one silence him.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
If, having gone before, they have fashioned divine strongholds as armor, have fashioned body-guards and all-round protective shields — render all of that powerless.
Here, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, pierce him fiercely in his vital spot. Here indeed stand over him, O Śakra; I am your ally. We take hold of you, O Indra; may we be in your good grace.
Just as Indra, having obtained the formal utterance, placed him beneath his foot — so I make that one inferior for all ages to come.
By birth thou art of the Āṅgirasa lineage — so they call thee, O lord of the forest. Do thou, the Pīlu tree, drive off the rākṣasas together with Indra the ally.
Drive away the rākṣasas, drive away those that prowl about; O Pīlu, drive away the piśācas, the flesh-devouring, the ill-omened ones.
She of whom they speak — whose fruit-cluster is bitter, pungent, and hidden away — to that golden-haired one, Arāti, we pay homage.
She who, vast and of great measure, has pervaded all the quarters of space — to that golden-haired one, Arāti, we pay homage.
Whoever licks at thy womb, the devourer of eggs, the corrupter of embryos — may the Pīlu tree smite from here that miserly one who would take thy son.
When thou, O Pīlu of Āṅgirasa lineage, stood ripened, O lord of the forest — then they proclaimed Indra born, mighty Śakra, facing Bṛhaspati.
As thou didst press back the furrow while ripening, O lord of the forest — even so, O Pīlu tree, drive off the rākṣasas together with Indra the ally.
Whatever of a man's own self has been consumed by piśācas — the Pīlu tree restores it again, and he eats of thy berry.
They call thee Pīlu; they call thee the fat one; they also call thee lord of the forest. All thy names are auspicious — with them do thou guard us from distress.
The Pīlu — slayer of rākṣasas, slayer of Vṛtra, crusher of piśācas — born first among trees: thee I bind upon thee for long life.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
How shall we speak to the Asura of heaven, how to the tawny Father of fierce might? O Varuṇa, having given the dappled cow as the southern fee, O Punarmagha, thou hast deemed it good in thy mind.
Not by desire alone do I become Punarmagha, having consulted whom I brought near this dappled cow. By what wisdom art thou greater than I, O Atharvan? By what birth art thou Jātavedas?
Truly I am profound in poetic wisdom; truly by my birth I am Jātavedas. Neither serf nor noble has measured the greatness of my vow which I shall uphold.
No other is more skilled in vision, no fashioner, no one more steadfast than thou, O Varuṇa, possessor of thine own power. For thou, indeed, knowest all births; even the crafty man fears thee.
For thou, O Varuṇa, possessor of thine own power, knowest all births, O thou before whom troops tremble. What is beyond yonder firmament? What is the lower beyond the lower, O unwearied one?
One thing is beyond yonder firmament; beyond the other lies yet another that is hard to see. This, knowing it, I declare to thee, O Varuṇa: let the Paṇis become speakers of what is beneath; let the defiled serfs creep low.
For thou, O Varuṇa, dost proclaim many blameable deeds among the Punarmagh ones. Do not, then, fall upon the Paṇi by so much; let not people call thee ungracious.
Let not people call me ungracious; again I give thee the dappled cow, O singer of praise. Come to me with all my hymn of praise among the folk, among the gods and among men, O sage.
I come to thy praises that grant increase; give me that which is yet ungiven. Thou art our seven-paced companion in yoke, our equal kinsman is Varuṇa, equal in birth.
I know indeed that which is our equal birth; I give thee what is yet ungiven. The god, life-sustaining, to the god who praises; the wise one of excellent insight to the wise one who lauds.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
For thou, O Varuṇa, possessor of thine own power, didst beget Atharvan, the progenitor, the all-divine. Make for him a wide and laudable life span; thou art our friend and supreme kinsman.
My roar is like a bull, like thunder from the sky; with fierce speech I shall drive it away from thee. I have seized its essence with this my grip, as the sun rises from the darkness like a light.
Whatever waterless poison is thine, that of thine I have now seized with these means. I seize the middle, the highest, and also the lowest; by fear it shall not prevail, and now it is thine no more.
With strength I smite thy strength; with body I smite thy body. With poison I smite thy poison. O serpent, lie thou still; live not. Let the poison flow back and return upon thee.
Of the black serpent, of the Taimāta, of the brown one, of the waterless one, and of the wrath of the all-conquering — I loose the bowstring as of a fierce bow, as one unyokes chariots.
O Kailāta, O dappled one, O Upatṛṇya, O brown one — listen to me, O black ones, O Alīkas. Do not stand in the way of our friend's desire. Make yourselves heard; indeed, be pleased, O serpents.
Āliki and Vili are thy father and thy mother. We know thy kinsman on every side. Thou art made powerless — what wilt thou do?
Daughter of Urugūlā, born of the slavegirl of the black one — she who was crawling about spreading her rash, has now rendered the powerful serpents powerless.
The eared porcupine spoke, roaming at the foot of the mountain: 'Whatever burrowing creatures these are, their poison is the most powerless of all.'
Not Tābuvam, not Tābuvam — thou art not really Tābuvam. By the Tābuvam the poison is made powerless.
Not Tastuvam, not Tastuvam — thou art not really Tastuvam. By the Tastuvam the poison is made powerless.
May this herb render thy poison powerless, O serpent — the Trāyamāṇā, the overpowering one, the possessor of power, the prevailing one. It has surely expelled the poison from cow, from horse, from man.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
O Āñjana with the three peaks, born from the Himavat — crush all the sorcerers and all the female demons of sorcery.
Thou art indeed a protector, a crusher of sorcerers, O Āñjana. Thou hast power over immortality, and thou art nourishment for the drink-offering.
Thou art the protection of men, the protection of cattle. For the protection of horses, of steeds, thou hast stood firm.
Protect me, protect what is dear to us, protect our wealth. Let not enmity cross us; let nothing afflict us.
No curse reaches him, no sorcery, no grief-causing spell. Viṣkandha does not afflict him who carries thee, O Āñjana.
From the spell cast through the mouth, from evil dreaming, from hereditary disease, from the curse, and from the evil eye, from its terrible gaze — protect us from that, O Āñjana.
Three are the servants of Āñjana: fever, the consumptive disease Balāsa, and the serpent. Highest among mountains, Trikakud is the name of thy father.
Thou art the pupil of Vṛtra's eye; thou art the two eyes of the mountain. Proclaimed by all the gods, thou art named Paridhi — the Encompasser.
The Gandharva Vaida knows thy name as a secret. From wherever thou art born, O Āñjana, come hither for the sake of our unharmed well-being.
Whether thou art Traikakuda or art called Yamunā — both thy names are auspicious; by both of them protect us, O Āñjana.
Into whatever limb by limb, joint by joint thou dost creep, O Āñjana — drive out the disease Yakṣma from that place, like the fierce serpent that strikes at the middle.
The surrounding attackers do not slay him; he does not fall among the fallen. Among men he does not die who carries thee, O Āñjana.
Knowing this, O Āñjana, I shall speak truly, not falsely. May I win the horse, the cow, the garment, and my own self, O thy man.
You who are a one-bull [potion], you are of releasing essence.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
You who are a two-bull [potion], you are of releasing essence.
You who are a three-bull [potion], you are of releasing essence.
You who are a four-bull [potion], you are of releasing essence.
You who are a five-bull [potion], you are of releasing essence.
You who are a six-bull [potion], you are of releasing essence.
You who are a seven-bull [potion], you are of releasing essence.
You who are an eight-bull [potion], you are of releasing essence.
You who are a nine-bull [potion], you are of releasing essence.
You who are a ten-bull [potion], you are of releasing essence.
You who are without water [waterless], you are of releasing essence.
One and ten are mine — O herb that repels adversaries! Truth-born, truth-protecting, may the honey-maker make you sweet.
Two and twenty are mine — O herb that repels adversaries! Truth-born, truth-protecting, may the honey-maker make you sweet.
Three and thirty are mine — O herb that repels adversaries! Truth-born, truth-protecting, may the honey-maker make you sweet.
Four and forty are mine — O herb that repels adversaries! Truth-born, truth-protecting, may the honey-maker make you sweet.
Five and fifty are mine — O herb that repels adversaries! Truth-born, truth-protecting, may the honey-maker make you sweet.
Six and sixty are mine — O herb that repels adversaries! Truth-born, truth-protecting, may the honey-maker make you sweet.
Seven and seventy are mine — O herb that repels adversaries! Truth-born, truth-protecting, may the honey-maker make you sweet.
Eight and eighty are mine — O herb that repels adversaries! Truth-born, truth-protecting, may the honey-maker make you sweet.
Nine and ninety are mine — O herb that repels adversaries! Truth-born, truth-protecting, may the honey-maker make you sweet.
Ten and a hundred are mine — O herb that repels adversaries! Truth-born, truth-protecting, may the honey-maker make you sweet.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
A hundred and a thousand are mine — O herb that repels adversaries! Truth-born, truth-protecting, may the honey-maker make you sweet.
You see hither, you see back, you see away, you see — heaven, the atmosphere, and earth: all that, O goddess, you behold.
The three heavens, the three earths, and these six great quarters — by you may I behold all sorcerers, O divine herb.
You are the pupil of that divine Suparṇa [the celestial eagle]; you have climbed up to earth like a weary bride carried in a vehicle.
Her has the thousand-eyed god placed in my right hand; by her I see all that has come to be and all that shall be.
As the four-eyed dog, as the dark horse among steeds, as fire facing in every direction — so are you, O herb.
You are the eye of Kaśyapa, the four-eyed one of Śuni; do not conceal from me the piśāca moving like the sun through the clear sky.
Show me the yātudhānas, show me the yātudhānīs; show me the kimīdin standing as though just bathed.
I have seized the all-protecting [herb] from the yātudhāna and the kimīdin; by it I see everything — both the Śūdra and the Ārya.
As the sun and moon behold all beings — so do you behold them; may the evil-living one not approach here.
He who flies through the atmosphere, he who crawls along the earth, he who regards heaven as his refuge — make that piśāca visible.
Reveal your forms; do not conceal yourself — for you, O thousand-eyed one, see [me] as I come toward you.
The mokṣeja, the toda, the tumala, those that dwell on the road, and the spotted ones — O herb, render powerless the venom of all these serpents.
Of the aśvakranda, the vaṇḍa, the pṛdāku, and the gonasa — O herb, render powerless the venom of all the white-patched ones as well.
Of the dyāṃpāta, the gavaka, and the snake with the godhā-striped back — make this whole breed of the black ones harmless; grant us freedom from harm.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
This breed of the svaja serpents — make that of the brown ones powerless. You are the remedy for every brown serpent here; you are the corrupter of venom.
Let the trāyamāṇā herb speak out against all the kings among serpents — the tiraścirājin, the black ones, and those that lie in ambush.
With might she overpowers the sorcerers; with might, the sorceresses. The power that has overpowered all of you — I have seized hold of its name.
Together with Paidva's power and with my fierce utterance — the blind serpents, the sṛjaya snakes, the śaphaka, and the rathavra: leaping upon all of them together with force, she has made them all devoid of venom.
The yellow one that is a vidradha of the asita serpent, and whatever else is a vidradha — she who is the submerger of the vidradhas, the purifier: she crushed them all.
The blue-throated one among the svajas, the tawny one among the svajas as well — O herb Arundhatī, you crush the speckle-tailed one.
Let not this man bitten by the serpent die; may his father's venom not be his. For I am bringing him this herb, Arundhatī.
This whole breed of the pṛdāku serpents — render it powerless, O jīvala. You are Indra's dear plant; you are here the corrupter of venom.
A hundred flow hither, a hundred flow yonder; a hundred are the shafts of Vṛtra. From those — O waters, flow apart and away.
Fluttering through the mid-space, they were born forth from the cloud. Golden-hued are those waters — may they be beneficent to your heart.
Benign be they to your heart; benign to the regions of your heart; benign to your liver and lungs; and benign also to your inner parts.
Whatever you have trembled with in your limbs, whatever in the head, whatever in the joints of the back — may the waters cleanse all of that away, as a craftsman planes the broken part of a cart.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Let heart be joined with heart, let the lobes of the lung be joined with the lobes. Release the seized limb with the waters; may the radiance of my heel come together whole.
The divine waters coming down from the mountains, flowing forth from the gods — whatever man they reach today, that man shall suffer no harm.
Beneficent to you be the Himāvat waters; beneficent too be the spring-fed waters. Beneficent to you be the ever-flowing waters; and beneficent too be the rain-waters.
Beneficent to you be the desert waters; beneficent too be the marshy waters. Beneficent to you be the well-dug waters; and those brought in jars — may they too be beneficent.
Cloudless, digging their own way, inspired, deep in their flowing — more healing than healers: thus do we address the waters directly.
By the divine waters, by the stream-flowing waters — by the waters that cleanse: O horses, become strong and swift!
Those waters are auspicious waters — waters that make one free of disease. Just as there is refreshment when one thirsts, so too are those waters the foremost remedy for you.
The powers gathered together have brahman as their chief; brahman in the beginning stretched out the highest heaven. Among all beings brahman was born first — who then is worthy to contend against brahman?
These heaven and earth are brahman; these seven rivers are brahman; all these Ādityas are brahman; the gods attend upon brahman.
The brahmaṇa speaks brahman; into brahman the night retreats. That which belongs to Savitṛ̥ is born of brahman; through brahman Agni shines forth.
The plants come to rest in brahman; the rains rain down as brahman. All this that is endowed with self — as far as the sun surveys it — that is brahman.
The hotr̥ priest is brahman, the sacrifice is brahman; the oblation-sticks are measured by brahman. The adhvaryu is born of brahman; through brahman the oblation is poured out.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The ladling-spoons laden with ghee are brahman; the altar is raised up through brahman. The threads of the sacrifice are brahman — the officiating priests who have prepared the oblation.
The bull of auspicious seed is brahman; the cows that produce the oblation are brahman. That chariot of the divine one which conquers while adorned with its own sound — it too is brahman.
Through brahman the plow is drawn; through brahman the chariot is yoked. Through brahman the two-footed man does not falter as he walks.
The seers were born of brahman; the royal warriors too are of brahman. This universe is brahman; all that is born is of brahman; the food that will be revealed is of brahman.
The śūdras who serve the royal warriors are brahman; brahman also are those who tax them. Their auspicious dwelling-place is brahman; through brahman are their assembly-sitters.
The fishermen are brahman, the slaves are brahman; these gamblers too are brahman. Woman and man, both born of brahman; women are brahman, and the weavers as well.
Brahman on the heights, brahman in the valleys; brahman in the enclosed spaces — the forest trees, the mountains are brahman, the plants are brahman. Brahman has stretched out through all this, between both heaven and earth.
Brahman alone became the highest, O Jātaveda; the thunderbolt-wielder shattered the great demon sorcerer. May Bhava and Śarva, dispatched by Māyā, release their fiery weapon against him for his destruction.
Whatever honey the Aśvinā, lotus-garlanded, have poured into the plants, which the herbs carry — with that I anoint the head of this woman.
Whatever honeybee-honey the Aśvinā have gathered from the flower, whatever honey is in food and salt — with that [I anoint her head].
Whatever honey the Aśvinā have gathered in guggulu-resin, in collyrium, whatever honey is in this honey-jar — [with that I anoint her head].
