He who refuses to give her to those sage-born petitioners is cut off among the gods and faces the wrath of the Brahmins.
He whose enjoyment of the vaśā cow belongs to another — if he desires a different one then — the unbestowed cow would harm the owner, for he refuses to give away the one that has been asked for.
Just as a treasure is laid up belonging to the Brahmins, so is the vaśā cow; they come to her wherever and in whatever family she is born.
When the Brahmins approach the vaśā cow, they come to what is their own; just as one would win over another through this — such is the means of not obstructing her.
She should roam freely for three years, being a true cow whose ailment is unrecognized; and then, O Nārada, one should identify the vaśā cow — then is the Brahmin to come for her.
He who calls her unsuitable — this treasure laid down by the gods — both Bhava and Śarva circle around him and shoot their arrows at him.
The hard-to-deceive one lies in wait for him who refuses to give the one that was asked for; no desire of his prospers — whatever he wishes to accomplish without giving her.
He who knows neither her udder nor her teats — yet by both means he milks her — if only he had been able to give the vaśā cow.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The gods ask for the vaśā cow, taking on the form of Brahmins; the mortal who does not give to all of them falls into their displeasure.
He falls into the displeasure of the cattle — he who has not given the vaśā cow to the Brahmins; if a mortal dishonors the share that the gods have laid away.
Even if a hundred Brahmins were to ask the cow-owner for the vaśā cow — then the gods declared: "Such is the vaśā of a knowing man."
He who, without giving to such a knowing man, gives the vaśā cow to another — for him the earth with all her deities becomes a place of hardship.
The gods begged for the vaśā cow from the one in whose family she was first born; this one Nārada recognized, and he led her out together with the gods.
May the vaśā cow render a man childless and poor in cattle — he who dishonors her even when she has been asked for by Brahmins.
For Agni-and-Soma, for Kāma, for Mitra and for Varuṇa — the Brahmins ask in their name; he who does not give is cut off from them.
As long as the owner of the vaśā cow himself has not listened to the sacred verses, she may roam among his cattle for that time — but she would not be as one heard of in his house.
He who, having listened to the sacred verses about her, then lets her wander among ordinary cattle — the gods, angered, cut short both his life and his prosperity.
The vaśā cow, roaming in many ways, is the treasure laid down by the gods; she reveals her forms according to whatever dwelling-place she desires to reach.
She makes herself manifest according to whatever dwelling-place she desires to reach; and so the vaśā cow turns her mind to the Brahmins for the purpose of being asked for.
She resolves it in her mind, and that resolve reaches even the gods; and so the Brahmins approach the vaśā cow, drawing near to beg for her.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
By the svadhā offering to the ancestors, by sacrifice to the gods, by the gift of the vaśā cow — the prince does not incur the wrath of his mother.
O prince, the vaśā cow is your mother — so it has come to be from the beginning. They declare that not giving her who is to be presented to the Brahmins is non-surrender of what is owed.
Just as the clarified butter received in the ladle would flow into the fire for the god, so indeed the Brahmins, if one does not give the vaśā cow, cut him off for the fire.
With the sacrificial cake as her calf, easily milked, she stands available for him in this world; for the one who has given her, the vaśā cow milks all desires in abundance.
In the realm of Yama too the vaśā cow milks all desires for the one who has given her; but they declare a hellish world for him who withholds her when she has been begged for.
The vaśā cow wanders about in distress, angry with her keeper; let him who regards her as barren be bound in the nooses of Death.
He who regards her as a barren animal and cooks the vaśā cow in his house — Bṛhaspati will make even his sons and grandsons become beggars.
Greatly does she blaze with wrath, roaming among the cattle, the cow; and so the vaśā cow milks poison for the keeper who has given her away in that manner.
Whatever is given to Brahmins becomes dear to the livestock; therefore that is dear about the vaśā cow: that she should become an oblation offered to the gods.
The vaśā cows that the gods set apart upon arising from the sacrifice — among them Nārada singled out the fearsome viliptyā cow.
The gods deliberated about her: is she a vaśā or not a vaśā? Nārada said to them: she is the most thoroughly vaśā among all vaśā cows.
How many vaśā cows born among men do you know, O Nārada? Which of them is the most fearsome? Whose flesh should a non-Brahmin not eat?

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The viliptyā cow, O Bṛhaspati, and also the sūtavaśā cow — of these, a non-Brahmin who desires prosperity should not eat.
Homage be to you, O Nārada — instruct us concerning the vaśā for the knowing one. Which is the most fearsome of them, by not giving which one would come to ruin?
The viliptyā, O Bṛhaspati, and the sūtavaśā cow — these one should give to the Brahmins, he who desires prosperity.
There are truly three kinds of vaśā: viliptyā, sūtavaśā, and vaśā. One should give these to Brahmins, resting at ease under the care of Prajāpati.
He who is asked should think: "This is an oblation for you, O Brahmins" — if the Brahmins should beg the vaśā from him which the fearsome one gave in his house.
The gods, angered, whispered about the vaśā cow: "He will not give her to us." By these very hymns of Bheda, therefore that man came to ruin.
And Bheda, when asked by Indra, took this vaśā cow away from Nārada; therefore the gods cut him off from well-being, saying "We are the superior ones.".
Those scoundrels who speak in favor of not giving the vaśā cow — the wretches, through their unwisdom, cut themselves off from Indra's favor.
He who, having brought the keeper of cattle to the other side, then says "Do not give" — those mindless ones circle around that weapon of Rudra.
Whether she has been offered or not offered in sacrifice, if one cooks the vaśā cow at home — having struck down both gods and Brahmins, the crooked one proceeds to the lower worlds.
Blood, flesh, skin, the crushed parts, the brain, the marrow, the body — let the flesh-eating fire devour all of these of so-and-so, son of so-and-so, born of such-and-such a woman.
To the gods who are present at morning, to the gods who are present at evening, to the gods who are present at all times — I cut off so-and-so, son of so-and-so, born of such-and-such a woman.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
To Vaiśvānara, the swift-bowman — I cut off this so-and-so, son of so-and-so, born of such-and-such a woman.
O swift-bowman, swift-handed one — pierce the heart, the liver, and the two kidneys of so-and-so, son of so-and-so, born of such-and-such a woman.
To Indra and Agni, to Prajāpati, to Parameṣṭhin, to King Soma, to King Varuṇa, to Pūṣan, to Dhātṛ, to Savitṛ, to Tvaṣṭṛ — I cut off this so-and-so, son of so-and-so, born of such-and-such a woman.
To Dawn, to Day, to Night, to the Sun — I cut off this [so-and-so, son of so-and-so, born of such-and-such a woman].
To the creeping plants, to the herbs, to the lord-of-the-forest trees, to the forest-born plants — I cut off this [so-and-so, son of so-and-so, born of such-and-such a woman].
To the waters, to Mātariśvan, to Heaven-and-Earth together — I cut off this [so-and-so, son of so-and-so, born of such-and-such a woman].
To the idā-year, to the pari-year, to the saṃ-year, to the great all-formed [year] — I cut off this [so-and-so, son of so-and-so, born of such-and-such a woman].
To the months, to the year — I cut off this [so-and-so, son of so-and-so, born of such-and-such a woman].
To the Maruts, to the Aśvins, to Brahmaṇaspati the brahman — I cut away that son of so-and-so, the descendant of so-and-so.
Those who made heaven, those who were born in heaven — from those makers of heaven, those creators of heaven, I cut away that son of so-and-so, the descendant of so-and-so. May those makers of heaven, those creators of heaven, drive that son of so-and-so, the descendant of so-and-so, away.
Those who performed austerity, those who were born in austerity — from those performers of austerity, those practisers of austerity, I cut away that one [son of so-and-so, the descendant of so-and-so]. May those performers of austerity, those practisers of austerity, drive that one [away].

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Those who made sacred knowledge, those who were born in sacred knowledge — from those makers of brahman, those creators of brahman, I cut away that son of so-and-so, the descendant of so-and-so. May those makers of brahman, those creators of brahman, drive that son of so-and-so, the descendant of so-and-so, away.
May gods and men behold that woman — sinful, pierced by evil, with dishevelled hair, without a counterpart, speaking false words — as one who has caused that son of so-and-so, the descendant of so-and-so, to weep.
Crows, vultures, herons, eagles, dogs, and flying creatures — may birds and omens range about at the cremation of that son of so-and-so, the descendant of so-and-so.
O Waters, carry away all that — the blame and the impurity — whatever evil dream we have experienced, whatever falsehood we have uttered in a verse.
The seven flowing rivers — may they release us from sin.
May they release me from the guilt of a curse, and also from what pertains to Varuṇa; and from the foot-fetter of Yama, and from every sin against the gods.
From slander of kin, from evil dream, from deceit — may they release me from the noose of Varuṇa.
May Indra, Varuṇa, Bṛhaspati, and Savitṛ bestow brilliance upon me.
I am the slayer of rivals, the slayer of foes; that one is my rival among my brothers, that one is my enemy.
I slay him; I pierce him with evil dream; I pierce him with short life; I pierce him with the arrow of diminishing vital substance; I thrust him downward along the path of death.
O Dream, we know your origin: you are the son of Sin, born from ill-fortune, the instrument of Yama. Thus do we know you, O Dream. Whatever dream is auspicious — that is mine; whatever is evil — that we send forth to the enemy. We direct it toward him; with it we pierce him; we pierce him with ill-fortune; we pierce him with utter loss of fortune; we pierce him with utter ruin; we pierce him with the seizure-demon; we pierce him with darkness; O Agni, we cut this enemy off for the flesh-devouring fire; we send him forth beset by the dreadful, cruel commands of the gods; we place him between the jaws of Vaiśvānara.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
[O Dream, we know your origin:] you are the son of the seizure-demon, born from Nirṛti [— thus do we know you, O Dream; and whatever is evil we send to the enemy, directing it, piercing him with it].
[O Dream, we know your origin:] you are the son of Varuṇa, born from Varuṇānī [— thus do we know you, O Dream; and whatever is evil we send to the enemy].
[O Dream, we know your origin:] you are the son of Day, born from Night [— thus do we know you, O Dream; and whatever is evil we send to the enemy].
[O Dream, we know your origin:] you are the son of Sky, born from Earth [— thus do we know you, O Dream; and whatever is evil we send to the enemy].
[O Dream, we know your origin:] you are the son of the forest trees, born from the healing plants [— thus do we know you, O Dream; and whatever is evil we send to the enemy].
[O Dream, we know your origin:] you are the son of the woodland growths, born from the creeping plants [— thus do we know you, O Dream; and whatever is evil we send to the enemy].
[O Dream, we know your origin:] you are the son of languor, born from drowsiness [— thus do we know you, O Dream; and whatever is evil we send to the enemy].
[O Dream, we know your origin:] you are the son of the Rakṣasas, born from the fierce demons [— thus do we know you, O Dream; and whatever is evil we send to the enemy].
O Dream, we know your origin: you are the son of the Gandharvas, born from the Apsarases, the instrument of Yama. Thus do we know you, O Dream — [so runs this verse] three times.
O Heaven and Earth, O Day and Night, O you adorned with constellations — let the evil dream pass from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so.
"Whatever evil is upon us" — thus the eighteen-verse hymn.
May we not stray from the path, O Indra, nor from the sacrifice of the soma-pressers; may enmities not stand between us.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
He who is the accomplisher of the sacrifice, the thread stretched out among the gods — may we partake of him who has received the oblation.
Reverence to the eye of Mitra and Varuṇa, to the great god — honor that cosmic order; proclaim the far-seeing one, born of the gods, the beacon, the son of heaven, the sun.
Heaven and the days are spread out there; no ungodly one dwells before you from ancient times. When you race with your swift horses in your chariot, one dominion follows the east and you travel, O Sun, upward by another light.
O Sun, with that very light by which you thrust away darkness and pervade the entire universe with your radiance — drive away from us by that same power all distress, all that is unsacrificed, all disease, and the evil dream.
All distress, disease, and what is unsacrificed — we send these away from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so.
O Heaven and Earth, carry away the evil dream, carry it far away — from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so.
O Wind and Purifier, carry it away [carry away the evil dream far away from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so].
O Indra and Agni, carry it away [carry away the evil dream far away from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so].
O Mitra and Varuṇa, carry it away [carry away the evil dream far away from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so].
O Bhava and Śarva, carry it away [carry away the evil dream far away from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so].
O divine Aśvins, carry away the evil dream, carry the evil dream far away [from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so].
O divine Maruts, carry away the evil dream, carry the evil dream far away [from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so].
O divine Fathers, carry away the evil dream, carry the evil dream far away [from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so].

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
O divine Sun, carry away the evil dream, carry the evil dream far away [from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so].
O divine Moon, carry away the evil dream, carry the evil dream far away [from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so].
O divine Constellations, carry away the evil dream, carry the evil dream far away [from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so].
O divine Waters, carry away the evil dream, carry the evil dream far away [from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so].
O divine Viṣṇu, carry away the evil dream [carry the evil dream far away from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so].
O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, carry it away [carry away the evil dream far away from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so].
O divine Dhātṛ, carry it away [carry away the evil dream far away from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so].
O divine Savitṛ, carry it away [carry away the evil dream far away from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so].
O divine Pūṣan, carry it away [carry away the evil dream far away from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so].
O divine Bṛhaspati, carry it away [carry away the evil dream far away from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so].
O divine Prajāpati, carry it away [carry away the evil dream far away from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so].
O divine Parameṣṭhin, carry away the evil dream, carry the evil dream far away [from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so].
O Day and Night, carry away the evil dream, carry the evil dream far away — from this man, son of so-and-so, offspring of so-and-so.
Indra poured out the thunderbolt to slay Vṛtra; Tvaṣṭṛ poured out the thunderbolt to slay Vṛtra.
That which is the thunderbolt, that is the Viśvānara fire; that which possesses sharp power, that is the all-conquering Viśvāṣāḍ; that which has the edge that can be grasped, that is Vaiśvānara.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
All this indeed is these three: Viśvānara, Vaiśvānara, and Viśvāṣāṭ.
He wins all the meritorious worlds and all the divinities, who, knowing thus, observes the vow of the bullock.
He took it up, he shook it up, he measured it out — saying: 'Let me hurl it forth.'
It slipped from his hand — the divine thunderbolt, the razor, the wheel-rim, thousand-edged, touching the sky.
It stood there hissing, becoming tawny-gold, finding its mark.
It entered the ocean; it burned the ocean.
Therefore the ocean swallowed its bad speech, for it had been burned by Vaiśvānara.
Śakra strode out; he pondered: 'That thunderbolt has fallen in with the Asuras — the gods must protect it; let me observe the vow.' And he observed the vow.
He became thin and lean; therefore the vow-observer becomes thin and lean — for it was as a thin, lean being that Indra thrust the Asuras away.
He ran to Parameṣṭhin.
He ran to Prajāpati.
He ran to Viṣṇu.
He ran to the Lord of the House.
He ran to Virāj.
He ran to Svarāj.
He ran to Samrāj.
He ran to Day-and-Night.
He ran to the Fortnights.
He ran to the Months.
He ran to the Seasons.
He ran to the Seasonal ones.
He ran to the Seers.
He ran to the descendants of the Seers.
He ran up to Aṅgiras.
He ran to the Āṅgirasas.
He ran to Atharvan.
He ran to the Ātharvaṇas.
The Marut-hosts ran after him toward all the gods — Soma first, then Indra and Agni.
They addressed him with inauspicious and cruel speech: 'We will slay you — we know you, we will cut you off, you shall not escape.' And he became calm.
Therefore, one who calms a brahmin who knows the Veda and has performed austerities merely milks them for benefit.
He took it up with Ṛk and Sāman, with Yajus and sacrifice, with the Gāyatra and the Vāmadevya.
All this indeed is Ṛk and Sāman — these two are the arms of Indra.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
He took it up; he set it in the joints.
Offspring is indeed prosperity, inexhaustible; cattle are the joints.
He who [performs this rite] obtains offspring, prosperity, and inexhaustible [wealth] — [see 17.27.4b].
He who [performs this rite] stands firm in all the directions.
He who [performs this rite] obtains all the auspicious worlds and all the deities.
He abides on the god-traversed paths; he who (does this) fully knows the god-traversed paths.
The vital breaths are sustained in him; he who (does this, in him they are sustained).
The limbs, joints, and body-parts of that Vṛtra were shattered. These mountains are indeed the limbs, joints, and body-parts of Vṛtra.
Whatever he desires in his heart and mind — 'may this succeed for me here' — that is made to succeed for him.
He who (does this) finds in this very (earth) a firm footing and a resting-place.
He came to the gods; the gods said to him: 'We commend this heavy vow — it surpasses both the wild beasts in the forest and the domestic cattle in the village.'
He approached the bull (anaḍvāh). The bull said to him: 'What shall be my recompense?' He replied: 'Choose a boon.' And so he chose a boon.
'May I be in the world of Bradhna; may I rest upon the summit of Bradhna' — thus he chose.
The world that is Bradhna, the summit of Bradhna — that world is the sixteenth above this one.
He who [observes this vow] attains the world of Bradhna and rests upon the summit of Bradhna.
Then the serpent Āśvatthī said: 'I will not reproach that brahmin whom I heard thus — lest I be cut off from his accumulated merit of rites and pious works.'
For it is indeed a powerful rite (kṛtyā) that moves among men — namely the bull, namely the one who observes the bull-vow.
Whoever speaks ill of one who knows this — that person's own accumulated rites and pious works are swept away by illusion.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Indeed, Indra first practised the bull-vow among the Asuras; he swept away their rites and pious works into illusion — for they (had wrongly) called him 'non-Indra'.
He stepped onto the back of the bull and came to know all the worlds.
The bull's two fore-legs are the two fortnights of the waxing moon; the two hind-legs are the two fortnights of the waning moon.
His two lips are the two sacrificial cake-offerings (puroḍāśa); his two nostrils are the two sacrificial ladles (sruva).
His two eyes are the sun and the moon; his blinks are the days and nights; his flanks are the rays of the sun. He who [observes this vow thus attains all worlds].
The droṇa-vessel is his head; King Soma is his brain.
His two horns are cosmic order (ṛta) and truth (satya).
Cosmic order and truth are indeed fixed (dhruva); therefore these two horns are firm.
He who [knows this] stands firm, in accord with the fixed reality of cosmic order and truth.
Faith (śraddhā) is indeed both moving and still; therefore one repeatedly inclines the ears again and again [to hear it].
He who [knows this] becomes worthy of faith — people place their faith in him.
He who [performs this rite] wins the stream of the Vasus, prosperity that is imperishable.
The seasons serve him; he is not cut down in the seasons — he who [performs this rite] becomes dear to the seasons.
Austerity, boon, greatness, and renown — the Ṛg-verses, the Sāman-chants, the Yajus-formulas, and the Brāhmaṇa all dwell within him.
He wins both the Brahman and the world — he who [performs this rite] becomes possessed of brahminical radiance.
He fully knows the god-traversed paths — he who, knowing thus, observes the vow of the ox.
He lives long, he attains the full span of life, he does not die before old age — he who, knowing thus, observes the vow of the ox.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
He spreads wide with offspring, with cattle, with houses, with wealth — he who, knowing thus, observes the vow of the ox.
He who hates us and whom we hate — compress his breaths, scatter his breaths.
You are Indra, you are the form of Indra; you are Prajāpati, you are Parameṣṭhin.
You are the sun-realm, you are heaven, you are the heavenly world; lead me to the heavenly world.
By that by which it carries this one, by that is the sacrifice; by that by which it carries, by that is the world.
By that by which it sees this one, by that it is the all; by that by which it conveys this one, by that it is the whole.
Its feet are its foundation. He who, knowing this, upholds the vow of the bull-ox becomes established with offspring, with cattle, with houses, with wealth.
Mount the reed; there is no world for you here — this lead is your allotted share, come hither. Whatever disease is in cattle, whatever disease is in men — with that, go down together to the nether regions.
Evil-proclaimer and ill-proclaimer, along with the female elephant and the she-elephant — all deaths and diseases too we drive away from here with this.
From here we drive away death, decay, and disease. O flesh-eating Agni, devour him who hates us; him whom we hate, we press forward to you.
If the flesh-eating fire or a tiger, lodging elsewhere, has entered this cattle-pen — making an offering of beans and ghee I send him far away; let him who sits in the waters go beyond the fires.
What angry men, in their wrath, made of you at the death of a man — that which is well-formed, O Agni, we kindle you with that anew.
The Ādityas, the Rudras, the Vasus restore you; Brahman, the guide of good things, restores you in the beginning. Bṛhaspati has established you anew for long life, for a hundred autumns.
That flesh-eating fire who has entered your house, beholding this other Jātavedas — him I carry away far for the sacrifice to the fathers; let him kindle the hot milk-offering at the highest resting-place.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The flesh-eating fire I send far away; let him, the bearer of filth, go to the realm of King Yama. Let this other Jātavedas remain here — the god, knowing, shall carry the oblation to the gods.
Being urged, I carry away the flesh-eating fire, death that harms people, with the thunderbolt. Knowing, I separate him by means of the Gārhapatya fire; his share is in the world of the fathers.
The flesh-eating fire, worthy of praise-verses though praising slaughter, I send forth along the paths that lead to the fathers. Do not come back by the god-faring paths — stay here, be awake among the fathers.
They kindle the saṃkasuka for well-being, becoming pure, bright, and purifying. He abandons defilement and passes beyond it — the kindled Agni, cleansing well, purifies.
The divine Agni Saṃkasuka has climbed the back of heaven. Being freed from distress, free us also from ill-repute.
In you, O Agni Saṃkasuka, we wipe away our impurities. We have become fit for sacrifice, purified — extend our life-spans forward.
Saṃkasuka, Vikasuka, and Nirṛtha too, and the one who is Nisvara — those of you, O Savedas, have caused disease to reel away, farther and farther.
From food, from men, from cattle, from horses — the flesh-eating fire that undermines life, we push away.
That which is among our horses, among our heroes, among our cattle, among our goats and sheep — the flesh-eating Agni that undermines the people, we push away.
O Agni, kindled and fed with oblation, do not depart from us. Shine right here in the sky, and for long be visible to the sun.
In whom the gods have wiped themselves, and men too — having wiped yourself in him, praised with ghee, O Agni, ascend to heaven.
Wipe yourself on lead, wipe yourself on reed — and whatever Agni Saṃkasuka there is; also on the dark wool of a sheep, the headache-pillow as its pad.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Having placed the evil force in lead, with the headache as its pad, wiping it on the dark wool of a sheep, they become pure and fit for sacrifice.
O Death, go away along that path of yours which is other than the god-trodden way. To those who have eyes and ears I speak: may many heroes be mine here.
These living ones have turned away from the dead; auspicious has been our invocation of the gods today. We have gone forward to dance and to laugh; endowed with good heroes, may we speak in the assembly.
I set this barrier for the living; let no other cross over to this purpose of theirs. May they, living long, traverse many autumns, setting Death aside as if by a mountain.
Just as the days come in succession, just as the seasons go together with the seasons, just as the earlier does not abandon the later — so, O Tvaṣṭṛ, arrange the life-spans of these.
Mount up in life, choosing old age, striving forward in succession wherever you go. May Tvaṣṭṛ of good birth, in harmony with them, lead all their life-span onward to full living.
The stony river flows — take hold, be vigorous, cross over, O friends. Leave behind here those who were of ill will; free from disease, may we rise above to the prizes.
Rise up, cross over, O friends — the rocky river rushes here. Leave behind those who were inauspicious; crossing to the auspicious and comfortable, may we rise above to the prizes.
Take hold of the gracious speech dedicated to all the gods, becoming pure, bright, and cleansing. Overcoming all adversities, rich in all heroes, may we rejoice for a hundred winters.
Going northward by the paths, with winds and waters, surpassing the lower ones by means of the higher — the seers, having gone forth twenty-one times, thrust Death away by the obliteration of footprints.
They who obliterate the footprint of Death, placing an ever-longer life yet further ahead — seated together, push Death away from the common seat; and then, as the living, may we speak in the assembly.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Let these women, unwidowed and having good husbands, enter the anointing with ghee. Tearless, free from disease, possessed of good jewels, let the women mount the womb-place first.
Let these heroes, unwidowed and of good birth, touch themselves with the anointing ghee. Tearless, free from disease, possessed of good jewels, may they mount from the comfortable womb-place onto the bed.
I separate these two with the oblation; with the sacred word I arrange them apart. I make the svadhā-offering undecaying for the Fathers; I release this one together with a long life-span.
That Fire of ours, O Fathers, the immortal who has entered into the hearts of mortals — I take that god for myself in my embrace; let him not hate us, and let us not hate him.
Turn away the gārhapatya fire from the flesh-devouring one; O departed one, go to the south. Make what is dear to the Fathers, to the self, to Brahman — make what is dear.
Taking two shares of the wealth, he destroys it through the rite of turning away: that is the Fire of the eldest son who has not been removed from the flesh-devouring function.
Whatever he plows, whatever he wins, and whatever he obtains by his garment — all of that belongs to the mortal no longer, if the flesh-devouring fire has not been removed.
He becomes unfit for sacrifice, his luster destroyed; there is no eating of the oblation with him. He cuts off plowing, cattle, and wealth — he who continues to follow the flesh-devouring fire.
He speaks much with greedy ones; the mortal enters into distress and comes to ruin — he whom the flesh-devouring fire, closely following him with full knowledge, harasses.
The house becomes fit to be seized, the household is destroyed, when the husband of a woman dies. He alone who is learned in Brahman and who has removed the flesh-devouring fire is the one to be sought out.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Whatever defilement and transgression we have committed, and whatever evil deed — may the waters cleanse me from that, and the fire called Saṃkasuka.
Those waters, knowing their way, have turned from below toward the north along the god-trodden paths. On the back of the bull-mountain, the ancient rivers run ever fresh.
O Agni, you who do not eat flesh — thrust away the flesh-devouring one; carry the company of gods.
The flesh-devouring fire has entered into this one; this one has followed the flesh-devouring fire. Making two tigers face in different directions, I carry away that auspicious other one.
The inner barrier of the gods, the outer boundary of humans — the gārhapatya fire stands between both. O Agni, extend the long life-span of the living; may those who have died go to the world of the Fathers.
The well-tended gārhapatya fire, scattering enemies, granting each day what is more and more excellent — O Agni, overcoming all rivals, place strength and wealth in these and in us.
Take hold of this Indra, the carrier, the fulfiller — he who knows your needs shall drive Death away from you. With him strike away the flying arrow; with him may you be protected all around from Rudra's shaft.
You follow day and night, bearing them, dwelling as the guardian, the one who leads across, endowed with good heroes. Bearing the bed of the unailing and cheerful one, be with us a long time, O you who carry the scent of man.
They are cut off among the gods and live in evil forever — those whom the flesh-devouring fire harasses from close by with full knowledge.
He tumbles forward as if with the mind and turns back again repeatedly — he upon whom the flesh-devouring fire, from close by, scatters itself like a horse scattering a reed.
Those flesh-eaters who gather together without faith, out of greed for wealth — they always snatch away the water-pot of others.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Knowing the iṣīkā-reed that wanders, the tilpiya-plant, the staff-plant, the reed — Indra, making them into fuel, consigned them into Yama's fire.
The black ewe is the appointed share among cattle; lead, they say, is the flesh-eater's — and the moon as well. Ground black lentils are the oblation, their fitting share. Go thou into the thicket of the wild forest.
Having directed back the sun toward the west, the knowing one indeed opened up the path. He pointed away the life-breaths of those others and, with long life, established these ones here.
Take hold of the bull as your raft — he shall carry you out of misfortune, out of disgrace. Mount the golden ship of Savitṛ; with six waves may we pass beyond darkness.
With cattle may we cross the hard-going darkness; with barley, O much-invoked Indra, all hunger. We, kings, foremost claimants of wealth, unharmed, may we cross over with straight paths.
O woman, bring forward the full jar, filled with the essences of waters, of plants, of ghee. Anoint these drinkers with the immortal nectar; may they be steadfast heroes, of united mind.
O man, stand upon the hide of the man; summon there whichever woman is dear to you. As great as you two were when you first came together in the beginning — that same youth of yours is united in the realm of Yama.
As great is the radiance spread out between you two, as great the vigor spread in the same measure, as great the eye spreading abundantly with strength — fire accompanies the body when it blazes; then, when ripened, you two as a couple shall come together.
Come together in this world, come together also on the path of the gods; you have always come together in the kingdom of Yama. Purified by purifying rites, call each other toward that — whatever seed has been born between the two of you.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
O sons who are the waters, enter into this living one; you who hold life, come together. Share among yourselves the immortality which they speak of — that rice-porridge which your mother cooks for you.
That which your father cooks and that which your mother cooks — for release from defilement and from the taint of speech — that rice-porridge, having a hundred streams, heavenly, by its greatness pervades both the two expanses of the sky.
Both expanses of the sky and both worlds — those heavenly regions won by sacrificers — the one among them that is luminous and sweet, that is foremost: upon that one may you two, with your sons, take refuge in old age.
Let the two of them take hold of every eastern direction; those who have faith follow this world. You two have measured the vessel — may it be full for you. That cooked offering, ripened, shall flow down to you two in the realm of the fathers.
Turning toward the southern direction, moving swiftly, let the two of them circle around this vessel. For the sake of that — the cooked offering — may Yama, in agreement with the fathers, grant you two abundant shelter.
The western direction — this indeed is the better one for you two, in which Soma is the overlord and the gracious. In that direction you two have measured; may the righteous accompany you. Then may we come together along with the cooked offering.
The northern realm, enriched with progeny, making the north direction our foremost — the pankti meter became the person. May we come together with all, with all his limbs.
This Virāj is steadfast — let homage be to her; may she be auspicious to our sons and to me. O goddess Aditi, all-desirable, guard our cooked offering as a cowherd guards his cattle.
Like a father, accompany us together with our sons; may the winds blow here upon us auspiciously, bringing ease. O two divinities, who cook the rice-porridge here — heat it for us and know it truly as ours.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Whatever black bird, flying here, came upon the mortar lodged and stuck in the hollow — or whatever slave-woman, with wet hand, smeared the mortar and pestle: purify them, burn them clean.
This pressing-stone, broad-based, bearer of strength — purified by purifying rites, let it drive away the demon. Mount the hide, bestow great shelter; let not the master and mistress of the house descend into the sin that harms their grandson.
The lord of the forest has come to us together with the gods, driving away demons and flesh-eating spirits. Let him be raised up high, let him speak forth his voice; by him may we conquer all the worlds.
Seven animal offerings received the sacrificial fat — the one among them that was rich in fat and the one that was lean. Thirty-three divinities accompany you; lead us toward the heavenly world.
Lead us toward the heavenly world; may we be united — wife together with sons. I take hold of the hand; let her follow here. May Nirṛti not pass us by, nor enmity.
Past that evil seizure may we go; dispelling darkness, speak thou sweetly. O implement born of the forest, raised up, do not injure us; do not shatter the grain that is going to the gods.
O wide-spreading one, ghee-backed, destined to be — knowing, of one womb, go toward that world. Present in the winnowing basket what has grown with rain; let it winnow away the chaff, removing that lustre from the husks.
Three worlds are measured by the brahman: yonder sky, earth, and the atmosphere between. Let the two of them take hold of the stalks that have been grasped; may they swell and come back again from the winnowing basket.
The many and various forms of cattle become one form in prosperity. Drive away this reddish skin; the pressing-stone purifies it as a washerman cleans garments.
As a mother resents her son, you recoil; I unite you, O earth, with the earth. Let the cooking pots and jars move together upon the altar, consecrated with sacrificial implements and with ghee.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
I place you, O earth, upon the earth; this body of yours is one, though transformed. Whatever is yoked, inscribed, and offered — with that I sow it, and may it not be heard by the two ears.
May Agni, the cook, protect you from the east; may Indra guard you from the south through his greatness; may Soma strengthen you from the west at the foundation; may Varuṇa unite you from the north.
Let them come from heaven, accompanying the earth; they accompany the wide atmosphere from the earth. Being pure, may they themselves be purified; may they lead us to the heavenly world.
Purified by purifiers, they flow pure; from the cloud they go to heaven and to the realms of the earth. Those life-giving ones, bearing the treasure of life, well-established, poured into the vessel — may Agni blaze around them.
They are abundant, and also measured; they are bright, pure, and immortal. Those waters — a foundation for the rice-dish belonging to the couple — instructing, flowing downward, well-guided.
They foam up, leaping about when heated; they throw off abundant foam and drops. Like a young woman in season who, seeing her husband — with these grains of rice, O waters, be united.
The counted drops accompany the earth; they are measured out with the vital breaths and with plants. The uncounted ones, being sown, shining like gold — all of them, the pure ones, completing everything, bring purity.
Raise up these that have settled at the bottom; may they unite themselves with the waters. The water that is in the vessel is unmixed — the measured rice-grains go forth in all directions.
Stretch forth the rib-bone; let them carry it swiftly. Without injuring, let them give the joint. May the plants over which Soma has sovereignty be without anger for me.
Spread fresh sacred grass for the rice-dish; let it be dear to the heart, pleasant to the eye. May the gods enter there together with the divine ones; seated to the south, may they partake of this.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
O Lord of the Forest, sit down upon the spread sacred grass, measured out by the Agniṣṭoma sacrifices and the deities. Like Tvaṣṭṛ who has fashioned a beautiful form with his axe — may they be seen going around the vessel.
O supporter, hold firm in the foundation of the earth; may the deities shake you, the unshakeable one. May that couple, alive, with living sons, move it away from around the fire-holder.
For sixty autumns we wrap this around; with cooked food may the two enjoy heavenly bliss. May sons and fathers sit down near it; O Agni, lead this heavenly one onward.
Having conquered all assembled worlds and as many desires as have been fulfilled — may the two of you plunge into it, O ladle, and into the place of resort; lift it up in the one vessel.
Spread out below, extend in front; pour ghee upon this vessel. Like a lowing cow calling her calf to the litter — O gods, bellow toward this one.
You have spread out this world as a layer; this heaven is wide, broad, and incomparable. May the eagle and the great buffalo lean upon it; may the gods offer it to the divine beings.
Whatever the wife cooks at a distance from you, or the husband from the wife, one beyond the other — may the two of you mingle that together; let it be in common for you both, prospering together, sharing this world.
As many sons as accompany this earth, who have been born from this one — call all of them to the vessel; the children, being born, shall come to the navel as their meeting-place.
Those streams of wealth anointed with honey, mixed with ghee, the navels of immortality — heaven holds all of them back; the guardian of the treasury has come to claim it in sixty autumns.
The guardian of the treasury seeks this treasury; let the others around be without mastery over it. This heaven, given and deposited by us, with its three kāṇḍas has ascended to the three heavens.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
May Agni scorch the demon that is ungodly here; let not the flesh-eating piśāca spring forth here. We thrust it away, we ward it off from us; may the Ādityas and Aṅgirases accompany us.
To the Ādityas and Aṅgirases we make known this honey mixed with ghee. With pure hands, having not struck the brahmin's, both well-doers have drunk from this heaven.
This final kāṇḍa has reached the summit of it, from which world the highest one has attained completion. Pour the clarified butter along with the ghee, mixed well — this is our portion of the Aṅgirases here.
For truth, for austerity, and for the deities we wrap around this treasury, this blessed store. Let it not fail us in dice-play, nor in battle; do not release it to another before me.
There is no sin here, no deficiency; there is nothing that goes being measured equally among friends. The cooked food enters again into the cook; may the vessel placed before us be unfailing.
I cook, and I alone speak; the deed is mine alone, even of the pitiable wife. A boyish world was born as a son; may the two of you take hold in succession; may our progeny be excelling.
Let us make the beloved one dear among the beloved; darkness shall smite those who hate you. Let the milk-cow, the ox, the bird, and whatever else belongs to man drive away death.
The fires know one another — the one that accompanies the plants and the one that accompanies the rivers. As many gods as shine in heaven have come to hold the golden light.
This one came together as the skin upon the person — all other cattle are without fire. Let the two of them clothe the self with royal power; and that garment shall be the covering, the face of the rice-offering.
Whatever falsehood you utter in dice, whatever at the assembly, or in competition out of desire for wealth — dwelling together on the same thread, you two shall deposit all that defilement therein.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Win the rain, go also to the gods; you shall send the smoke of the skin flying upward and around. Heaven, all-encompassing and all-accomplishing, is of one womb — go up to that world.
Heaven spread out the body in many ways, so that you may know the different colors within the self. Purifying itself, it has conquered the dark and the bright; that which is red — that I offer for you into the fire.
To the eastern quarter, to Agni the overlord, to the dark one the guardian, to the Āditya bearing arrows — we wrap this around. May they protect us; may what is fated for us not lead us here to old age. May old age deliver us over to death; then may we come together with what is ripened.
To the southern quarter, to Indra the overlord, to Tiraścirāja the guardian, to the Vasus bearing arrows — this [we wrap around, with the same protective prayer as in the east].
To the western quarter, to Varuṇa the overlord, to the serpent Pṛdāku the guardian, to Mitra bearing arrows — this [we wrap around, with the same protective prayer as in the east].
To the northern quarter, to Soma the overlord, to the serpent Svaja the guardian, to Vāta bearing arrows — this [we wrap around, with the same protective prayer as in the east].
To the fixed quarter — the zenith — to Viṣṇu the overlord, to Kalmāṣagrīva the guardian, to the plants bearing arrows — this [we wrap around, with the same protective prayer as in the east].
To the upper quarter, to Bṛhaspati the overlord, to Śvitra the guardian, to the thunderbolts bearing arrows — we wrap this around. May they protect us; may what is fated for us not lead us here to old age. May old age deliver us over to death; then may we come together with what is ripened.
By truth the earth is upheld; by the sun the sky is upheld; by cosmic order (ṛta) the Ādityas stand firm; in heaven Soma is exalted.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
By Soma the Ādityas are mighty; by Soma the great earth endures; therefore Soma is placed in the lap of these constellations.
One who has drunk thinks he has drunk Soma when they press the plant; the Soma that the brahmins know — of that no earthly being partakes.
Protected by covering rites, guarded by Bārhaté hymns, O Soma, you stand listening to the pressing-stones; no earthly being eats of you.
Thought was the bridal cushion, sight the anointing; heaven and earth were the casket when Sūryā went to her husband.
The Raibhī verse was the gift-accompanying (bride's) escort; the Nārāśaṃsī was the wooing chant; adorned with the Gāthā song, Sūryā's auspicious garment comes.
The praise-hymns (stoma) were the bridal supports; the meter was the headdress (kurīra); the Aśvins were Sūryā's suitors; Agni went as the vanguard.
Soma became the wooer of the bride; the Aśvins were both her suitors; when Sūryā was proclaimed in mind as destined for her lord, Savitṛ gave her away.
Mind was her chariot-body; heaven was its canopy; two bright bullocks were yoked when Sūryā went to her husband.
The two cows driven on by Ṛk and Sāman came as your Sāman-verses; your two wheels were hearing itself; in heaven the path moves ever to and fro.
Your two wheels are pure as you travel; the axle of the wind is driven; Sūryā mounted the mind-made chariot, going forth toward her lord.
The bridal procession of Sūryā moved forward, the one whom Savitṛ released; at the (asterism) Agha cattle are slaughtered; under the Phalgunīs she is carried in procession.
When you two Aśvins came questioning, with a three-wheeled vehicle for the bridal procession of Sūryā — where was your one wheel, where did you stand to guide?
When you two lords of prosperity came to choose Sūryā as bride, all the gods knew that of yours; Pūṣan chose you as fathers — as a son does.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Your two wheels, O Sūryā, the brahmins know in their proper seasons; but the one wheel that is hidden — only the truly devoted know that.
I release you from the snare of Varuṇa with which the gracious Savitṛ bound you; in the womb of cosmic order, in the world of the well-performed, may it be easy for you, O bride, together with your husband.
We worship Aryaman, the good kinsman, finder of a husband; may they release me from here and from there, as a cucumber from its stalk.
May they release me from here and from there, may he make her well-bound from that side; so that she, O Indra the bounteous, may be blessed with fine sons and good fortune.
May Bhaga lead you from here, taking your hand; may the Aśvins carry you forward in their chariot; go to the house, that you may be mistress of the house, a free woman who speaks at the assembly.
May what is dear to you here prosper for progeny; be wakeful in this house for the gārhapatya (householder's fire); unite your body with this husband; and then as an elder you shall speak at the assembly.
Remain here together, be not parted; enjoy a long life; playing with sons and grandsons, rejoicing in your own home.
These two youths roam east and west by their power, playing they go around the sacrifice; one surveys all the worlds; the other, assigning the seasons, is born ever new.
Born again and again he becomes new, the banner of the days; he goes to the fore of the dawns; apportioning the share to the gods as he comes, the moon extends long life.
Give away the śāmūlya garment to the brahmins; distribute the goods; this witchcraft, having become a footprint-tracker, enters the wife who enters the husband.
It becomes dark-red, the attachment of witchcraft is dissolved; her kinsmen prosper while the husband is bound in fetters.
The body becomes inauspicious, afflicted by that evil (charm); when the husband wraps his own limb with the bride's garment.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The tearing away, the cutting apart, and also the further trimming — look upon the forms of Sūryā's (garment); the brahmin purifies these.
This is harsh, bitter, hard like a hoof-paring, poisonous — not fit to eat; only that brahmin who knows Sūryā truly deserves to handle the bridal rites.
That brahmin carries away the soft, auspicious garment — he who studies the expiation rite by which the wife comes to no harm.
You two bring together abundant fortune; let them speak truth, roused by the truth; O Brahmaṇaspati, make this husband shine for her; and let the good provider speak this word beautifully.
Remain here; go not away — O cattle, multiply this one with offspring. Going beautifully, the ruddy cows radiant with soma-lustre: may all the gods fix your hearts here.
O cattle, enter this one together with your offspring; he does not diminish the share of the gods. Pūṣan and all the Maruts drive you for his sake; Dhātṛ and Savitṛ urge you on for him.
May the paths be thornless and straight by which our friends go to seek the bride for us. May Bhaga, may Aryaman, may Dhātṛ unite and send us forth with lustre.
With that by which the Aśvins anointed the hip of the great naked one, or with that of Sūrā — with that by which the dice were anointed — with that endow her with lustre.
Whatever lustre is laid in the dice, and whatever is placed in the Sūrā drink, whatever lustre is in cattle — O Aśvins, with that endow her with lustre.
He who shines without fuel in the midst of the waters, whom the inspired priests praise at sacrifices — O Son of Waters, grant the honey-sweet waters by which Indra, the mighty, grew strong.
This dazzling, body-blemishing seizer — I push it away. That which shines bright and auspicious in the flames — I raise that up.
May the brāhmaṇas bring hither the headdress for her; may the waters — not slayers of heroes — rise up. May she quickly go around Aryaman's fire; the father-in-law and brother-in-law await her.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Auspicious to you be the gold, and auspicious be the waters; auspicious be the union, auspicious the piercing of the yoke-pin. Auspicious to you be the waters purified a hundredfold; touch your body together with your husband in well-being.
Just as the bull has engendered the Sindhu's sovereignty over the rivers — so be you a sovereign queen, going home to your husband's house.
Be a sovereign queen among the fathers-in-law; be a sovereign queen over the mothers-in-law as well. Be a sovereign queen over the sisters-in-law; be a sovereign queen over the brothers-in-law too.
Those divine women who cut and wove, those who on both sides fixed the borders — may they clothe you to old age; put on this garment full of life.
They weep for a living man yet lead the ritual forth; the men have pondered the long procession onward. What boon they have stirred up here for the ancestors — that comfort be for husbands, an embrace for the bride.
A firm, gentle stone I hold for you for offspring, in the lap of divine Earth. Mount it, you who are praised and blessed with good heroes; may Savitṛ make your life long.
May the god Savitṛ take your hand; may king Soma make you rich in offspring. May Agni Jātavedas make the fortunate wife, together with her husband, live to old age.
I take your hand for good fortune, so that you may grow old with me as your husband. Bhaga, Aryaman, Savitṛ, Purandhi — the gods have given you to me for household mastery.
With that by which Agni took the right hand of this Earth — with that I take your hand; do not falter together with me.
Dhātṛ took your hand; Savitṛ took your hand. Bhaga took your hand; Aryaman took your hand. By sacred law you are wife — I am your householder.
May she be mine, my nurturer — Bṛhaspati has given you to me. Live together with me as husband, bearing offspring, for a hundred autumns.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned a garment for beauty, by the instruction of Bṛhaspati among the wise. With that, may Savitṛ and Bhaga clothe this woman for offspring, even as they clothed Sūryā.
May the houses enfold you with lustre and good fortune; let go of this luminous form — as Dawn in the sight of the sun.
Indra and Agni, Heaven and Earth, and Pūṣan, Mitra and Varuṇa, Bhaga, both Aśvins, Bṛhaspati, the Maruts, Brahman, and Soma — may they all increase this woman with offspring.
Bṛhaspati first arranged Sūryā's hair upon her head. With that we adorn this woman together with her husband, O Aśvins.
This is that form which the woman put on below — you wish to know the wife moving with her mind. I shall pursue her together with the Navagva companions; who, knowing this, has untied this snare?
I shall loose her form into myself — he who sees knows the nest of the mind. I do not consume a stolen thing; freed by the mind, loosening Varuṇa's noose of my own accord.
This Varuṇa's noose I loosen, with which Savitṛ the benevolent bound you. A wide world, an easy path — this I make for you, O bride, together with your husband.
Rise up; smite away the demon; place this woman in good fortune. Dhātṛ the wise has found the husband for her; may king Bhaga go before, knowing the way.
Bhaga has fashioned the four feet; Bhaga has fashioned the four lotuses. Tvaṣṭṛ has carved the leather thongs in the middle — may she be auspicious to us.
With this clarified butter as oblation — for offspring and the excellent, for cattle and for sight — let us kindle Agni fully together.
The bridal conveyance is fair with kiṃśuka flowers, all-formed, golden-hued, well-rolling, well-wheeled. Mount it, O Sūryā, into the world of immortality; make the bridal journey gentle for husbands.
Let not the post harm the girl on the god-made path. We make the divine gate of the house, and the bride's path, gentle.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Let brahman be yoked behind, brahman in front; brahman at the end, brahman in the middle, brahman on all sides. Reaching the god-city unassailed, benign and gentle, reign in the world of your husband.
For you they first led Sūryā forth together with the bridal procession; O Agni, now give back the bride to her husbands together with offspring.
Agni has given back the wife together with life and vital radiance; long-lived may be her husband — may he live a hundred autumns.
First Soma was your husband; then the Gandharva was your next lord; Agni was your third husband; the fourth is born of mortal man.
Soma gave her to the Gandharva; the Gandharva gave her to Agni; Agni gave both wealth and sons to me, and also gave this woman.
Good will has come to you two, O Vājinīvasus; O Aśvins, may desires find rest in your hearts. You two became guardians as a pair, as Lords of Welfare; may we attain the dear abodes of Aryaman.
Rejoicing with an auspicious mind, bestow wealth abundant in all heroes, worthy of praise; O Lords of Welfare, make easy the ford, well-accessible the watering-place; strike down evil thought from the most steadfast path.
Strike away the demons, strike away evil thought — O Lords of Welfare, having gone from here on this bridal journey; O Agni, knower of the field, going before the cows, conquering demons, thrust aside enemies from the front.
Whatever herbs, whatever rivers, whatever fields, whatever forests there are — let those guardians protect you, O bride rich in offspring, for your husband.
We have set forth on this easy path, bearing good fortune, where the hero suffers no harm and wins the wealth of others.
Hear this well from me, O men — by this blessing the master and mistress of the house attain happiness. Those Gandharvas and divine Apsarases who dwell today in these forest trees — may they be gentle to this bride; let them not harm the bridal procession as it is borne along.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Whatever diseases follow the people and accompany the gleaming bridal procession of the bride — may the gods worthy of sacrifice lead those diseases back to where they came from.
May those who roam about, who beset the master and mistress of the house, not find them; may they pass over what is hard to cross by an easy path; let the hostile ones run away.
I illuminate the bridal procession with sacred prayer, with the houses, with a non-terrible eye, with Mitra's gaze. Whatever is bound and all-formed in this one — may Savitā make that gentle for her husbands.
This woman has come home as an auspicious one; Dhātā has found this world for her. May Aryaman, Bhaga, both Aśvins, and Prajāpati increase her with offspring.
This woman has come to a fruitful field possessed of soul; O men, sow seed in this one. Bearing the mighty seed of the bull in her flanks, may she generate offspring for you.
Stand firm here like Virāj, like Viṣṇu, O Sarasvatī; may she spring forth like dūrvā grass for Indra; may she be in the good favor of Bhaga.
Let the wave beat on the yoke-pin; let the waters release the bonds. May the two blameless, sinless ones — not evildoers — approach prosperity.
With non-terrible eye, not harming the husband, gentle, prosperous, most pleasant, well-ruling in the houses — rich in offspring, bearing heroes, loving her husband's brothers — creep toward this householder's fire.
Not harming the husband's brothers, not harming the husband — be gentle, well-disposed toward the cattle, having good heroes; bearing heroes, loving the husband's brothers, gentle — may we prosper together with you being of good spirit.
Arise! Seeking what have you come here? I, the overpowering one, rebuke you — be gone from this house. O Nirṛti, seeker of the empty, you came here — arise, O Ill-will, fly away; do not linger here any longer.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
When this bride has worshipped first the householder's fire, then, O woman, make obeisance to Sarasvatī and to the Fathers.
Bring this hide as a protective armor, to be spread beneath this woman; may she bring forth through Sinīvālī; may she be in the good favor of Bhaga.
Spread the balbaja grass upon the red skin; sitting down there, may she who has fine offspring worship this fire.
The balbaja grass that you lay down and the skin you spread beneath — upon that let her mount, she who has fine offspring, the maiden who wins a husband.
Mount the hide, sit near the fire — this god destroys all demons; O most auspicious one, sit near this fire as a joint wife; honor the gods here.
From this mother's lap may various forms of cattle be born into being; generate offspring here for this husband of yours; may this son of yours be excellent in seniority.
Most auspicious, the one who leads the household onward, most pleasant to the husband, a source of happiness to the father-in-law, gentle to the mother-in-law — may you enter these homes; may you be rich in offspring, living to old age.
This bride is most auspicious — come together and behold her; having given good fortune to her, depart with the misfortune.
Whatever young women of ill heart are here, and whatever old women too — they have indeed bestowed vital radiance upon her; now depart to your homes.
The bridal chariot spread with gold, bearing all forms — upon it Sūryā, daughter of Savitā, has mounted for great good fortune.
Ascend the bridal bed with glad spirit; beget offspring here for this husband. Awakening wisely like Indrāṇī, radiant and mighty, keep watch at dawn.
The gods at the first bestowed the wife upon him; they touched body with body together. Like the sun, O woman, all-formed in thy greatness, bearing offspring, be propitious to thy husband.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Rise up hence, for she is the wife of a husband; I entreat Viśvāvasu with reverence and songs. Seek a kinswoman who sits with the fathers and dwells in the dark — that is thy share by birth; know him as such.
The Apsarases who revel in common joy between the oblation-cart and the sun — go to them, to thy birthplace; Gandharva, I make obeisance to thee in due season.
We make obeisance to the mind of the Gandharva and to his wrath and to his eye. Viśvāvasu, I make obeisance to thee with prayer; pass beyond to the Apsarases and to the bride.
May we be well-minded with wealth; from here we have turned the Gandharva away. That god has gone to his highest abode; we have gone forward, extending our life-span.
Let the two parents unite in season; father and mother, be ye the source of seed. Let the young man cause the young woman to mount upon him; may you two make offspring here, rejoicing together.
May Prajāpati beget offspring for you two; may Aryaman anoint you both with day and night. She who is not ill-omened enters the husband's world; be thou auspicious to us among bipeds and quadrupeds.
O Pūṣan, impel for us that most auspicious one into whom men sow their seed, who spreads her thighs for us with desire, into whom, with desire, we would thrust the phallus.
Ascend her thigh, lay on thy hand, embrace thy wife with glad spirit. May you two beget offspring; may you flourish in wealth here; may Savitā grant long life to you both.
The bridal portion of the two brides that they gave us — the garment of the bride — that do you two, Bṛhaspati and Indra, grant together with favor to the brahmin.
Given by the gods together with beauty is this bridal garment of the bride. He who gives it to a discerning brahmin — he indeed smites the demons of the marriage-bed.
Awakening from the pleasant womb, laughing together, rejoicing in greatness — you two who have good cattle, good sons, a good home, may you cross over and live to see dawning mornings.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Wearing new garments, fragrant and well-clad, I have come forth alive to the dawning mornings. Like a bird from the egg I have freed myself from every sin.
O adorning Heaven-and-Earth, in whose realm is happiness, mighty in vow — may the seven flowing waters release us from distress.
To Sūryā, to the gods, to Mitra and to Varuṇa — to those who are the wise overseers of existence — to them I have made obeisance.
He who is shattered even apart from harm, torn before the collar-bones — the bounteous Indra, Purūravas, is the reuniter of joints, the restorer of what is wrenched asunder.
Let darkness depart away from us — whatever is dark blue, tawny, or red. The scorching, spotted she-demon — I release her onto this post.
As many sorceries as cling about us, as many nooses of King Varuṇa — those that harm growth and those that do not bring prosperity — all of them I release onto this post.
Whatever borders, whatever selvages there are, the warp-threads and the weft-threads — the garment woven by women: may that touch me pleasantly and bring me ease.
These willing young girls, going toward a husband from the world of the fathers — they have poured down the consecration. Svāhā!
What was released by Bṛhaspati the All-gods upheld; the vigor that has entered into the cows — with that we unite this woman.
What was released by Bṛhaspati the All-gods upheld; the brilliance that has entered into the cows — with that we unite this woman.
What was released by Bṛhaspati the All-gods upheld; the milk-nourishment that has entered into the cows — with that we unite this woman.
What was released by Bṛhaspati the All-gods upheld; the fame that has entered into the cows — with that we unite this woman.
What was released by Bṛhaspati the All-gods upheld; the fortune that has entered into the cows — with that we unite this woman.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
When that daughter of thine, with disheveled hair, wept aloud, causing much sin with her weeping — may Agni and Savitā release thee from that guilt.
When those hair-bearing people gathered in thy house, causing sin with their weeping together — [may Agni and Savitā release thee from that guilt].
When the kinswomen and when the young women in thy house, gathered together, caused sin with their weeping — [may Agni and Savitā release thee from that guilt].
When these two spouses both at the wedding caused sin, causing sin with their weeping — [may Agni and Savitā release thee from that guilt].
Whatever evil has been wrought by evildoers upon your offspring, your cattle, or what is established in your houses — may Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin.
This woman speaks, scattering flower-blossoms: "May my husband have long life; may my fathers prosper."
O Indra, unite this couple here like a pair of cakravāka birds. Blessed with offspring, auspicious, may they enjoy long life.
Whatever sorcery was wrought upon the seat, the pillow, or the resting-place, whatever malefic rite was performed at the wedding bathing — that we now lay to rest.
Whatever misdeed, whatever defilement occurred at the wedding and in the wedding procession — all that trouble we wipe away upon the blanket of the saṃbhala.
Having deposited the impurity upon the saṃbhala, and the sin upon the blanket, we have become pure and fit for sacrifice; may they carry our life-spans forward.
That body of mine which is most dear to me is afraid of the garment. Do thou, O Lord of the forest, fashion her lower garment at the front — let us not suffer harm.
This is the crafted comb of the hundred-toothed kaṅkata tree. Let it scrape away the impurity of the hair, let it scratch away the impurity of the head.
From limb to limb, do you put down the disease away from her. Let it not reach the earth, nor the gods, nor heaven; let it not reach the wide atmosphere. Let it not reach the waters — this impurity, O Agni; let it not reach Yama and all the Fathers.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
I bind you with the sap of the earth; I bind you with the sap of the plants; I bind you with offspring and with wealth. So bound and equipped, win this prize.
I am ama, thou art sā; I am heaven, thou art earth. I am mind, thou art speech. So let us two come together here and beget offspring.
May the foremost among us long for a wife; may the generous ones long for a son. Unharmed, may we follow together for the great winning of strength.
The Fathers who, beholding the bride, have come to this wedding procession — may they grant to this bride, the mistress of the household, prosperous shelter with offspring.
Those who have come before, stretching out the cord, having given offspring and wealth to her here — may they lead her along the path to what has not yet been reached. This virāj, rich in offspring, has conquered.
Awake fully, awaking with a good awakening, for long life, for a hundred autumns. Enter the houses with a well-disposed mind; may Savitṛ make your life long.
I release your cord, I release your reins, I release the yoke-straps and the fastening bands. Unharmed, in this light be auspicious to your husband.
Be gentle to your fathers-in-law; be gentle to your husband and his household. Be gentle to this entire clan; be gentle for the flourishing of these people.
Rise up, O Vājin who dwells within the waters; enter this kingdom filled with truth. May Rohita, who engendered all this universe, carry you well-borne to sovereignty.
The vāja who is within the waters has risen up; enter and ascend to your own sources. Bearing Soma, settle here the waters, the plants, the cattle, the four-footed and the two-footed.
You mighty Maruts, sons of Pṛśni, yoked with Indra, smite down the enemies. May Rohita hear you, O generous ones; the thrice-seven Maruts, full of sweet joy.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
He climbed, Rohita climbed, he climbed fully — the embryo upon the lap of the mothers and of the births. Grasping those, he found the six wide spaces; looking ahead to a path, he has proclaimed this kingdom here.
Here Rohita has seized your kingdom; he has scattered your enemies; you have become fearless. For you, heaven and earth with their riches shall milk desire here with their mighty ones.
Rohita engendered heaven and earth; Parameṣṭhin stretched out that thread. There the unborn, the one-footed, took his seat; he firmly established heaven and earth with his power.
Rohita firmly established heaven and earth; by him the vault of heaven was propped up; by him the firmament was measured out and the realms spread; by him the gods found immortality.
Rohita touched all forms, gathering together both the sprouts and the climbers. Having climbed heaven with great greatness, may he anoint your kingdom with milk and ghee.
Your climbers, your sprouts, your ascenders, with which you fill heaven and the atmosphere — nourished by the sacred word and by milk, be wakeful in the clan, in the kingdom of Rohita.
Those clans of yours that were born from austerity, that followed the gāyatrī-calf — may they come here. May they enter you with an auspicious mind; the well-mothered calf Rohita comes toward you.
Rohita has stood erect above the vault of heaven, the youthful seer generating all forms. Agni blazes with sharp light; in the third wheel of the atmosphere the beloved things shine.
The thousand-horned bull, Jātavedas, fed with oblations of ghee, whose back is Soma, possessing good heroes — do not abandon me, I implore you, lest I abandon you. Bestow on me increase in cattle and increase in heroes.
Rohita is the begetter and the mouth of the sacrifice. With speech, hearing, and mind I offer oblation to Rohita. The gods go to Rohita with benevolent hearts. May he lift me up; going together, may he cause me to ascend.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Rohita distributed the sacrifice to Viśvakarman; therefore these vital powers have come to me. I shall declare your navel upon the greatness of the world.
The bṛhatī meter has ascended you, and the paṅkti; the kakubh has ascended you with brilliance, O Vishvaveda. The uṣṇih, the syllable, the vaṣaṭkāra have ascended you; Rohita together with seed has ascended you.
This one clothes the womb of the earth; this one clothes heaven and the atmosphere. This one has reached the luminous dwelling of the blazing sun, the celestial realms.
O Lord of Speech, may earth be pleasant for us, pleasant the womb, the couch, most auspicious. May breath remain here among us in friendship. Around you, O Parameṣṭhin, may Agni set you with radiance.
O Lord of Speech, the five seasons belonging to Viśvakarman that have come around — [...] [...] may Rohita establish around with radiance.
O Lord of Speech, goodwill and mind — let our cattle rest content in the stall, and offspring in their wombs. May breath remain here among us in friendship. Around you, O Parameṣṭhin, I myself establish with radiance.
May divine Savitṛ establish around you with radiance; may Agni and Mitra-Varuṇa look upon you. All grudging hostile powers depart — rise up! Make this realm full of true and pleasant things.
You whom the dappled mare carries on the chariot as a dappled back — you, Rohita, travel beautifully, releasing the waters. By him, O Brahmaṇaspati, cause this highest ascent, the great rising.
Rohiṇī, devoted to the vow of Rohita, noble, well-winged, vast, of great brilliance — with her may we win prizes of all forms; with her may we overcome the battles of the clans.
This is the seat of Rohiṇī belonging to Rohita; yonder is the path along which the dappled one travels. The Gandharvas, the Kashyapas, lead her upward; the poets guard her with unwavering attention.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The tawny horses of the sun, bearing banners, immortal, always carry the chariot with ease. Rohita the god, drinking ghee, blazing, has entered heaven and the dappled cow.
Rohita the bull with sharp horns, who has come to encompass Agni and encompass the sun, who props up earth and heaven — from him the gods release their creations.
Rohita, ascending heaven, from the great ocean all around — Rohita has ascended everywhere, the ascender.
Measure out this milk-rich, ghee-rich cow of the gods, unrivaled — she is not to be touched improperly. Let Indra drink the Soma; may there be peace; let Agni sing forth — drive away the adversaries.
Agni is kindled, blazing up, nourished by ghee, fed with ghee — Agni the conquering, the all-conquering, let him smite my rivals.
Let Agni smite and burn those who attack us. With fire that eats raw flesh we burn our rivals.
O Agni, cast the rival down away from us; O Bṛhaspati, make the kinsman who rises against us stumble. May Indra-Agni and Mitra-Varuṇa fall upon those below, showing no pity.
Strike those who face downward down, O Indra, with your thunderbolt, O you of mighty arms. Then my rivals I seize with the fierces of Agni.
Rising, O divine Sun, make my rivals fall below. Strike them down with a stone; may they go into the lowest darkness.
The calf of virāj, the bull of thoughts, bright-backed, has ascended the atmosphere. With ghee they praise the calf as the hymn of praise; may the priests make him grow — he who is brahman — with sacred utterance.
Ascend heaven and ascend earth; ascend dominion and ascend wealth; ascend offspring and ascend immortality. With Rohita touch your own body.
The gods who uphold the realm, who travel around the sun on every side — may Rohita, in agreement with them, benevolently bestow the realm upon you.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The sacrifices purified by brahman carry you upward; the tawny steeds of the path carry you. You shine beyond the ocean, beyond the flood.
Upon Rohita heaven and earth are founded — winning wealth, winning cattle, winning all, winning by union. His treasures are a thousand and seven. I shall declare your navel upon the greatness of the world.
Full of fame you travel through the directions and the quarters; full of fame among cattle and among men. Glorious in the lap of the earth, of Aditi, I am as beautiful as Savitṛ.
Being there, he knows things here; being here, he sees those things. From here the wise see the shining sun, the all-knowing, in heaven.
The god worships the god, moving within the ocean. They kindle the same fire; the far-seeing poets know him.
She who has become one-footed, two-footed, four-footed, eight-footed, nine-footed — the verse of the universe with a thousand syllables: from her the oceans flow forth in all directions.
Ascending to the sky, the immortal one protected my speech. The brahman-purified sacrifices carry you upward. The bay steeds carry you as you drink ghee.
I know that undying thing of yours — your foothold in the sky, your dwelling-place in the highest heaven.
The sun looks out over the sky; the sun looks over the earth; the sun looks over the waters. The sun, the one eye of all beings, has ascended the great sky.
The enclosures were vast; the earth became the vedi. There Rohita set down these two fires — the cold dew and the blazing heat.
Having set down the cold and the blaze and made the mountains into sacrificial posts, the two fires — knowers of the heavenly world — sacrifice with rain as ghee for Rohita.
For Rohita the sky-knower, Agni was established through brahman. From him arose the blaze, from him the cold, from him the sacrifice was born.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Agni kindled by brahman, grown great by brahman, fed with oblations of brahman — the two fires kindled by brahman sacrifice for Rohita, knower of the sky.
One is established in the waters; another is established in truth. [The rest of the verse is lacunose in the manuscript.]
Him whom the wind adorns, him whom Indra and Brahmaṇaspati adorn — the two fires kindled by brahman sacrifice for Rohita, knower of the sky.
Having fashioned the earth as the vedi and the sky as the south, having made that blaze the fire, Rohita made everything animated, with rain as the ghee.
Rain became the ghee, the blaze became the fire, the earth became the vedi. There Agni fashioned these mountains upright with his hymns.
Having fashioned them upright with hymns, Rohita addressed the earth: "From you let all this be born — whatever has existed and whatever shall be."
That sacrifice was the first being, the first to be born as what will be. From that sacrifice everything shines forth here — whatever Rohita the seer has upheld.
His bright banners rise and blaze in the sky — those of Āditya who sees men, who holds the great vow, who is bountiful.
The knower of the directions, resounding with his flame, well-winged, flying swiftly across the sea — we praise the sun, guardian of the world, who illumines all the directions with his rays.
That you go swiftly eastward and westward by your own power, and draw the two days of varied form by your māyā — that, O Āditya, is your greatness; great is your renown, that you alone are born encompassing the entire world.
Him the wise, the swift, the blazing — whom the seven great bay mares carry — whom Atri, upon being praised, raised to the sky — may we see you, him, traversing your course.
Let no one deceive you as you traverse your course; pass swiftly through ease and through hardship. As you go, O sun, measuring out both the sky and the divine earth with day and night —

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Good fortune to your moving chariot, O sun, with which you circuit both ends at once; mount that chariot comfortably, drawn by the best of your bay horses, swift as thought.
O sun, mount comfortably the radiant chariot, pleasant, well-harnessed, of prize horses — the one your finest bay mares draw: a hundred steeds, or indeed the seven great ones.
The sun yoked seven great golden-skinned bay mares to the chariot for the journey. The bright one, shaking off darkness, freed himself beyond the realm of dust, and the god ascended to the sky.
The gods came with a great banner; removing darkness they advanced toward the light. The heavenly great-winged one, the mighty, surveyed all the worlds — the son of Aditi.
Rising, you stretch out your rays; you behold all living beings. With your power you illuminate both oceans, blazing you encompass all the worlds.
These two young ones, yearning, travel around the sea by māyā, moving east and west. One wraps itself around all the worlds; the bay mares carry the other with their golden trappings.
Atri held you in the sky, O sun, to make the months. Thus you go, well-sustained, blazing with heat upon the heavenly light, shining upon all beings.
The calf flows together toward both ends, as toward two mothers. Surely even now the gods yonder have known this brahman since of old.
What is leaning toward the sea — that the sun desires to win. His path is stretched out vast, the one that goes both east and west.
