The sacrifice goes forth fully extended, being arranged; the sacrificer [goes] toward the heavenly world. May the fires take pleasure in it as the all-offered oblation; may the gods in this very place recognize his portion and share.
The mind of the sacrificer has mounted Agni, about to fly upward to the vault of heaven, to the sky. May the luminous heavenly path, broad and god-traversed, shine forth from the sky for him.
May Agni be your Hotṛ-priest and Adhvaryu; may Bṛhaspati and Indra be your Brahmin-priest on the right. This sacrifice, having been offered and concluded, let it go to where the prior pathway of the offered oblations leads.
Let the rice-cake cauldron here, containing milk-porridge, take its seat — propping up the earth as the sky [props up] what is above. We worship you who are world-makers and path-makers, you who here are the ghee-portions of the gods.
Let the rice-cake cauldron here, containing drop-offerings, take its seat [— propping up the earth as the sky props up what is above. We worship you who are world-makers and path-makers, you who here are the ghee-portions of the gods].
Let the rice-cake cauldron here, containing curds, take its seat [— propping up the earth as the sky props up what is above. We worship you who are world-makers and path-makers, you who here are the ghee-portions of the gods].

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Let the rice-cake cauldron here, containing ghee, take its seat [— propping up the earth as the sky props up what is above. We worship you who are world-makers and path-makers, you who here are the ghee-portions of the gods].
Let the rice-cake cauldron here, containing meat, take its seat [— propping up the earth as the sky props up what is above. We worship you who are world-makers and path-makers, you who here are the ghee-portions of the gods].
Let the rice-cake cauldron here, containing barley, take its seat — propping up the earth as the sky props up what is above. We worship you who are world-makers and path-makers, you who here are the ghee-portions of the gods.
The pots covered with rice-cakes that the gods have held up for you — may those be yours: rich in ancestral refreshment, honey-sweet, dripping with ghee.
These parched grains mixed with sesame that I scatter for you, full of ancestral refreshment — may they be abundant and mighty for you; may King Yama approve them for you that you may grow inexhaustibly great.
The drop has fallen toward the primeval sky, toward this womb here, and toward that which is the former one. The seven offerers pour oblation in succession to the drop that travels along the womb of cosmic order.
The seers who behold mankind look upon your wealth — the hundred-streamed wind, the hymn, the one who knows the sun. Those who praise and honor [it] always — they milk the southern one, the seven-mothered, for their sacrificial fee.
They milk the spring, the four-holed pot, the gracious cow full of honey, for well-being. O Agni, do not harm Aditi, who is exhilarating strength among the people, in the highest heaven.
May the god Savitṛ give you this garment to wear; clad in it, may you walk satisfied in the realm of Yama.
The parched grains became a milch-cow; sesame became her calf. In the realm of Yama, may you live by means of her who is inexhaustible.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
May these parched grains of yours become wish-fulfilling cows — tawny ones, swift as falcons, of varied forms and uniform forms, with sesame as their calves — let them attend upon you.
Tawny-grained, fawn-coloured, swift as falcons — among these the dark-grained, fawn-hued milch-cows are yours; with sesame as calves, ever yielding nourishment for him, may they be unfailing for all time.
I pour this oblation into Vaiśvānara — this spring of a thousand streams, flowing in a hundred channels — which, swelling, bears up the father, the grandfather, and the great-grandfathers.
May they attend upon that inexhaustible spring of a hundred streams, spreading wide on the surface of the waters, yielding nourishment without faltering — there where the world of the righteous is.
This consciousness assembled through ritual piling — let his kinsmen look upon it. A mortal comes to immortality, to deathlessness; make the world for him along with all his kin.
Be here as the winner of wealth; let mind be here, let purpose be here. Be here more rich in heroes, life-sustaining, unimpeded.
These honey-sweet divine waters, satisfying sons and grandsons, yielding the refreshment of svadhā and immortality to the fathers — may these divine waters refresh both the living and the dead.
Let the waters impel this fire, this sacrifice; may the fathers delight in us. Those who attend upon the nourishment of the monthly offerings — may they grant us wealth rich in all heroes.
They kindle the immortal, the bearer of oblations, the one who delights in ghee; he knows the treasures laid away and the fathers who have gone to the farther shore.
The churned drink I heap for you, the mix I heap for you, the rice-pottage, the flesh — may these be endowed with svadhā for you, full of sweetness, dripping with ghee.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The Sarasvatī whom the righteous invoke as they approach the sacrifice from the south — O all-formed one, do not give these away here to the thousand-eyed one; make their life long.
This is the ancient path ahead by which your forefathers departed. Those lead-cattle who are auspicious to him — let them carry you to the world of the righteous.
I settle you in the earth, into the earth; may the god Dhātṛ, Savitṛ, extend life for us. Let the finder of treasure go forward from here; then, O fathers, be united with the dead.
This dakṣiṇā has come to us auspiciously, given by him — a well-milking cow, life-sustaining; joining with life in youth, may old age lead it away to the fathers at last.
You two, come forward; push away whatever has overcome and oppressed you here. Come hither, you two inviolable ones — that is better — as food for me, the giver, and for the fathers here.
This sacred grass I spread forward for the fathers; the upper portion I spread out for the living gods. Let the man mount that, becoming fit for consecration; may the departed fathers recognise you.
Having thus sat upon the sacred grass, becoming fit for consecration, may the departed fathers recognise you; as joint by joint knit together, so gather your body — I order your limbs together by means of brahman.
The leaf is king, the cover of the oblation-pots; nourishment and strength along with vigour have come to us — ordaining long life for the living, for longevity of a hundred autumns.
He who has become the share of nourishment, the lord of those who sacrifice and those who eat stone-ground grain — worship him, O Viśvamitras, with oblations; may that Yama ordain for us a longer span of life.
As the five human clans shaved the top-lock for Yama, so I shave the top-lock — be plentiful for me in this way.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Bear this gold which your father carried of old; from the heaven whence it came, stretch out your father's right hand in blessing.
For those who are living and those who are dead, those who are born and those who are worthy of sacrifice — let a stream of ghee, flowing in a hundred channels, flow overflowing to them all.
The bull of inspired thoughts flows pure, the far-seeing one, the sun of days, the extender of dawns, of the sky; the breath of the rivers has cried aloud to the jars, entering the heart of Indra with wisdom.
Your fierce smoke spreads through heaven, the bright flame stretched out on high; like the sun, you blaze with flashing brilliance, O Pāvaka, shining with beauty.
The Soma flows forth for the release of Indra; as a friend, he does not diminish the compact of friendship. Like a young man rushing toward women, Soma pours together into the jar along the path of the hundred coursings.
Come hither, O Soma-drinking fathers, along the deep ancestral paths; bestowing upon us offspring and wealth, for longevity, for a span of a hundred autumns.
Depart, O Soma-drinking fathers, along the deep ancestral paths; and thereafter, month by month, come again to our home for the oblation and the food, rich in progeny and heroes.
They have eaten; they have rejoiced; the beloved ones have been honoured; the self-luminous ones have been praised. Depart, O fathers, to your homes.
Whatever single limb Agni Jātavedas took from you and conveyed to the world of the fathers — that same limb I now restore into you again. With all your limbs complete, O ancestors, all of you rejoice.
There — here indeed is your mind. As kinswomen cluster around a kaputsala bird, O Earth, cover him over.
Take delight, do not be afraid, O dung-enriched ones, in this cattle-yard. Bearing vigor, single-dung-makers, of excellent vows — may we dwell beside you with these living houses.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The gods have bestowed vigor upon me; humans too have bestowed vigor. I have brought vigor from the ancestors; may my houses be full of vigor.
The gods have bestowed milk upon me; humans too have bestowed milk. I have brought milk from the ancestors; may my houses be rich in milk.
Loosen the highest fetter from us, O Varuṇa; loosen the lowest; unloose the middle one. Then, O Āditya, may we be sinless in your vow, and free for Aditi.
Those hundred bonds of yours, O Varuṇa, those thousand sacred and vast fetters stretched wide — from all of them may Varuṇa, Soma, Indra, all the Maruts, and the Svarkāḥ release us.
Release all fetters from us, O Varuṇa — those by which I am bound when lying on my side, those by which when stretched out. Then may we live a hundred autumns, protected and guarded, O king, as belonging to you.
We implore the abatement of your wrath with obeisances; we implore it with sacrifices, with oblations. […] Whatever sins committed against us, O Varuṇa, O wise king, those you have loosened.
The moon runs within the waters; the eagle runs through the sky. O lightnings, your golden-wheeled ones find no foothold. Know for me the two worlds of this one.
Sing at evening, sing the great hymn, sing it brilliantly, O Atharvan. Praise the god Savitṛ.
Praise him, the one within the river, the son of truth, the youthful one — he of guileless speech, of goodly grace.
May that god Savitṛ, lord of good things, press out for us good things — through this good praise may he grant us easy passage.
O priests, press the soma for Indra and run the rite — he who hears the praiser's call, and hears our invocation.
Press the soma for Indra the soma-drinker, the wielder of the vajra — he is the young conqueror, the ruler, much praised by men.
Let the soma drops enter you, O full one, as birds enter a tree — crush and strike down the hostile demons.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Far from us be that bolt, O gods — may it be elsewhere. Far from mortals be the curse.
May our bounty be as a friend; may Indra be our friend, and Savitṛ our friend. May Bhaga, of true law, be our friend.
May the divine goddesses, mistresses of men, attend us with great shelter and aid — they whose wings are uncut.
I implore Agni and Bhava — all protect us, press down the serpent, the disease, and fierce plague. O Aditi, keep divine fear far from us; O Maruts, grant us shelter and heroic strength.
I implore heaven and earth, the mountains, the waters, the sky, the sun, the broad atmosphere, the forest trees, the plants, the cows, and the sacred verses — may the lords of cosmic order be gracious to us.
I call Viṣṇu, Pūṣan, Brahmaṇaspati, Bhaga, the worthy Savitṛ for our aid. May Soma, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Agni, and mighty Bhaga come here to protect us.
May Indra and Pūṣan protect us; may Varuṇa and the Maruts protect us. O Child of the Waters, O seven rivers, protect us — may Viṣṇu protect us, and heaven too.
May heaven and earth protect us for our victory; may the pressing stone protect us, may Soma protect us from distress. May the goddess Sarasvatī, of sweet invocation, protect us; may Agni protect us with his benevolent guardians.
May the two divine Aśvins, of great wonders, protect us; may Dawn and Night keep us safe. O Child of the Waters, of unwavering protection — O god at the summit of all — O Aditi, grant us shelter.
Tvaṣṭṛ, my divine speech, Parjanya, Brahmaṇaspati — may Aditi now protect us with sons and brothers; may she grant strength hard to cross for our rescue.
May Aṃśa, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, and Aditi protect us from distress. May the unharmed one drive away his enmity, and ward off the enemy near him.
O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, increase us for all wholeness; advance our resolve and our glory together. Protect us, O wide one, ever-vigilant; O Father Heaven, drive away misfortune from here.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Those who afflict our body with words and sorcerous acts, O Soma — cut them down low so that they may wither; may they not see the sun rising.
With your arrows, O Soma, with your bow, with your fist-smiting power do we prevail. Cut down those who have done this wrong — we strike them with staffs and with mighty acts.
May the treader lead them by the footstep; may the ancestors teach them their doom with blows — so that not one of them may live.
By the path by which Soma, Aditi, and the Mitras travel, the guileless ones — by that path be our protector.
He who harms us the well-praised, the ill-praiser, O Soma — strike him in the face with the vajra; crushed, he shall go away.
He who attacks us, O Soma — both the kinsman and the outsider — cut off his strength; like great heaven, smite him with your own killing blow.
O gods, may evil return upon the evil-doer; may guilt recognize him who made the guilt. May the knowing son return to strike the father — and whatever is his own is struck down too.
With what curse he curses, and with what curse we curse him in return — grasping both together, from that near place let them hurl the bolt at him.
The curses that dwell in the earth, those in the broad atmosphere, those in the wind's current — with all of these we roll him over: him who hates us, and him whom we hate.
Those who have crept around us bearing harmful charms — may the god pluck out their root as one pulls up a cucumber vine.
When the evil-placing gods seek to fasten evil upon another — the burden of that evil, hard to bear, shall come back upon its maker.
Let the evil of the evil-placer flow back again, as glory flows; like the great flood of the river Sindhu, let it roll back upon them.
The lightning bolt ever hurled, flying westward, has indeed fallen — may it come back and strike the one who sent it.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The one who ever presses forward against another, smearing arrows with poison — let the arrow strike him back in return.
Whatever you hurl abundantly against the one facing you to drive him away — eat that as poison eats poison.
Homage to you, O Son of the slope, from where you gather heat — be gracious to our bodies; bring well-being to our offspring.
Homage to you, O Son of the slope; homage to your burning bolt. We know your highest abode in the hidden place — you are set within the ocean as the navel.
You whom all the gods begot, fashioning you as an arrow, swift and fierce for casting — praised in our assembly, be gracious to us under the direction of Mitra and Varuṇa.
O Maruts with sun-like skin, O Sons of the slope, grant us shelter, grant us wide protection.
Be gracious, be completely gracious — be gracious to us for the sake of our cows, our offspring, and our bodies.
Homage to you, O lightning; homage to you, O thunder. Homage to you, O hailstone, with which you hurl against the steadfast one.
He who, being no god, attacks us — O Brahmaṇaspati, deliver all of him up to us.
With those powers by which you, O Soma, overcome and subdue the asuras — with those same powers be our protector.
The strengths of the asuras that you, O gods, have chosen for yourselves — with those same strengths speak on our behalf.
O Agni, fed with ghee, lead him upward, to the highest place; unite him with radiance — may he become a sharer in the gods' portion.
O Indra, make him foremost among his kinsmen; may he be the master of his peers. Unite him with the abundance of wealth; make him great through offspring.
He in whose house we make the oblation — him, O Agni, do you increase. May Soma speak on his behalf, and this Brahmaṇaspati too.
We implore Vaiśvānara, the possessor of cosmic order, the lord of the light of truth — the unceasing, blazing heat.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
He spread this forth, lifting up the heavenly light of sacrifice; the self-willed one releases the seasons.
Agni in his beloved abodes, the desire of all that has been and all that shall be — the sole sovereign shines resplendent.
As the sun circles the sky, I have come to the birth-place of the serpents; as the night sweeps aside the other world, so ward off this poison.
By what was uttered in ancient times by the brahmin-priests, by the seers, by the gods — by whatever existed and shall come to be — with that I ward off your poison.
The rivers are mingled with honey; the mountains and hills are honey; sweet is the Paruṣṇī, sweet the water-plants — may there be ease for the face, ease for the heart.
As this broad earth has borne the established world, so may your embryo be held firm, to be brought forth for the Vivifier.
[Lacuna] ... may these forest-lords be borne ... [Lacuna].
As this broad earth has borne the mountains and the waters, so may your embryo be held firm, to be brought forth for well-being.
Flowing by day and flowing by night — I, of excellent resolve, call upon you, divine waters, you who flow on.
May the waters, invoked, the active ones, release from here for guidance — may they immediately come to pass.
At the impulsion of the divine Savitṛ, human beings perform their work — may these waters and herbs be propitious to us.
Of your hundred channels and of your thousand veins, those that stand in the middle — together they have come to rest at the extremities.
Around you the sand-made bows stood firm even crosswise; stand still, trembling lightly, be at peace.
Those kinswomen who go yonder, all clad in red — like women without brothers they stand, their splendor struck down.
Stand still, O lower one; stand still, O upper one; and you too stand still, O middle one; may the little finger also stand still; may the great vein stand still.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Homage to the deaths inflicted by gods, homage to the deaths inflicted by kings; and those deaths that belong to the common folk — to them, O Death, I offer you reverence.
Homage to you in your aspect of pronouncing over, homage to you in your aspect of pronouncing away; O Death, homage to your benevolent thought, and to your malevolent thought this homage.
Homage to your sorcerers, homage to your remedies; O Death, homage to your roots, and to the brahmin-priests this homage.
The nine and the ninety that come together towards the neck — may all of them vanish from here, like the growths of the apacit disease.
The seven and the seventy that come together towards the shoulders — may all of them vanish from here, like the growths of the apacit disease.
The five and the fifty that come together towards the throat — may all of them vanish from here, like the growths of the apacit disease.
The devouring one, the non-devouring one — your essence, O fierce devourer; we have eaten your gruel — for you are indeed that one by which you have devoured yourself.
The brown one and the brown-eared one, the blue-eared pot-lady — O Corpse-gazer.
O Tauvilikā, with Avelā — one has devoured, Ailava has devoured; here, accepting your own oblation with mind — svāhā.
Svāhā — with mind I make this offering; into her whose they were I pour it, O terrible one, for the releasing of these bound ones.
People think of you as Earth; I know you all around as Nirṛti, from every side; in truth you are rich in oblations — this is your portion, and through it service is to be rendered to you — svāhā.
So thus, O Nirṛti of all desirable things, release from us your iron bonds; you who are allied with Yama as his twin — the one who hates us and the one we hate, upon him cast all those bonds back.
You are the highest among plants; the trees are your support. May there be support for us against the one who seeks to harm us.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Whether he who seeks to harm us has kinsmen or has no kinsmen — crossing beyond all those with kinsmen, may I become the highest.
Just as Soma is called the highest oblation among plants, so — like you among trees — may I become the highest.
By the word of Indra, of Mitra, and of Varuṇa, and by the word of all the gods, we ward off the disease from you.
Just as Vṛtra held back these waters striving to flow in every direction, so I ward off your disease with Agni Vaiśvānara.
With a firm oblation we anoint the firm Soma; here let Indra make the clans, the tribute-bearing ones, yours alone.
I have brought you here; you have become present within, firm, standing unshaken; may all the clans come to you — let not the kingdom slip away from you.
Be here, do not go away, standing unshaken like a mountain; be firm here, O Indra — hold the kingdom firm here.
Indra made this one firm with a firm oblation; in his favor Soma spoke out, and so did Brahmaṇaspati here.
May the divine Savitṛ hold your realm firm, may divine Bṛhaspati hold it firm; may Indra and Agni hold your realm, the unshaken, firmly in place.
Firm is the sky, firm is the earth, firm are the oceans and the mountains; firm indeed by sacred law, firm — firm is this king of the clans.
The bull of Indra, the bull of the sky, the bull of the earth is this one; bull of all that exists — become the sole bull.
The ocean rules over the flowing waters; Agni is the lord of the earth; the Sun rules over the constellations; you [rule over ...] [Lacuna].
You are the sovereign of the Asuras, the chief among human beings; you are a half-sharer among the gods — become the sole bull.
Indra and Pūṣan have run around the paths of these enemies; may those armies of the foes yonder be confused today and henceforth.
Bewildered, may the foes wander like headless serpents; then, of these whose fire is blocked, let Indra smite the best one after another.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Bind the bull's hide upon these enemies; strike terror as of the antelope into them; may the foe rush away in retreat, and may the cow approach toward us.
O mighty Agni, you yoke all things together for the lord; you are kindled in the seat of refreshment — bring us riches.
Be of one mind, be united, may your minds be in accord; as the gods of old, in concord, attend to their share.
Common is your prayer, common your assembly, common your mind — your thoughts together; with a common oblation I offer for you, that you may be of one accord.
The sun rises across the sky, having mounted all the regions before; Āditya passes over the mountains, seen by all, the destroyer of the unseen evil.
I have brought the herb of Kaṇva, knowing the life-force, renowned, the all-healing plant — quell this person's unseen afflictions.
The cows have settled in the cowpen, the wild beasts have rested; the banners of the people have been furled, the unseen evils have been checked.
You flow forth from the Himālaya and make your way to the Sindhu; those divine waters have surely given me that heart-illumining medicine.
Whatever flashed through the eyes, through the heels, and through the heart — the waters have expelled all that, as Tvaṣṭṛ removes a defect from a cart.
All you rivers, queens of the Sindhu, consorts of the Sindhu — give us the medicine for that; with it we shall enjoy your gift.
May the divine hosts purify me, may the Manus purify me by thought, may all beings purify me — may the purifying stream purify me.
May the purifying current purify me for will, for power, for life, and for long beholding of the sun.
O divine Savitṛ, purify us with both — with the filter and with your impulse — for clear sight.
The foremost dart of jealousy, the lowest and the highest — the wrath that dwells in the heart, the grief — these we charm out of you.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
That which is lodged in your heart, tending toward the mind, about to fly — from that I release your jealousy, as steam is released from a skin.
As the earth is dead in mind toward the dead, more dead in mind than the dead — as the mind of a corpse is dead — so let the mind of jealousy be dead.
May Heaven and Earth, the two all-knowing ones, may the bright and great South wind carry me across; with awareness let Soma, Agni, Vāyu, Savitṛ, and Bhaga come along with the self-law.
Mind has come back to us, life has come back, sight has come back, intention has come back; Vaiśvānara, undeceived, protector of the body, stands within, guarding from misfortune and from blame.
We have come together with radiance, with vital sap, with our bodies, with the auspicious mind; may Tvaṣṭṛ, well-shaped, make wide room — let him fashion the body's injury into wholeness.
This is that superior yoke by which I adorn Indra for the conquest; increase his dominion, his glory, his greatness — as rain increases the grass.
O Agni and Soma, increase his sovereignty, increase his wealth; and for the supremacy of his kingdom make the yoke highest.
Both the one with kin and the one without kin, the one born here and the one born outside — all of them you deliver to us, for the sacrificer who presses the soma.
May great fame, driven by Indra, thousand-peaked, well-wrought, powerful, increase; flowing forth for long life — increase the oblation-bearer for all-round completeness.
Indra was born with glory, Agni with glory, Soma was born with glory; of all that exists I am the most glorious.
We, glorious, serve you, O Agni, the glorious one, with glories and with this oblation; grant us the kingdom driven by Indra — may we be under your protection, under your advocacy.
I draw your wrath from your heart as one draws the bowstring from a bow; then, becoming of one mind, we two shall go together like friends.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
We lead your anger away so we two may go together like friends; with a heavy stone we press your wrath down below.
I tread upon your anger with both heels and forefeet; I drive away from you the rod-worthy blow, I drive away your wrath.
The path was golden, the oars were golden, the boats were golden by which I brought kuṣṭha here.
Born on the mountain where the suparṇa bird cries, born around the Himālaya — they come famed with riches: O kuṣṭha, come here, destroyer of fever.
You who are born in the mountains, mightiest of herbs — O kuṣṭha, come here, destroyer of fever, driving fever away from here.
Make great obeisance to the Idāvatsara, the Parivatsara, and the Saṃvatsara; may we be in the good favor of those worthy of sacrifice, in their auspicious goodwill.
Your many god-trodden paths that pass along Heaven and Earth — whichever of these may bring us victory, may all the gods surround us for that one.
Autumn, winter, the cool season, spring, summer, the rains — set us in good course; grant us a share in cattle and in plants — only in a sheltered place may we dwell in your shelter.
Let Vaiśvānara come forth to us with help from afar; may Agni with hymns free us from distress.
May Vaiśvānara come to us, together attending this sacrifice and my praise-song.
May Vaiśvānara along with the Aṅgirasas fashion our praise-song and sacrifice; may he seize brilliant light and the sun among these.
I have conquered you when scratched, I have conquered you when blocked; as a wolf churns a sheep, so I churn what you have done.
As a thunderbolt always strikes a tree without resistance, so may I strike that gambler with the dice, without resistance.
From the swift and the slow, from the clans that seek the gods — may fortune come together from all sides; what is made is in my hand.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
As long as the sky endures, as long as the earth, as long as the sun shines — for that long I release poison into you, as long as the rivers flow.
They rise up breathing out like cattle from the stall; of the snakes that are seen, the poison has no one to speak it away.
The speckle-bowed one struck at the junction of the arteries; the poison leapt to the head and scattered through the limbs.
May the serpent not slay us, O gods, us with our offspring, together with our men; let it not spread what is closed, let it not close what is open.
I set tooth against your teeth, I set jaw against your jaws; I set tongue against your tongue, I set mouth against your mouth.
Homage to the dark serpent, homage to the king who goes sideways; homage to the coiling tawny one, homage to the divine folk.
To the mind, to consciousness, to thought, to intention, and to understanding; to wisdom, to learning, and to sight — we pay homage with our oblation.
To the in-breath, to the out-breath, to the diffused breath, to the abundantly seed-bearing; to Sarasvatī of wide extent — we pay homage with our oblation.
May the divine seers, protectors of the body, the pure ones, born of austerity, not abandon us. O immortals, accompany us mortals; grant us further lifespan to live.
This indeed is the remedy, this is Rudra's remedy, by which they warded off the arrow of single point and hundred barbs.
Sprinkle us with the jālāṣa water; moisten us with the jālāṣa. Grant us that jālāṣa, the auspicious remedy, to keep us alive.
May there be ease for us and joy for us; let nothing whatever afflict us. May earth cleanse away disease; may all be a remedy for us.
May Indra the bountiful make me glorious; may Soma, Varuṇa, Vāyu, and Agni make me glorious. May the god Savitṛ make me glorious; may I be dear to the giver, beloved of the sacrificial fee.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
As Indra is glorious between heaven and earth, as the waters are among the plants — as he is among all the gods — so may we be glorious among the gods.
Glorious ourselves, with glories we approach glorious Indra; we honor him with this oblation. May he establish for us the sovereignty driven by Indra; may we be under his protection, his special pleaders.
Let Varuṇa come here; let Soma, Agni, and Bṛhaspati come here together with the Vasus. O kinsmen, all of one mind, come together to share the glory of this fierce and discerning one.
Come here, do not depart from us. May Pūṣan make for you a pathless way if you go beyond. The lord of the homestead has called you here; may your delight, O kinsmen, rest in me.
Whatever vigor is within your hearts, whatever intention has entered your minds — that I attune with oblation and clarified butter; may your delight, O kinsmen, rest in me.
Come to my thought, all of you, at the moment of departure and departure, as to the invocation of Indra and Agni. May Bṛhaspati yoke you to me; be of one mind and follow my speech.
I seize your minds with my mind; come to my thought with your thoughts. I make your hearts subject to my will; come following in my path, come to me.
Let your eye come to me, let your breath come to me; may the Dhātṛ make your path follow my footstep. Whether your elders or your young ones — come, following in my path, come with those who follow.
You were born above the gods; you are placed as a friend of Soma. As such, be gracious for the in-breath, the out-breath, and the sight of this one.
You were indeed struck against the iron post, bound by the thousand deaths. May Yama give you back to me; to that god we pay homage with oblation.
The bond that the divine Nirṛti has bound upon your neck, the unbreakable fetter — that I loose from you for life and for strength. Being released, eat untroubled food.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Homage to you, O Nirṛti who possesses all good things; loosen this iron bond. You, being in accord with Yama and the Fathers, cause this one to ascend to the highest vault of heaven.
Offer this well into the inner fire, with clarified butter, as the destroyer of sorcerers. O Agni, burn the demons from afar; let them not scorch our bodies.
Śarva has broken your necks, O Piśācas; may Agni crush your ribs. The all-potent plant has united you with death.
Make us free of Piśācas below, free of Piśācas above; O Indra, make us free of Piśācas behind, free of Piśācas in front.
Indra first made the Asuras handless. We too cut off the arms of our enemies with this oblation.
Let the enemy be handless, powerless against us — those who come against us in battle with their armies. Strike them together, O Indra, with a great blow; let the sin-slayer, piercing them, make them flee.
Let their fury sink down, let their two arms yoked to the mind sink down. O Parāśara, crush their outward-turned vigor; bring the wealth here toward us.
You who stretch your bows, who draw them back, who shoot and run — stand there as enemies made handless; today Indra has dispersed you.
Let the enemies be handless; we wither their limbs. O Indra, may we divide up their possessions among our herds.
The handlessness you gods shoot as an arrow upon the handless — may my warriors conquer with steadfast Indra as their ally.
The aśvattha tree has climbed the śamī tree; there the rite for begetting a son is performed. That very thing is his remedy — what they bring forth in women.
The seed truly arises in the male and is poured into the female. That indeed is the means of obtaining a son — so spoke Prajāpati.
Prajāpati reflected and Sinīvālī fashioned it: placing the female nature elsewhere, and placing the male nature here.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
"The plants over which Soma is king" — thus one verse [cited by reference].
May they release me from the curse-born sin, and from that which belongs to Varuṇa; and from the snare of Yama, from all evil done against the gods.
Whatever sin we have committed with the eye, with the mind, or with speech, whether waking or sleeping — from that sin may wise Soma purify me by his sovereign power.
Let the sacrifice be all-conquering; let Agni be all-conquering; let Soma be all-conquering; let Indra be all-conquering. So that this one may overcome all battle hosts — thus we offer this oblation at the Agnihotra.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, may there be self-power; swell here the progeny-rich sovereignty with sweetness. Drive hatred and Nirṛti away; bestow upon this one sovereignty, brilliance, and vital force.
"This hero" — thus one verse [cited by reference].
Like the onslaught of fire his vigor advances, and like one intoxicated he goes away wailing. To you, O Fever — ruddy, tawny, bearing scorching treasure — let there be homage.
Homage to Yama, homage to Death, homage to King Varuṇa the radiant. Homage to the lord of the field, homage to the sky, homage to the earth, homage to the plants.
This one who makes people yellow, burning them up, assailing them like fire — be without sap now, O Fever; depart hence, downward or away.
Indra conquers; may he not be conquered. The overlord shall rule as king among kings. Being much praised, worthy of invocation, worthy of acclaim — worthy of approach and homage, may he be here.
You, O Indra, are the overlord, famed; you are the overcoming power over people. Rule over these divine peoples; may your ageless sovereignty be endowed with long life.
In the eastern direction you are the overlord, O Indra; in the northern direction you are the slayer of Vṛtra and the Dasyus. Wherever the famous rivers flow, that is your conquest; to the south you are the bull, worthy of oblation.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
I call upon Indra, who is most spacious, to protect you from the snares that have ensnared you before; I invoke the mighty one, the swift-striker, who bears many names, the sole-born.
Whatever martial blow seeks to slay you today and cannot be lifted — around that we wrap the two arms of Indra on all sides.
We wrap the two arms of Indra, the protector, all around; may he protect us. O divine Savitṛ and King Soma, make us well-minded for our well-being.
The gods gave it, the Sun gave it, Heaven gave it, the Earth gave it; all the Sarasvatīs, of one mind, gave the antidote to poison.
With the water that the gods poured into you, O grasshoppers, in the desert — with that, O god-impelled ones, corrupt this poison.
You are the daughter of the asuras, you are the sister of the gods; born of heaven and earth, you have rendered the poison powerless.
The loosening of bones, the loosening of joints, what has seized the heart and made it ill — drive out entirely the balāsa-disease, that which dwells in the limbs and in the joints.
From the balāsa-afflicted man I drive out the balāsa, as one sheds a lotus; I cut its root-bond like the root of a gourd.
Fly forth from here, O balāsa, like a fine-winged bird from its nest; like a yearling colt freed from its tether, flee away — you killer of heroes.
Swell up, breathe, grow, and spread out; let your phallus grow as the limb grows — with that, arouse the woman.
That by which they fatten the lean, that by which they invigorate the sick — with that, O Brahmaṇaspati, stretch his member like a bowstring on a bow.
I stretch your member, like the bowstring upon a bow; stride forth unflaggingly, like an antelope mounting a female rohit-deer.
O gods, this pigeon that was sent — desiring something, it came here as a messenger of Nirṛti; let us worship it, let us perform an expiation for it. May there be peace for our bipeds and quadrupeds.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
May the sent pigeon be auspicious to us; O gods, may the bird in our house be blameless. May the wise Agni accept our oblation; may the winged arrow turn aside from us.
The winged arrow does not harm us; the fire-kindler makes a foothold at the fire-altar. May there be welfare for our cattle and our men; may the pigeon not injure us here, O gods.
Rejoicing in refreshment, let us drive the cow around, stopping up the stations of misfortune. With the verse drive off the pigeon, driving it away; may the one who dwells with us fly forth, abandoning us, to find strength elsewhere.
I push you away, I drive you forth, O pigeon, along with the rakṣas; we send you to that place from which you will not come back again.
As this draught-animal, O Aśvins, comes together and moves in harmony — so let your mind come together toward me and move in harmony.
I press your mind as a royal horse presses the spine; as grass cut by a sickle, so let your mind be wound around me.
Of the collyrium, of the sweet-smelling herb, of the kuṣṭha plant, and of the nalada — I bring the swift compeller of Fortune with both hands.
Here comes Aryaman from the east, with loosened forelock; may he seek a husband for the unmarried girl, and also a wife for the un-fathered man.
She grew weary, O Aryaman, going to the assembly of others; O Aryaman, surely now another comes to her assembly.
Dhātṛ has upheld the earth; Dhātṛ has upheld the sky and the sun; may Dhātṛ bestow upon this unmarried girl a desirable husband.
The waters sent sweetness to me; the Sun brought me radiant desire; for me the gods and all the heat-born ones — for me the god Savitṛ has established expanse.
I have upheld the earth and the sky; I brought forth the seven rivers together; whatever truth and falsehood I speak — I encompass all speech and all desire.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
I pervade the earth and the sky; I released the seven seasons together; I have come to encompass all speech — I who have enjoyed Agni and Soma as companions.
For our draught-oxen first, for our milch-cows, O Arundhatī — grant shelter to the non-milking one, to the fledgling, to the four-footed.
The plant Arundhatī, together with the gods, grants shelter; may she make the cow-pen rich in milk and the men free from disease.
I invoke the all-formed, the fortunate, the life-giving one; may she carry far away from our cattle the shaft of Rudra.
Yama, Death, the sin-slayer Nirṛti, Bhava, Śarva the archer, the blue-crested one — may these divine beings, who have risen up in battle-array, guard our heroes round about.
With mind, with oblations, with the fire, with ghee — to Śarva the archer and to King Bhava — I make obeisance to those worthy of obeisance; may they lead the evil poisons away from us to elsewhere.
Protect us from the evil poisons, from slaying — O Agni, Soma, and Maruts of pure might; O All-Gods, Maruts, Vaiśvadeva, may we be in the good graces of Vāta and Parjanya.
Let them know together in mind, let them be of one accord in understanding; let them not fight with divine wrath. Let no tumult arise on the great day of conflict; let the striker fall on the day of Indra's arrival.
We bring together your minds, your vows, your intentions; these who are of divided vow — them we cause to know together with you.
The bringing-together of your minds, and also the bringing-together of your hearts — that which is the wearied share of Fortune, with that he brings you into accord.
Let your bodies come together, your minds together, and your skins together; Brahmaṇaspati and Soma bring you into mutual accord.
Accord with our own people, accord with strangers — O Aśvins, you two, bestow accord here upon us.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
As the Ādityas and Vasus came together — fierce Maruts without enmity — so, O three-named one, without enmity, make this people of one mind.
Drive that rival from his dwelling — he who makes war; with the oblation that drives away, O Indra, shatter him completely.
Go to the three distant realms, go beyond the five peoples; go to the seven luminous regions — as far as the Sun is in the sky.
The divine Indra has driven you to the most distant remote region, so that you will not come back for endless years.
For you, O apāmārga plant, have come to be one whose fruit faces backward; ward off all curses from me, warding them farther and farther away.
Whatever a rival curses, whatever a kinsman curses against us, whatever a Brahmin curses out of anger — all that let be under our feet.
She who hates evil, who is god-impelled, the radiant one, the driver-away of curses — she has washed away all curses from me like filth with water.
When they sit around him, when they compose him for inspection — the kindled fire rises up with its tongues from above the heart.
I take hold of the station of Agni, the mighty scorcher, for life; the one who cannot be prevented sees the smoke rising from his mouth.
He who knows this kindling-wood laid together with a kṣatriya — he who does not set his foot in the crooked place, he is for death.
The circling ones do not slay him; he does not sink down among the prostrate — that kṣatriya who, knowing, utters the name of Agni for long life.
Heaven has stood firm, earth has stood firm, this entire world has stood firm. These mountains stand steady; in their steadiness the horses have found rest.
Him who raises up at going forth, who raises up at the final journey, the one who is the guardian of return and of coming back — him too I call upon.
The turnings, the counter-turnings, the return-course, the approach — the four turnings of Agni: with these we satisfy you.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
O Jātavedas, turn him back. Let there be a hundred turnings for you, a thousand counter-turnings for you. With these, turn him back.
Let the one who tears asunder be powerless, O god Soma. Be gracious to us, O Maruts, in this sacrifice. Let not oppression find us, let not ill-omen reach us; let not the hateful misfortune reach us.
Whatever divine stroke today approaches us seeking to slay — you two, O Mitra and Varuṇa, drive it away from us entirely.
Drive away sin from this side and from that side, O Varuṇa. Spread out great shelter; drive away the stroke — wide protection.
Drive away the eastern enemies, O Indra, O Maghavan; push away the western ones, O conqueror. Drive away the northern ones, drive away those who are lower in the south, so that we may rejoice in your wide shelter.
With that oblation of the existent being, let this man be replenished again. The wife that I have found for him — let her grow abundant with vital sap.
Let her grow abundant with offspring, let her grow abundant with dominion. May these two be of thousandfold vigor through the yoke-pole — unwasted.
Tvaṣṭar begot the wife; Tvaṣṭar placed you as husband for her. May Tvaṣṭar make a thousand life-spans, a long life, for you two.
He flies through mid-air, beholding all beings. This is the greatness of the divine dog; for him I pour this oblation.
Your birth is in the waters, your dwelling-place is in heaven, your self is the ocean, your greatness is on the earth. This is the greatness of the divine dog; for him I pour this oblation.
Those three Kālakāñjas who rest in heaven like gods — I call all of them for help, for the unharmed wholeness of this man.
You who cause a man to faint, O divine dog, the killer of menless ones — you I push away with sacred formula. Do not slay this man.
The divine dog who is tawny, iron-toothed, and roaming about — his name I have seized, for the unharmed wholeness of this man: "May he live for us," so saying.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
May this one, the lord of the sky, Saṃsphāna, protect us — unequaled in our homes.
You, lord of the sky, sustain nourishing strength in our homes. Let abundance come, let riches come.
O god Saṃsphāna, you are the lord of thousandfold nourishment. Grant us a share of it; may we partake of your portion; may we be sharers of your portion. Svāhā!
You are a controller, you extend the hand, you drive away the demons. This one has become a wearer of the bracelet, grasping offspring and wealth.
O bracelet, hold the womb wide open for the making of an embryo. Place a son within the boundary; make him come — come!
The bracelet that Aditi wore out of longing for a son — Tvaṣṭar has bound that very one onto her, so that she might bring forth a son.
Come! Of the one who has come, approaching, I seize the name — of Indra the slayer of Vṛtra, the king, the lord of the Vasus, the performer of a hundred deeds.
By the path by which the two Aśvins carried Sāvitrī the daughter of the Sun — by that same path Bhaga has spoken: "Let him bring home a wife."
Your goad, O Indra, the great one of gold, the giver of goods — with it, place for him who desires a wife his wife, O performer of a hundred deeds.
Come to us first, O Intelligence, with cows and horses. You are in the rays of the sun; you are the one worthy of worship for us.
Intelligence, the foremost, full of sacred formulas, praised by seers, drunk deep by those who practice chastity — that intelligence I choose with the help of the gods.
Intelligence in the evening, intelligence in the morning, intelligence around midday — intelligence rising with the sun, we have praised it as it stirs.
In the sap of the earthly one, in the strength of the divine Bhaga's body — Soma has placed life for him, Bṛhaspati has placed brilliance.
Place life for him, O Jātavedas; place offspring and vigor deeply within, O Tvaṣṭar. Press out abundance of riches for him, O Savitṛ. This one of yours shall live a hundred autumns.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
May Āśīr grant us nourishment and fine offspring; let it place skill and wealth of bright luster. Conquering fields by might, O Indra, making rivals lower and subdued.
Savitṛ has come here with the razor, with warm water — come! The Ādityas, the Rudras, the Vasus, of one mind, the wise ones, have shaved for King Soma.
With the razor with which Savitṛ, knowing, shaved for King Soma and for Varuṇa — with that razor the brahmin-priests shave this one of his. Let this hero be untired and long-lived.
Let Aditi shave the beard; let the waters drench him with brilliance. Let Prajāpati hold him again and again for good shaving.
Your arteries and veins that are distributed along your limbs — from all of them together we call forth the poisons out.
The arrow that Rudra has fixed in your limbs and in your heart — that very one today we tear out of you, pointing it away in all directions.
Homage to your face, O Rudra, homage to your arrows that are fitted on the bow. Homage to those that are being released; homage to those aimed at us.
Your hundred veins that flow downward from the head — let them burst open separately, each following that channel of blood.
Let the ones bearing moisture flow along that channel of blood, so that they may not linger inside him — like water flowing in its course.
Let the sun go westward; the streams made to flow go westward. Let this downward-flowing channel from blood cut through the herbs.
This barley they have plowed with eight teams, with six teams. May it indeed strip away the bodily blemish from you, driving it westward.
The wind blows downward; the sun burns downward. The inviolable cow milks downward. Let your blemish go downward.
The waters are indeed healers; the waters are the ones that drive away disease. Let the waters, moving toward the ocean, carry your blemish away.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Those who come to battle having made their banners row by row — Indra has bound them around with a cord; you, O Agni, bind them too.
However many streams come, however many battle-fronts there are — Indra has bound them around with a cord; you, O Agni, bind them too.
Bind together the farthest ones, bind together the nearest ones, and also bind the middle ones together. Indra has bound them around with a cord; you, O Agni, bind them too.
Bṛhaspati has made the binding for you, Savitṛ has made the binding. Indra and Agni have made the binding, Bhaga and the two Aśvins have made the binding.
Your radiances, O divine Sun, spread across the sky as you rise — with all of them, make me radiant today before mankind.
Place me in radiance among the brahmin-priests; place me in radiance among the kings. In radiance among the clan-folk and the Śūdras — place radiance in radiance in me.
The radiances that are in gold, those that are in Agni, and those that are in the Sun — O Indra and Agni, place those radiances in me. Place radiance upon radiance, O Bṛhaspati.
Release me from evil, O sin, being subdued, grant us ease. Place me, unstraying, in auspicious abodes.
That evil which does not abandon me — we abandon it. Be spoken away from us elsewhere, O thousand-eyed immortal.
At the turning of the road we press out one freed from sin. Go to him who hates us; strike down him whom we hate.
You are bound up like a corpse; I have found no enjoyment in you. I split your head, O sin, so that you may not come again.
May Indra guard us by day from the snare of death, for well-being. May Heaven guard us in our midst, may Earth the queen guard us, for well-being.
May the Sun guard us by day from the snare of death, for well-being. May the Wind guard us in our midst; may Day-and-Night guard us, for well-being.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
May Soma guard us by day from the snare of death, for well-being. May the Waters guard us in our midst; may Dissolution not rule over us.
Together be your sight, together your heart, together your mind uniting with mind — through ghee, through the oblation with clarified butter, for this cow whose calf is of the same form.
The charm of union which Kakṣīvān, son of the Aṅgirasas, knew — with that charm the gods have today united you two beloved ones together.
The union-charm of your minds, and the union-charm of your hearts — and what portion of Bhaga is exhausted — with that I unite you two.
I seize your mind with my mind, your eye with my eye. Embrace me thus, so that your mind may be fixed in me.
Let that one turn toward me as the two wheels of a chariot. Let that one wind around me in mind, like a blade of grass severed by a sickle.
I have gone around you with this herb — away from the sorceress, away from the mother, away from the sister; I have gone around you away from other women with this herb.
You who are the assembly-hall of Indra, in whom they sit at council, whose leaves are gold — to you, O Aśvattha tree, homage.
You who fill the atmosphere with branches, downward-rooted, whose leaves are the sacred metres — to you, O Aśvattha tree, homage.
You whom the deer does not reach, nor the bird flying on its wings — you who prop up the entire sky — to you, O Aśvattha tree, homage.
Born under the star Jyeṣṭhaghni, released from Yama's snare — growing up, may you not harm your parents. May your two tigers be gentle and auspicious; may all misfortunes pass over you.
A hero was born on a tiger-day, born of the nakṣatra, full of heroes, well-heroic. Growing up, may he not harm his parents; may the gods accept the oblation for him.
The Rohiṇī stars, wives of the gods, swell like a milk cow — there let the three Vyaṣṭakā festivals speak over all, for offspring and for the living world, for you both.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
When the powerful gods churned fire-drill with fire-drill, person with person in the damp wood — here let that pair of the same womb flourish, a living offspring reaching old age with splendid brilliance.
O Aśvins, smite the locust and the tarda-bird and the mouse; split the head, grind the jaws and teeth. So that they may not devour our grain and rend it — make for us freedom from fear for our grain.
Ho, tarda-bird! Ho, locust! Ho, jabhya and upakvasa! — not eating this grain, not harming it, be driven away!
O lord of tarda-birds, lord of the vagha, O sharp-toothed one — hear us. The oblation unsavored, like a hotr priest's offering, approach with clipped tongues!
O tarda, with the jabhya's lapping tongue — whoever first seeks to satiate himself on this heavenly ambrosia — pierce him face-on at the vital spot with a flame.
Those born from clouds, those born from the wind, those who came into being from the sky — we bind shut the mouths of the sons of Marīci.
The white ones, the green ones, the black ones, and the red ones — under the command of Kabandha, we crush the locusts.
Fly through the atmosphere; do not fall upon the grain. Settle on the ridges of the mountains; eat grass and potsherds, O locusts — that is as your people.
Just as horses harnessed to a yoke draw well — so, urine, burst forth; open and release the mouth of the bladder.
Opened is your bladder's hole, like the ocean's vessel. I split open your urinary passage — the obstruction — as if opening a dam.
Those aged ones, the tongue-lickers, who rise from the ocean — they know the cure of urinary disease and of both urinary organs.
The wrinkles of the head, the wrinkles of the face, the wrinkles from limb to limb, from the mouth — may Indrāṇī wipe away all those wrinkles from the skin.
The wrinkles that were born on the skin, those that came into being around the body — may Indrāṇī attach all those wrinkles onto the branches of the Śamī tree.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
My wrinkle has climbed up the Śamī tree and forsaken me. This one Indra's wife made the receptacle of wrinkles.
Just as the Sun draws to itself the brilliances of the nakṣatras in the sky — so I take to myself the splendor and vital force of my rivals.
Whatever brilliance belongs to my rivals, whatever fame resides among my adversaries — may Indra the slayer of Vṛtra, Dhātā, and Savitā make that shine within me.
Whatever cattle belong to my rivals, whatever wealth lies among my adversaries — having won it as if by conquest in a game, may Savitā make that shine within me.
Truth alone shall conquer, not falsehood; the path of truth shall be straight and good. Speaking truth, let us tend the sacred fire; by truth did Heaven and Earth spread apart.
By the truth of Vāgbhāga, by the benevolence of Rudra, and with Indra pronouncing over it — may we know dominion over the people and the power of speech.
That arrow of yours, O Rudra, which is aimed at speech, or that which is fitted to it — the means by which we quarrel — destroy the injury caused by that.
Destroy the injury caused by that — whether the true or the false — by him who, O Indra slayer of Vṛtra, seeks to conquer us in speech through injury.
Rise up, burst upward, O breath; settle here abundantly, fill this. And let it pour from above as if from the midst of the ocean.
The ocean with a hundred streams, with a thousand streams, inexhaustible — Indra moving from the east, O full cattle-pen, fill this.
Fill here, fill full here; O bull, make the procreative organs active. Here let cows be born, here horses, here men. Let the one with a thousand gifts of honor here settle upon the territory.
To Jyeṣṭhaghni, to the nakṣatras, to day, to night — this homage. I offer to Viśvakarman; may he, being gracious, show us mercy.
May this one not slay the firstborn, O Agni; he strips away the root-destroying one from them. Loosen the snares of the seizure, knowing it; free the father, the son, the mother — release them all.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Release their snares, O Agni — the three that were raised up in threes, by which they were bound. Growing up, may this one not harm the father; may he not harm the mother who bore him.
Loosen the snares of the seizure that bind — her whom the wise ones guard with sacred formulas. O Agni, release their bonds; day after day may well-being follow for the one born of you.
Turn back; do not go away — let the Revatī stars cling to us. O Agni and Soma, O Punarvasu, increase the wealth of this one.
Turn these back again; bring these close again. Let Indra hold these back; let Agni come to them.
I place around you on all sides strength, ghee, and milk. Whatever gods are worthy of sacrifice — may they unite me with riches.
Homage be to the serpents, whoever they are throughout the earth, those in the atmosphere, those in the sky — homage to those serpents.
Those that are yonder in the luminous realm of heaven, those in the rays of the sun, those whose dwelling has been made in the waters — homage to those serpents.
Those that are the arrows of the sorcerers or of the forest-lords, those that lie coiled in pits — homage to those serpents.
With the oblation of barley-remnant may we increase him so that, full of brilliance, he may achieve heroic deeds; in concert with the gods may he overcome his rivals — may undecaying sovereignty and long life be his.
With the virile barley as a milk-rich oblation may the gods protect the life-force of the remnant; for the gods have placed great manly power in him — may Indra bestow vigour upon him.
Together with the oblation of the remnant, together with the hymns of praise, together with life-force and lustre, may he bestow milk; for the gods have placed great manly power in him — may Indra bestow vigour upon him.
May Vāyu assemble them; may Tvaṣṭṛ be established for their flourishing; may Indra speak on their behalf; may Rudra attend to their abundance.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Just as the gods and the asuras did it, just as humans likewise did — so, O Aśvins, produce the auspicious mark for thousandfold prosperity.
With a red knife make a pair of marks on the ears; the Aśvins have made that mark — may it be plentiful through offspring.
The tawny fair-winged ones travel the dark path, clothed in water, they fly up to heaven; and they return from the seat of cosmic order — thereupon the earth spreads open with ghee.
Make these waters and herbs milk-rich, O Maruts with golden breasts, when you stir; and there you swell with strength and goodwill, where, O Maruts, you men pour the sweet drink.
Swollen with water, O Maruts, rouse them with rain when you fill all the valleys; the reed-grass trembles like a maiden struck, stirring like a wife toward her husband.
Like Tvaṣṭṛ, like Pūṣan, the beloved of the home, great good fortune — the two bulls have come to us; rejoicing in good pastures in all directions, be for us the vanguard of this wealth.
Let them come hither, yielding sweetness, free from disease, eager, of all forms; becoming many and multiplying — here may Indra delight you, O cows.
May Prajāpati generate these offspring; may Tvaṣṭṛ, of gracious mind, establish them; may the lord of nourishment, in concert with the seasons throughout the year, place nourishment in me.
You are indeed named the mighty one; you were born from power. Powerful Indra is among the gods — for power we dig you up.
With the powerful divine remedy, the hundred-jointed one, with that thousand-stemmed plant I bring about restoration.
I have seized the name of the powerful divine remedy; the diseases have dispersed away from the man, as if by a blessing.
Let Nirṛti depart; let nothing of her remain here. Away from her bonds of power — the hundred deaths I drive away.
Your hundred snares, O Death, set to slay the mortal — all of them we worship away from you with the power of sacrifice.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Let the hundred deaths that belong to Nirṛti depart from here, away! We drive away their darkness; we establish breath and light.
These three-times-seven repellers — with them Indra spoke to me: 'Let them ward off poison,' he said, 'let them corrupt the poison.'
Speak this out, O Maruts — this counter-spell of great Indra; she is worth a thousand, she wards off poison.
Heaven has stood firm; the earth has stood firm; this entire world has stood firm; the fearlessnesses against poison have stood firm — like a feeble one facing headwinds.
Just as a well-sharpened arrow flies swiftly away — so, O reed-grass, fly away together with the rush of the wind.
Just as the bright eye of one who has sight flies away aflame — [fly away] together with the rays of the sun.
Just as the mind of wrathful intent flies away by leagues — so, O reed-grass, fly away along the outflow of the ocean.
Go away from here, be fierce, be not weak; let all the gods summon you, let all the clans choose you.
With the oblation of the descent we send you off downward; here may Indra make the clans his own, bringing tribute.
Indra, Kaśyapa, then Agni — Iḍā is your fourth companion; with whatever has been, is, and shall be present — with that I send you off.
Disease does not cling to him; the curse does not reach him — whom the fragrant odour of the bdellium remedy reaches.
Whom the fragrant odour of the bdellium remedy reaches — from him diseases scatter in all directions, like deer from an arrow.
What is bdellium, what is Sindhu salt, or what is the sea-herb — I have seized the name of both for his inviolability.
The gods ploughed this barley mixed with honey on the Sarasvatī, on the jewel-field; Indra the hundred-powered was lord of the plough; the Maruts, bountiful givers, were the ploughmen.
O broad-leafed one, auspicious, dreaming upward, rich in truth — be gentle to our hair as a mother to her sons; grant us welfare.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Whatever intoxication of yours causes dishevelled hair, loosened hair, by which you make a man ridiculous — you who move like one who kills an embryo from afar — from that offspring of yours I cause the hair to grow well.
I place the auspicious goddess of intention in the fore; may the mother of thought be easy for us to invoke. Whatever hope I pursue as my sole goal, let it be mine; may I know her as entered into the mind.
O Bṛhaspati, come to us with intention, approach us with intention; then bestow Bhaga upon us, and be easy for us to invoke.
May Bṛhaspati the Āṅgirasa acknowledge my intention and this speech; he of whom the gods became divinities — may Desire with its good guidance follow after us.
Now let us invoke the mind with a hymn of praise to Narāśaṃsa, and with the thoughts of the fathers.
May the mind come back to us again, for will, for discernment, for living — and for long beholding of the sun.
May the fathers, the divine folk, give us back our mind; may we join the living throng.
We, O Soma, in your observance, bearing mind in our bodies — may we join, possessing offspring.
Lustre for me, O Mitra and Varuṇa; lustre, O divine Sarasvatī; both of you Aśvins, garlanded with lotuses, grant lustre to me.
Whatever lustre is placed in the sacrificer, whatever is placed in the sacrifice, whatever lustre is in the tawny sura-drink — of that lustre may I partake.
The streams that flow down from springs, the streams of heaven, from rivers — with the lustre of all those waters I sprinkle you.
When the constellations made Śakadhūma king, they granted him an auspicious day — from that the kingdom was born.
May there be an auspicious day for us in the evening; may there be an auspicious day for us in the morning; O Śakadhūma, always make an auspicious day for us.
You who have made an auspicious day for us in the evening, in the morning, and during the day — to you, O king of constellations Śakadhūma, homage always.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
What they call the Śakadhūma day, the first-born light of the constellations at the fore — may that win for us a honey-sweet gain, and may it grant us wealth with all heroes.
In the post, in the pit, enmity has been made with the radiance of the gods. May fire be between you two, so that you two shall not be together.
As a person hates a serpent, or a serpent hates a person, may a mountain be between you two, so that you two shall not be together.
May your intentions be different, may your thoughts be different. May you two turn away in opposite directions, so that you two shall not be together.
Here are two lotuses, two beaks — do not let them touch that one, O lord of the throat. O destroyer, burn him up.
This thing of yours — whether it was or was not, whether it was yours or not — may it perish from here, just as wealth seen in a dream perishes.
Swallow, swallow, swallow down the unripened one. May the petty, mean thing perish.
For long life, for strength, for my wholeness and freedom from harm — the eagle has declared to me: this is the remedy for what clings.
As the wise ones, purifying meal with a sieve, have fashioned speech — from your limbs, from all your limbs, I cut away that which clings.
Cut away what clings — for the thigh is a healer. The divine eagle has declared: this is the remedy for what clings.
I have come as the overpowering one, as Viśvakarmā, armed with my own weapons. Ordering the affairs of Mitra, I am unconquerable in all these directions.
I am the one who convenes assemblies; I am the high priest of the clans. Ordering my friendships, may steadfast speech be in me.
I take away your sight, I take away your speech, I take away your assembly. Taking away your welfare and security, may I be supreme.
Agni, joined with sacred power, the slayer of demons — may he drive away from here the evil-named enemy who lies upon your body and womb.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The evil-named enemy who lies upon your body and womb — may Agni, the slayer of demons, together with his ally sacred power, drive him away from here.
From the monstrous demons, from the hostile sorcerers — may Agni, the slayer of demons, protect you with his benevolent body from them.
O divine Agni and Savitṛ, bestowing nourishment and vigor — protect me from evil conduct; grant me a share in good conduct. May I attain bliss under your two sheltering graces.
This very thing I approach you two with, this very thing I invoke — what we have heard coming from you. May the Lord of Speech grant it; may my learning abide in me.
Let me not steal from my offspring; may I not fail through what I have learned. O Agni, make our toil fruitful, rich in wealth.
Standing in the middle, brilliant with radiance — made for life and glory. Win favor among the All-Gods; do you win favor with Bṛhaspati.
With ghee one wins offspring; with ghee one attains riches. With ghee one wins from the gods what is life-giving and radiance-bestowing.
O Parjanya, the fig-berries — rivers have poured their embryo into you for well-being. The divine boundary-goddesses of sacred power have poured life-giving radiance.
As a bull elephant follows the footsteps of a cow elephant step by step, so do you, O inviolable cow, follow the footsteps of your calf step by step.
As the two wheels of a chariot scatter the dust of the road, so do I scatter the mind and heart of that one for winning love.
Indra's is the first word; the gods' is the second word; the Aśvins' is the third word — with that we bring the cow into compliance.
Up from here, the two dark, trembling ones have gone aloft like two vultures to the sky — the two scorching ones, the intensely scorching ones, those who burn up this person's heart.
Scorch him through and through; scorch him, ignite and ignite him. O Agni, burn the serpent's venom like grass, along with his confusion.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Sit down, O you two who are thoroughly seated; come back, go to where there is joy. The black cow of Sarasvatī is yours.
As the darkest night, as a black cow with black tracks — as the appearance of those whose cheeks are streaked, so may this head of mine be.
As a charcoal anointed with oil, as a black ladle — may this head of mine be like the dark blemish of his successor.
As a black flame scatters from a burning forest fire — as the face of that Niṣāda, so may this head of mine be.
Whatever that one offers with mind or speech, with sacrifices, with oblations, with sacrificial formulas — may Nirṛti, allied with Death, destroy his oblation before it is seen.
The sorcerers, Nirṛti, and also the demons — let them strike down his truth with falsehood. Sent forth by Indra, let them churn up his oblation; may what that one offers not be fulfilled.
O Agni, we set around you the inspired fort, O mighty one — you of bold color, day after day the slayer of the destroyers.
Two falcons that win the heavenly light, supreme rulers, swooping down together — the oblation of one who fights against us is destroyed, of whoever wages war against us.
Svāhā to the earth, to the forest trees, to the plants, to Agni the overlord.
Svāhā to the atmosphere, to breath, to the birds, to Vāyu the overlord.
Svāhā to the sky, to the eye, to the asterisms, to Sūrya the overlord.
The pippalī plants have spoken together, coming forth from their origin: the man whom we living ones shall reach — he shall not be harmed.
The pippalī — remedy when thrown, and also remedy when pierced — the gods have fashioned her, saying: 'She is indeed sufficient for living.'
The Asuras dug you down; the gods dug you up again. O pippalī, remedy when thrown, you are the healer of one afflicted by wind-sickness.
When the owl hoots — that is futile; when the pigeon makes its mark in the fire — to Yama whose two messengers have been dispatched and have come here, homage be to him, to Death.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Whatever messenger of yours, O Nirṛti, has come — unsent or sent — to our house: let the pigeon and owl be footless in that. You have come here speaking of non-hostile slaying; you have settled here for the sake of good heroism.
He who first settled on the slope, searching out the path for the many — he who rules over this world's bipeds and quadrupeds — to that Yama, homage be, to Death.
As the black one spreads out, following the cow, assuming forms through the Asura's magic — so may this hymn of my vigor, with this my member, make her fully equal to me.
As great as the member of a creature with limbs, of a boar, of an elephant, of a donkey — as great as that of a powerful stallion — may my phallus grow to that size.
As the phallus of a certain one is made large and swollen by the wind — as great as the phallus of a boar — may my phallus grow to that size.
Whose might encompasses dust, comrades, struggle, people, forest, and heaven — the power of Indra is not to be withstood.
The bold strength of the bold one — as of old it stood firm — great is the exhilarating power of Indra.
May he bestow upon us that wealth, abundant, tawny-hued — Indra, the most mighty lord among the peoples.
Bring life-span hither, O Agni, O Jātavedas, master of bodies, so that I may dwell here long as sovereign ruler over my progeny.
May Indra bestow life-span upon me; may the god Bṛhaspati bestow life-span; may all the gods and Day-and-Night create life-span for me.
May the life-giving one purify life-span; may breath bestow breath upon me — that which the gods have fashioned for the gods, going to the heavenly light in due order.
Let the cloud-bearing, roaring waters rise up from the ocean; let the spring waters, the sea-born waters — with those we gratify you.
The waters that are celestial, those that were born around the wind — Indra with the Maruts, of satisfied spirit: with those we gratify you.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The herbs that are dry, those that are green, those that have grown along the earth — all the herbs together: with those we gratify you.
May insight and good-thought of all forms enter into us, bringing mighty hymns; may the many Ṛk verses anoint me like cows, so that we may be listeners in the worlds.
Consecration, ardor, the breath of the mind — Bṛhaspati is the source of this speech; may the Vedas, may knowledge in abundance abide in me. O Agni and Soma, bestow glory upon us.
O Agni, when we gaze upon the heat with ardor — may we be dear to sacred learning, long-lived and of good intelligence.
The disease that overcame you as you were born from your mother or from your father — that wasting illness we drive away from you; let it enter and take refuge in another.
The wasting disease that lodges in your heart, that stands in the navel, that penetrates the belly, and that which clings in the extremities — that wasting illness we drive away from you; let it enter and take refuge in another.
Head-disease, limb-disease, the swelling of the sinews, the evil curse, the spreading eruption — the wasting disease in your marrow, in your joints, in your bowels — that wasting illness we drive away from you; let it enter and take refuge in another.
Agni the demon-slayer, sharp, sharp-horned — let him smite the demon, thrust away the enemy, and shoot away the ill-proclaimer.
Let strength and vigor come to you from the distant realm, from all around heaven; from the hills and mountains, bestowing life-span upon you from all sides.
May the earth give your breath back to you again; may divine heaven, may the atmosphere give it back again; may Soma restore your body again; may Pūṣan restore the path that leads to well-being.
Kaṣkiṣā, Kaṣpiṣā, Yevāṣā — this one here; sandy, dusty particles rushing, eager as desired cows.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The unseen, and also the seen — the seen and the unseen: slay them, O lord of wealth, with the weapon of Indra.
These and those of every form — the vultures and the cuckoos too are slain.
O Desire, desire me; turn toward me, come back to me; may your mind run after me like a calf toward its innocent dam.
O Abhīlā, O Abhimādanī — may that one become intoxicated with me; we know, O flying one, the name-charm of your arrow.
I take your mind to myself, like a mind-stealer stealing the mind; your mind is set in me like a chariot in the chariot-bearer.
That sun has risen together with my fortune; I am the priest of the clans — honey-handed, honey-tongued; may firm speech abide in me.
I become visible among humans with the banner of the clan-chief; may the great one be ours alone over all the directions, over all the kings.
Sweeter than the sweet, more honey-like than honey, dearer than a dear friend's intimacy — O Ādityas, make me so.
O Agni, you are Brahman; know this — speak forth to us. If this shall be so, or if not, then be pleased with this oblation here. Svāhā!
I question Heaven-and-Earth, I question Indra, I question Bṛhaspati; I question the gods worthy of sacrifice — for whom shall I live?
O King Yama, this ladle is raised up for knowledge, this oblation is set forth — be pleased with it. Be gladdened with the oblation for one whose life has not yet departed; let what belongs to the departed go to Nirṛti.
Whatever has sucked you out from the flesh, from the stirred drink, from the cooked food — may Agni, the universal healer, protect you from that sin.
The wind that blows upon you from below and from above — may the waters that bring universal well-being protect you from sin.
Death from you, Nirṛti from you, wasting disease — we press them down away from you, so that you may be free of wounds, full of upward strength, and superior.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
May Vaiśvānara purify us with his rays; may the Wind, the vigorous one, purify us with breath and clouds; may Heaven-and-Earth, rich in milk, keepers of cosmic order, worthy of sacrifice, purify me.
May Prajāpati guard us with the five seasons, may the Year guard us with all its stations; may breath remain here with us in fellowship — I place it back again into the self.
Take hold of the truth-speech belonging to all the gods, being pure, clean, and purifying; praising with it in the communal rejoicings, may we become masters of riches.
Take hold of the splendor belonging to all men, whose spreading forms have backs filled with light. Praising here, rejoicing in the communal festivity, may we long behold the sun rising.
The Avatka plant is my remedy, the Avatka plant is my surrounding incantation; you are of human nature — do not pierce me, being the healer of disease.
Bring the Śambhuleha plant hither — the milk shoots it upward; that is the remedy for the flowing wound, and it has indeed destroyed the disease.
In the rivers, in the reed beds, in pots and in jars — the remedy by sprinkling: that remedy I make for you. Eat flesh, drink water, O Paṭpaṭiṅga, O Vipaścala — look clearly!
We have found what we sought — the oblation that destroys the Piśācas; with it we smite the flesh-eaters and all the she-sorcerers.
The foot-soldiers desire you, the chariot-warriors desire you; they buy you with cows and horses — it is as if you were immortality itself.
The remedy named Amamri, lifted up from the earth — a speaker told that to me: "This alone will carry you across."
You are the eye of man, the eye of the cow, the eye of the horse; you are the eye of what has been and what shall be, the eye of the Apsarases.
You are the eye of the eagle, the eye of the serpent, and also of the dog; you are the eye of all that sees, and of all that stirs in the universe.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
I addressed the thousand-eyed one who seizes and ensnares: "Show me the sorcerers — show me the she-sorcerers."
I have seen beyond this earth, beyond the sky, beyond the sun; beyond all these beings I have seen — the demonesses have been seen through.
Show me the sorcerers, show me the demonesses; show me all those who intend evil — with this in mind I take hold of you, O herb.
Thus you, thousand-eyed one, see forward as you approach; you are the power that devours the sorcerers.
These serpent-like creatures here on the far side, three times seven, shedding their skins — with their shed skin we cover the eyes of the one who lies in wait with evil intent.
Let her go in all directions, cutting, bearing a club as it were; those with evil intent who reappear repeatedly in every direction — may they be unfulfilled.
Away, you lurkers on the path! Let the evildoer flow away like water. Let neither the many be able to overpower, nor the small ones dare to attack.
Go forward, kick with both feet, carry to the house of the generous giver; let Indrāṇī go first — unconquered, unrobbed, along the path.
The Phālguna gem has come here, together with strength and the bestower of strength — that by which Indra cut down the heroes of the Dasyus and the Asuras.
May the gods anoint me with radiance and milk; may both heaven and earth anoint me with radiance; may god Savitā bestow radiance upon me, may the wise sage Kaśyapa bestow radiance upon me.
