May the waters bestow radiance upon me, may the plants bestow radiance upon me; let all beings, coming together, place radiance in my face.
Those that stand spread out in the east, like cows wandering on the road — the long-pepper plants, healers of wind-sickness, carrying one across.
You are the urine of Rudra, the navel of the immortal; you are established as a root in the earth — named Viṣāṇā, healer of wind-sickness.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
May there be well-being for your kidneys, well-being for your liver, well-being for your spleen; may there be well-being for your ribs and marrow, may there be well-being for your body.
For the cruel thing has not reached your body, O Agni, the mortal; let the monkey, the brown one, sharpen its own point — like a cow its calf-membrane.
It roars together and apart like a storm, when the upper one gnaws the lower; crushing head with head, water with water, the brown one with the swift green ones flays the shoots.
The birds of good feather raised their voice upon the heavenly perch; the black, vigorous ones danced; when they lead down the expiation of the lower one, the many have placed their seed — sped by the sun.
With the Śāṃśapa-bhaga, together with the ally Indra, I make myself prosperous — let all enmities flee away.
The one that is blind, the one that flows again — the bhaga established in the trees; may the Śāṃśapa-bhaga be mine — let all enmities flee away.
As you overcame the trees together with the ally Indra, so make me prosperous — let all enmities flee away.
The blue-red one, born from around the Himālayas — the Kīśmīla demon born from the sky upon the plowed fields — I have driven it away.
Born from a cloud, born from the rain, born from around the sky, born from the ocean — the Kīśmīla we destroy.
You who are born from fog, you who are born from dew, you who are born from water — you who are the embryo of lightning, O Kīśmīla, be gracious to us.
These sand grains, brought from around the river, which cannot be counted — with those gathered grains I have driven away Yama's Kīśmīla.
By you, O Vibhīdaka tree, the Asuras were formerly defeated and slain; you who drive away rivals — shake off the enemies.
Let the Vibhīdaka split them apart like a bull with sharp horns; and may it subdue the rivals, and may it strike down those who show malice.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The overpowering one has cut through the rivals, has laid low those who hate me; it has prevailed over them, possessing prosperity on both sides.
The attacker, the counter-attacker, the mouse, the Kakubha-worm, the earthworm — the small creatures, the chirping ones — all of these we crush.
I bind shut the face, the mouth, of the mouse with Muñja grass — so that, unable to eat, it may go away from the plowed fields.
The mouse with bound mouth, thrust away, driven far off and repelled — I break its teeth; we knock out its two eyes.
O Aśvins, lords of the auspicious, anoint me with the honey of the bee, so that I may speak a speech full of radiance among the people.
I am glorious to the one who blinks, I am glorious to the one who beholds in return; I come here as glorious, and I am glorious there too.
To every being here, and to every one who sees — to all of them I am indeed glorious.
Push away, uncover whatever this is or is not; make the sight blind and impaired — do this to the eyes.
Having made the golden limb, the plow-handle, and the cataract — gods, take that away.
May my mind be possessed of sight, may my heart be possessed of sight; may my consciousness be possessed of sight, may my eye be possessed of sight — place sight in my two eyes.
Soma is king, and Savitā is king, Bhava is king, and the world is king; Śarva is king and Śarman is king — may those gods grant us shelter.
Bṛhaspati with the Ādityas, Bhaga together with Soma, the All-Gods, the wide atmosphere — may those gods grant us shelter.
Strike out the un-pierced one and also loosen the taut one; O All-Gods, O Maruts, do not direct your missile at us.
This is the flowing-down of waters, the resting place of the ocean; make our houses face away in the middle of the lake.
On your coming and on your going, may blossoming Dūrvā grass grow; or may a spring arise here, or a lotus-filled lake.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
With the after-birth of snow, O house, we wrap you around; may you be for us a cool lake, may Agni grant the remedy.
This Darbha grass is free of anger, for one's own sake and for wandering; freed of anger it is the calmer of anger — may it be that for you.
This one with many roots goes down to the ocean; the Darbha grass established in the earth — may that be free of anger for you.
We lead away the path of your jaw, the path of your mouth; so that, being under my control and without protest, you may sit up near my mind.
With whatever bonds you are wrapped round and bound, fixed limb upon limb again and again — may they be unraveled for you, for the cut ones exist as cut; O Pūṣan, wiper-away, may he wipe away the sins of the embryo-slayer.
The gods wiped this off upon Trita; Trita wiped it off upon human beings; if it has not gotten away from you at the middle then I remove it from you by the sacred formula.
Enter the heat rays, enter the smoke along the wind, go to the lofty ones, or else to the mist; following the foam of rivers may that vanish away — O Pūṣan, wiper-away, may he wipe away the sins of the embryo-slayer.
O Agni, burn back the demon-brought thing that has been brought in pots; that one will go away unapproachable — this one has become able to live.
Whatever is claw-like, whatever is hoof-like, whatever sprouts, whatever is flower-like — the Urvā fish, the Madhūlaka plant: this one will drink of that, free of flux, free of disease.
The divine waters that flow from the ocean and from around the Himālayas — the waters that bring well-being to all — may those healing ones come here.
O fair one, with skin as thy covering and teeth as thy bedding, O wise one — as one pours abundance around a single cow in the pen, so have I poured radiance around thee.
Like the foremost of geese gazing ahead upon the path before — O tongue, do not tremble, do not falter; speak thou as thou hast spoken before.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Radiant may I rise, before the Brahmin and the Rājanya, before the Śūdra and the Ārya, and before whomsoever we desire, and before every one who sees.
Step forward with both feet turned hither; let thy mind be turned toward me hither. Let thy wrath, which was turned away from thee who now faces me, turn back.
O blessed goat-eating one, there is light here in front, darkness beyond. From this threshing-floor knowledge we turn thee back again hither.
As they gather rice together on the rice-threshing floor with flails, so I gather together thy scattered mind toward me.
Thou art the best of fragrant things, the middlemost of what is carried. By thee the bride exults; that splendour of thine do I take unto myself.
From the crown-born ones of thy crown, O unaged woman who has found her husband — I take the bull's sap from the head.
That sweetness which is in thy limbs and that love which is in thy heart — that we draw out from thee and cause to shine blazing in me.
Be swift as the wind, O steed; being yoked, go at Indra's urging, swift as thought. Let the divine Maruts yoke thee; let Tvaṣṭṛ place swiftness in thy feet.
That swiftness of thine, O steed, stored in the secret place, which moves in the eagle and which moves in the wind — with that, O steed, strong with strength, win the race, able to carry through to the finish.
Upon the seated one's mind, upon the seated one's eye — becoming like the wind of the one who is sitting, win the race, able to carry through to the finish.
Thy body, O steed, bearing thy frame, shall bestow bounty on us, comfort on thee. O unharmed one, the great gods for sustenance would make thee bend down like a heavenly light, like the sun.
May Indra, the Vṛtra-slayer who conquers the obstructer, carry me across unharmed. May he well guide for me the chariot, the charioteer, and the horses.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
May Indra lead me by that path which is fearless and easy to travel. May he carry me across to the right; may I not be harmed in the meeting of combatants.
O heart's delight, bow down around us; make a complete circuit for the body. Ward off the feathered arrow and also the unfeathered one that wounds.
All gods, O Ādityas, honour this oblation. In this sacrifice do not waver; the oblation is made for immortality.
Both the narrow and the wide pit I open with my magic power. Drawing forth the sacred knowledge from both of them, then we perform the ritual acts.
From the vessel out of which we have drawn the Veda, into that same vessel we place it back again. By the might of the Brahman, with what has been offered and accomplished, may the gods protect me here with fervent power.
Vaiśvānara, the universal Agni, has engendered a fresh goodwill for us, growing great with the earth's strength.
O purifying one, O Agni Vaiśvānara, shine brilliantly for us, invoked with the Jamadagnins' oblations.
The great Agni Vaiśvānara shone upon the back of heaven; with his light he drives away the darkness.
The remedy has been brought from the head of the flying deer — that which is as blue-tinged as it is bright-gleaming; and that indeed destroys the hereditary disease.
Anumati approved; the bull's son approved. The ploughmen approved; the cows too approved.
Reverence to the stretching ones, to the fastened garment-cords, and to the heart. Reverence to the lord of the field; reverence to the lady of the field.
I inflame thine inmost heart, touching it over with the hand. O long-haired one, by thy bull-lust let thy testicles not wither like a head.
Let Agni heat thee; let the Sun heat thee; let the Wind yoke thee and the Maruts yoke thee. Let thy mind go after the wild deer, after the mirages.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
I rouse thee up from languishing; I rouse thee up from the house. Do not touch upon sitting idle, O good one; stand up, go forward to the assembly.
Stir up the one who is slow to be stirred, and make her one who carries the torch, for her husband and for her father-in-law.
O Harāṃsayu, destroy utterly together, O seer, the vital essence and the knowledge that flow over the eyebrows.
Together with the rushing of the wind, together with the rays of the Sun, together uplifted with the Sun, we destroy the rival wife.
The long-tongued, loud-voiced ones by whom wet garments arise — the cows, mothers of ghee, have made a remedy in heaven.
The black one, mother by name, has flowed forth — the outgrowth of the bright ones. With the root of the divine sage I cut all those away.
I cut away the first of them; I cut away the middle one as well; and then I cut away the last of them entirely, like a tuft of hair.
Go away, O lord of the mind! Why dost thou proclaim ill-omened things? Depart — I desire thee not; roam among trees and forests.
What we have incurred through ill speech, through base speech, through hostile speech — what while waking, what while sleeping — may Agni place all misdeeds and all that is displeasing far away from us.
Whatever falsehood we practice, O Indra, O Brahmaṇaspati — may Pracetas the Āṅgirasa guard us from those who hate us.
Here make me supreme; overpower the one who makes battle against me. Drive away the sorcery from us; drive away the curses from us.
He who would shake us with his mind, and he who has pressed upon us with evil — the intention of that one, O gods, release the heart's thoughts.
Like a horse at the pole, difficult to yoke, I carry ten as a counter-draught. O Brahmaṇaspati, smite the sorcerer with both thy tusks.
Thou who art born above others, who hast grown up above the crown of the head — O rival-banisher, shake down the adversaries.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
This one is mighty, enraged in conflict, pressed down upon the earth. With that I shall bring him to naught so that he shall go to the place of standing still.
He has come to a standstill, the great one without a domain; the one with cramped limbs falls at the standstill. Whoever is king of that inner standing-place — he shall go to the highest standing.
The king has gone to his abode; the Sun has gone to the sky. Rising, O Vṛtra-slayer, the spleen — the king of limbs, the slayer of men — has gone.
As a bypath merges into the great road, so do thou, O spleen, return to us whence thou hast come attacking.
The strength given by Indra — this from the Āsuras, Śitaṅga and from Śālvata too — to thee: let those two drive away the evil, unpleasing Kaṇvas; then be thou the house-lord of these houses.
Thou, O Agni, art the house-lord of the houses; thou art the begetter and giver of offspring. Do thou thrust away the evil, unpleasing Kaṇvas, always repelled, driven out hence, these sinful ones.
Having bound the cruel thing with hides, cause the fear of the deer. Drive the wild animals forward; destroy the mirages.
If thou art afflicted by Apsaras, if a demon has seized thee — for that I pour for thee an apaplava oblation with my mind.
With a hundred nooses and with a thousand nooses I bind your mind to me, as a fisherman binds a fish with his net.
I have taken your right foot, your heart. I have placed your foot in my lap — I have made you subject to my will.
Like a cow that has been tethered, I cause you to fall at my feet. That wind-charm, that binding-spell — it has been made to draw you in.
I lead your mind as a horse-tether leads a horse. I bind your mind to you as sandals are bound to the feet.
As surā (beer), as honey, as dice drawn to the gaming-board, as the mind of one longing for cattle — so let your mind turn toward me.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
So make me your beloved; place me within your heart; so that, your mind undivided, you will not even speak of other women.
With this vaiṣṭapa oblation placed in the hands of Bhaga, we touch you — for good fortune and for well-being.
O Bhaga, unite me with her! Do not scorch her from behind or from beyond. And with that fortune which is Bhaga's own fortune, unite me with her, O Bhaga!
I unite you with Bhaga as the month unites with surā — so that you may be dear to your husband and favored by your brothers-in-law.
From here rises the divine word, shot like an arrow into the quiver. With it I shall conquer and drive away my rivals.
May Agni with the Vasus protect me from the east; may Savitṛ with the Ādityas protect me from the south; may Indra with the Maruts protect me from the west; may all the gods guard me from the north.
Protect me from the demon-rākṣasas; protect me from the human-rākṣasas; protect me from every rākṣasa.
That mountain yonder, the three-peaked one, which stands firm with its two horns — let it stand holding the swooping-winged, the upward-rushing one, as it holds balāsa disease.
The celestial Suparṇa (eagle) flies down, iron-fanged, iron-beaked. Let it drive away from here the swooping, the upward-rushing wasting disease.
Fly away together, O balāsa, with the jay and the kikidī bird; perish together with the rushing of the wind and with the nihākā.
Do not sing at the śābalī hound, the śauṇeya that draws well. We render homage to you with a good offering. With an undistracted eye — you, O śamakā, let śamayā calm you.
You who disfigure, who diminish beauty — you who devour together with a paramour as husband, guarding the house — O śamakā, let śamayā calm you.
Anoint yourself, smear yourself well — when anointed go to the calming. And seek cows for the ancestors with knowledge and with Bhaga. O śamakā, let śamayā calm you.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Go away, O evil of the mind; step further away! Beyond Nirṛti the eye looks out — the mind of the living is in many places.
They choose the auspicious boon; they yoke the auspicious dakṣiṇā; the eye of Vaivasvata is auspicious — the mind of the living is in many places.
Whatever flaw is in my mind and in my speech — whatever went to Sarasvatī driven by anger of thought — may Bṛhaspati, in accord with all the gods, bind that together again.
Thrive, thrive more greatly — thrive, O receivers! O hundred-handed one, gather in; O thousand-handed one, pour in abundantly.
Pour it in right here, pour it all in right here — let there be thriving in this place. Let this herb be prosperous, like the confluence of the ocean.
The tīrā plants have come up and gathered close; the great tīrā plants have arrived. As rivers after rain bring abundance here — let them bring thriving hither.
Let the pegs spread apart, like donkeys hard to yoke. Let all the threads become confused — the nāḍī tube wrapped around the loom-frame.
Let the shuttles fall forward; let the banks and the winding-spool fall forward. Let all the threads become confused in the blind stretched warp-yarn.
The āyavanī rod, the winding-spool, the pattern-stick, the spool, the shuttles — let all the threads become confused in the blind, stretched warp-yarn.
She who first makes the peacock-pattern — together with the spider and with śakā — the Kṛttikās, wives of the gods, have confused this thread.
Let Agni go first; let Bṛhaspati go before us. And then, O Bhaga, grant us your boon — for you are the giver of wealth.
May the śūdra and the ārya grant us bounty; may the king, even Vṛtrahā (Indra), grant us bounty; and may everything that has a self grant us the dakṣiṇā reward.
O seer, you stretch out the path of the sacrifice, shining upon the back of Ṛta. By which path you carry the oblation, O divine messenger — may the wise one be more glorious from here than from there.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Honey-handed, honey-tongued, honey-complexioned, honey-vowed, and honey-commanding — may Bhaga enrich me with radiance.
She who returns again three times seven, wearing many forms — may Vācaspati place the force of her weapon far away from me.
Driven back by the word from the kṛtyā, endowed with Indra's power, made to stay awake though asleep — driven back by the declaration of the simple one, let it turn back and strike the maker.
Inasmuch as you boast greatly and think 'I am the kṛtyā' — turning back and departing, you shall be slain like poison by poison.
Let the evil-proclaiming one pass beyond; let us not come together with him. May both Heaven and Earth protect us from distress.
O barley, drive away from us all hatreds with the barley oblation. Upon the neck of the one who has worked the kṛtyā with malevolent heart — release it back upon him.
Let one of you assist another; let each help the other. Like horses galloping forward — the plants that slay the kṛtyā, the plants that slay hostility.
Go not near the cattle, do not linger near them; follow the difficult passes of the roads. Let the rival wife perish from here; let her go far away from her home.
Whose name I take up, in whom the resting-and-pouring-in abides — from that far-off distance of the remote one, we cause the rival wife to be destroyed.
Beyond thirty-three mountains and beyond four hills — O Brahmaṇaspati, drive the rival wife away, along with her embryos.
Let the sea-faring Maruts exhilarate upward; let both Heaven and Earth rise up. Let the ocean's floods rush up against you; let this Agni burn you up.
Whatever radiance a rival wife has taken from that woman there — let that one be below as the disparager, while I am above.
I bind onto you this herb that drives away rival wives — so that this man may be your husband and become the father of your sons.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Whatever debts of mine persist in this world — the debts of Yama by whose force I move — of those, O Agni, I become free from debt; of those, O Agni, let this be the clearing.
Your seven downward slopes, and also your three, your downward courses, and those that turn toward us — the three luminous regions on this side, eightfold — may all these, O Agni, be of one mind with you. Knowing this, carry the usury down to Yama.
Your upward bodies, O Jātavedas, those that go crosswise and those that go along — yoked together with them, praised, O Agni — knowing this, carry the usury down to Yama.
Destroy the grey hair of the head; bring back that which is black. O herb, make it grow — render the hair yet blacker.
As is collyrium, so art thou; as is the three-peaked plant, so art thou. From that origin, from that assembly of thine — the dawns that shine forth, one after another.
Where it exists, where it stands, from where let it vanish — the sword-like thing: the divine eagle has declared this to be the remedy for grey hair.
From the vast sky, from the atmosphere, a drop of waters fell upon me for the sake of the sap. Unite me, O Agni, with vital power and with milk, through the sacrifices of the seers and through the deeds of the virtuous.
If that fruit fell from a tree, if it fell from the atmosphere, that too is but the wind. Where the body is untouched, where the garment is untouched — there Dissolution does not reach from beyond.
The ointment is fragrant, and so is the garment; bright is the gold upon it, purified. All the purifying strainers are spread over this one — let him live a hundred autumns; this is thine.
He who shatters the spine, who approaches with licking — all the jāyānya standing afar, and whatever jāyānya has taken refuge in the corners of the sky.
The jāyānya is a bird that flies and enters a man. I know thy name, O jāyānya — the place from which thou art born.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
I know indeed thy name, the place from which thou, O jāyānya, art born. How then couldst thou strike there, if I were to make an oblation?
He who enters the mouth and makes the belly large — the disease that is born here, that jāyānya I have utterly destroyed.
From the ārohā plant my mouth is born; from the ārohā plant are my loins. From the ārohā plant I am wholly born — from the coupling of the bull.
Sweeter than liquor, more pleasing than salt — I am more desirable than the cows.
The great bull with the moist navel held thee back — thee, O wind. To thee, O divine Earth, I give the act of attraction; I take away thy dryness of mouth.
United in mind, united in good seed, let the two of us offer the oblation well to the gods. Let those whose portion this is delight in it. Let the two of us rise up together, undisturbed, with good fortune.
By that light by which the gods rose to heaven, by which the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the Rudras rose, by which the Aṅgirases ascended to the sun — by that let the two sacrificers rise up in well-being.
The odana-rice that Aditi cooked when desiring a son, by which Kaśyapa encompassed offspring — the odana that is cooked for all the gods: let our share in it be inexhaustible at the right time.
The breath of Soma blows from the east; from the south let the wind of Indra blow to us. From that direction which is the mother, which is the west — let that wind be auspicious to us here, O gods.
The breath of Mitra blows from the north; upward from Bṛhaspati let the wind blow. That wind which blows knowing the atmosphere — let that god be auspicious to us here.
He who blows from the north, he who blows from the east, he who blows from the south, and he who blows from the west — he who blows upward in those upper regions: let that god be auspicious to us here.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
O Wind, thou blowest through three atmospheres; thou blowest through three remote distances. O thou of a thousand eyes, slayer of Vṛtra, guard us here; drive away the hereditary disease and blemish.
There no wife has gone in wretchedness, no one weeping and wailing in resistance, no one carrying a burden. Where Indra, the far-striding and discerning one, stands for us — let him grant us that great safety.
Let Indra confuse their army; let the Maruts smite them with might. By the blazing force of Agni and of Wind, scatter them in all directions and destroy them.
Neither heaven nor earth nor Aditi nor the wealth-winning power is theirs. Let Agni take away their sight; let them go back utterly defeated.
O Indra, smash the village of the enemies, the foe who comes against us intending to slay. Just as these are driven away by Indra — so let me turn the settlement with Agni's help.
Driven away by Indra, let them make their yoke go crooked; let them go by paths turned away, suffering harm. Conquering them, let us settle upon that, turning the settlement with Agni.
The village of the enemies, attacked and driven away by Indra — Agni splits it open. Let these warriors be worthy of praise, those for whom I proceed with oblation and clarified butter.
Aryaman, the auspicious god whom the maiden worshipped — let that god, the slayer of Vṛtra, release her from here and from that place.
O King Varuṇa, this kinswoman makes offering to thee. Bring to her a husband who is truly good and desirable.
O Lord of wealth, make him cry out with longing; make the suitor single-minded. Make everything turn to the right; bring her a husband who is desirable.
From the west and from the east, from the north and from below as well — full is the track of Bhaga; by it we turn this woman toward him, with glory and with good fortune.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
There is no blood of the moth, of the woodpecker, or of the gnats; there is no collision of flight, no upward effort — the disease will be downcast and gone from here.
It slunk away footless; footless it departed; puffing with its snout it departed. The evil-cooker too has departed from here. The disease, once gone, will perish; piercing and swelling will likewise perish.
Just as the sun, rising, conceals the moon — so do thou, O mighty herb, conceal and drive this disease away from here.
It slunk away footless; footless it departed; puffing with its snout it departed. The evil-cooker too has departed from here. The disease, once gone, will perish; piercing and swelling will likewise perish.
Not on stone, not on what has stone, let not even a sliver of stone remain for thee. As much stone as there is of thy stone — so much is the residue of stone that is thine.
Just as water poured out from the top of the sacrificial post reaches the ground — so do thou, O sapless stone, having been poured out, reach the ground.
Thou art the thunderbolt, the slayer of rivals — with thee today I would overcome Vṛtra. Thee, O Lord of the forest, chief of trees, today we lift up for long life.
Thou, Indra, as our foremost priest, guard us from the demon on all sides. The cows have lowed in accord — in accord with the glory, O Bṛhaspati.
O Breath, protect breath; be gracious to the living soul for the sake of the breath of life. O Nirṛti, by thy dissolution, release us from the bonds.
O Hatsuka, bow around us; make a girding for our bodies. Keep away the arrow that carries leaf, and likewise the leafless one that wounds.
Let Prajāpati unite thee with offspring, with a son, with good fortune. Let destiny guide thee here; the desire of the brahmin impels — place a male within her by the impulsion of Savitṛ.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Let the boy creep forth from thee, from the curve, from above a man. According to the season, above the seasonable one — him whom Dhātṛ fashioned for thee.
Whom Dhātṛ fashioned for thee, whom Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned for thee, whom the brahmin power fashioned for thee — find that son; for his sake live thou to live.
The brilliant ones stand smeared with dust, the hotrī-priests of the sacrifice dripping with the stones. Whatever of Soma they pour down here — that is the form of the sacrificer yonder.
Those who, having abandoned the luster of the brahmin, clothe him with dust and dirt as his color — whatever of Soma they pour down here, that is the form of the sacrificer yonder.
Just as a well-appointed chariot without a charioteer, abandoning its left yoke-horse, goes on the course of demons — so the sacrifice forsakes the sacrificer when they lead the Soma-rite to those who drink Soma improperly.
The Vedic meters go away from the sacrificer when they lead the Soma-rite to those who drink Soma improperly. When a non-brahmin drinks the Soma — that is indeed a breach, to be covered over with the sacrificial fee.
Thou art the ruddy one, the swift one, the all-encompassing drink, first brought around for the gods. May the digger suffer no harm — nor he for whom we dig thee.
O gods, let us not reach evil; do not lead us by the path of evil. May I not wound the hand of my companion in my desire for wealth.
O gods, do not give me over; do not make me sick. May I not wound the head of my companion; may I not err.
My face is discerning, my eyes are sweet-glancing; through both my ears flows abundant hearing.
My tongue pours forth sweetness, my tongue speaks sweetly; with that tongue of mine today may I utter honeyed speech.
As the honey-makers gather honey upon honey, so today with metres may I utter honeyed speech.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Purified by the purifying filter of Vāyu, Soma is set in place face to face; he is the yokemate and friend of Indra.
Whatever transgression, O Varuṇa, mortals commit against the divine folk — if we have overstepped your ordinances in any way, do not injure us, O god, for that sin.
May the Waters as mothers refresh us; may the clarifying-with-ghee ones purify us with ghee. For the divine Waters carry away all defilement; I come forth pure and cleansed from them.
Both Mitra the sovereign and Varuṇa the king — may they share your portion at the morning pressing, O Agni. I too make my portion after theirs; O Bhaga, enter me endowed with solar splendour.
Enter us endowed with solar splendour, O all-knowing lord of the mind. Soma, ever-wakeful and blameless, and Indra, gladdened and praised by men.
May we, O Indra, share in your delight, in the brightness and radiance of the gleaming, thousand-fold glorious one — offspring and refreshment.
May Agni Vaiśvānara, maker of the path, lord of all peoples, guard us at the morning pressing; may that purifier establish wealth for us. May we be long-lived and share the portion together.
May all the gods, the Maruts, and Indra not forsake us at this second pressing. Speaking what is dear to them and long-lived, may we be in the good favour of the gods.
This third pressing of the seers, with which through cosmic order they set the cup in motion — the sons of Sudhanvan, having attained immortality, lead us toward well-offered sacrifice and better things.
May the rivers flow together, the winds blow together, the birds fly together. Strengthen this sacrifice, O praises; I offer with the jointly-flowing oblation.
Guard this sacrifice, O oblations, and also O confluent streams, guard this sacrifice. Strengthen this sacrifice, O praises; I offer with the jointly-flowing oblation.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Taking hold of every form and every age, I embrace it on all sides. May the four quarters strengthen this sacrifice; I offer with the jointly-flowing oblation.
The pot sewn together with the immortal gods has come to us; having placed the sister-pot upon me it stood firm. Truly the former seers, having lamented, may they fully extend the life of the lord of the sacrifice.
We have made the flowing pot free of disease — Tvaṣṭṛ, Vāyu, Earth, and Atmosphere. Whatever drips from it and is offered into the fire — let that be; misfortune shall not reach that from beyond.
This drop has dripped into the fire; misfortune shall not blow it away from beyond. Waxing strong through the oblation of Viśvāvasu, may this sacrifice go to the world of the well-doers.
You are the eagle of the Gāyatrī metre; I take hold of you after; carry me across to safety.
You are the sovereign of the Triṣṭubh metre; I take hold of you after; carry me across to safety.
You are the high note, you are the melody of the Jagatī metre; I take hold of you after; carry me across to safety.
O Trāyamāṇā, hand me over to the all-knowing one. O all-knowing one, protect all our bipeds and quadrupeds and whatever is ours.
O all-knowing one, hand me over to the all-seeing one. O all-seeing one, protect all our bipeds and quadrupeds and whatever is ours.
O all-seeing one, hand me over to the auspicious one. O auspicious one, protect all our bipeds and quadrupeds and whatever is ours.
O auspicious one, hand me over to Trāyamāṇā. O Trāyamāṇā, protect all our bipeds and quadrupeds and whatever is ours.
Dig out, break apart, destroy — move here freely without harm being done. Let me be united with life-span; let life-span be united with me.
Dig out, break apart, destroy — move here freely without harm being done. Let me be united with brilliance; let brilliance be united with me.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Dig out, break apart, destroy — move here freely without harm being done. Let me be united with radiant energy; let radiant energy be united with me.
Dig out, break apart, destroy — move here freely without harm being done. Let me be united with offspring; let offspring be united with me.
Dig out, break apart, destroy — move here freely without harm being done. Let me be united with cattle; let cattle be united with me.
You are the seed of heaven, the navel of earth. You are the navel; make me the navel.
You are the seed of heaven, the power of earth. You are power; let the act be done for your power.
You are the seed of heaven, the wealth of earth. You are wealth; let the act be done for your wealth.
You are the seed of heaven, the nourishment of earth. You are nourishment; let the act be done for your nourishment.
You are the seed of heaven, the prosperity of earth. You are prosperity; let the act be done for your prosperity. You are prosperity, you are what has come to be; may I become fully prosperous.
You are the bright one, you are the resplendent one. Just as you are resplendent with resplendence, so may I shine with resplendence.
Evening after evening Agni is the lord of our house; morning after morning the giver of benevolence. O wealth-treasury, be rich upon rich; kindling you, may we nourish the body.
Morning after morning Agni is the lord of our house; evening after evening the giver of benevolence. O wealth-treasury, be rich upon rich; kindling you, may we prosper a hundred winters.
He who openly curses us, he who steals — and a rival who acts with intentional wrath — may divine Agni release those bonds; may Varuṇa, firm in his ordinances, drive curses away.
Send forth speech to Agni, the bull of the settlements; may he carry us across beyond our enemies.
He who shines through all things from a far, far distance — may he carry us across beyond our enemies.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Agni who crushes the demons with his bright flame — may he carry us across beyond our enemies.
He who looks out over all the worlds and sees them together — may he carry us across beyond our enemies.
The winds blow sweet to the righteous one; the rivers pour forth sweetness; may the cows be sweet-giving for us.
The night is sweet, and so too the dawns; sweet is the earthly atmosphere; may the plants be sweet for us.
May the lord of the forest be sweet for us; may the sun be sweet; may heaven, our father, be sweet.
For you, O Waters, are the sources of well-being — grant us strength for great joy and seeing.
Of that most auspicious essence of yours, grant us a share here, like eager mothers.
For that we are ready for you, for whose dwelling you invigorate; O Waters, regenerate us too.
This speckled cow has stepped forward and sat down again upon the mother; and at the dawning she meets the father.
From its in-breath comes the out-breath; the luminous one moves within; the great bull has revealed the sky.
Thirty realms shine out; Speech has clung to the bird; it responds at each dwelling, day after day with its brilliances.
When the mighty ones mounted upon Speech, seeking to win the atmosphere, the bull-gods made themselves glad together.
Standing upon Speech, the mighty one has released wide-ranging speech; the great bulls made themselves glad in the sky.
The mighty one has released Speech; it shines out maintaining the abodes. The barhis grass of Vimada has spread forth.
You are firm, you are a support, unassailed, well-held by Viśvakarman. May the ocean not uproot you; may the eagle not—unshaken one, strengthen this.
You are unconquered, you are overpowering; overpower the enemy, overpower the one who marshals troops. You are of a thousand-fold heroic strength—with that, quicken this one.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
You came into being from the waters and from the essence of the earth; you arose above Viśvakarman. Tvaṣṭṛ proceeds, assigning your form; knowing that divine origin of yours, he was first.
Sixty and ninety snares are spread between the Adhvaryu-priest and Agni the Hotṛ. They ensnare the simple man; the wise one passes beyond, and follows the path of cosmic order.
The Adhvaryu who, knowing the seven priestly offices, sacrifices in precedence of the Hotṛ and kindles the fire—he elevates the sacrifice and makes the offering non-violent; he who understands the distribution of the oblation.
Here, O distributor, in the distribution of the oblation, let him not exclude the one entitled to a share, let him not harm him. Let not one known as shareless be deluded.
May the wind blow the healing herb, the auspicious and bliss-bringing one, to our heart. May it carry our life-spans across to safety.
O Wind, you are our father, you are our brother, and you are our friend. Make us to live.
Whatever healing remedy is stored in secret in your house up there, O Wind—give us of that to live.
O Dream, you are neither living nor dead among the gods; you carry immortality within you. Varuṇānī is your mother, Yama is your father.
As they settle a fraction, as they settle a hoof-debt, as they settle a debt—so do we today settle all evil dreaming into the inauspicious one.
You are called Araru—thus do we know you, O Dream. O Dream, establish good dreaming for us.
The gods do not eat the oblation of this one before all others; he is excluded from the world of the well-doers. He himself has cultivated an evil mind—for he is a malefactor dwelling among humans.
He who has slain his mother, slain his father, slain his sister, and those other evildoers—their defilement was wiped off on the two prescribed ones, as men wipe off filth.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
This very one the gods drove out—the slayer of the embryo reaches that world. Not for your ritual act with oblation does one who is implored receive a kingdom; these mighty ones sever the snare.
That serpent which glides here as the ākhū, as the vyūkha, making a rustling sound—against it you are the encircling medicine, the crusher of scorpions.
The peacock eats the scorpion; we eat the peacock. Against it you are the encircling medicine, the crusher of scorpions.
The waters are indeed the healers; the waters drive away disease. The waters are the healer of everything; the waters crush the scorpion.
You, O Agni, are the guardian of vows, O god, both among the immortals and among mortals. You are to be praised at the sacrifices.
Whatever vows of yours we have transgressed, O gods—we who know less than those who know—may Agni, the all-knowing one who has entered into the Soma and the Brāhmaṇas, make that whole again.
We have come upon the path of the gods; whatever we are able to convey along it—may Agni the all-knowing one sacrifice; he alone is the Hotṛ; he conducts the offering and appoints the seasonal rites.
Rouse up the possessive woman, drive her away like one with a bad dwelling, like one with a bad foot. Fly her mind away from the everlasting seasons.
Make her fly away like cooked meat before a sword, like a bird in flight. Make the deer fly away in pursuit; destroy her mirage-desires.
Turn the two cows in opposite directions; turn the two yoked ones in opposite directions. May yonder sun on high turn the two of you asunder in opposite directions.
Violent is the poison, firm is the poison, great is the greatness of the poison. The poison made the enemy's head fly apart into a hundred pieces.
Burn them together as a cattle-pen, as the earth rolls forth its wealth. Whomever you creep into, O poison, burn him up as fire does.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Seize hold of the flesh, shake off the body-hairs. Sow dust into the vertebrae; cut them apart; torment the one who lies with feet upward.
I am sweeter than honey, sweeter than the honey-pourer, more full of sweetness. Honey in my mouth indeed—a sweet abode has been made there.
You gaze upon me alone, like a deer thirsting for water. Speak up to me from beneath my feet, like a frog from a cow's hoof-print.
Speak up to me from beneath my feet, like a frog from a cow's hoof-print. And then, to sit and wait yonder—like a bound dog that has been struck.
Proclaim a plentiful cow-pen, rich in good heroes, rich in many men—so that from here they may not perish. Thus proclaim my cow-pen.
Proclaim, O lord of the daughter; proclaim, O brother-in-law. The buttocks of those without heroes have risen up behind you—slay the kiṣkindhā folk.
When the owl calls out, that is futile; when the dove makes a step in the fire—to that Yama who has listened with attentive ears, the poet, the praiseworthy one, let there be homage today.
The snares that belong to Indra and those that belong to Varuṇa—may the goddess Nirṛti place them far from us.
The snares that belong to Vaiśvānara and those that belong to the Maruts—may the goddess Nirṛti place them far from us.
The snares that belong to the Viśvedevas and those that belong to Viśvakarman—may the goddess Nirṛti place them far from us.
Among Nārada, the gambler, Varuṇa, and Soma, they sought the great majesty. Viśvakarman found it in the ocean; I place the weeping of dice into this one.
Whatever mind has entered into your hands and into your eyes—with a springing motion, with the weeping-curse I make that weep in his joints.
Three divine Apsarases—one by one, each alone, each going on the path of the departed—the name of one of them is told. May the Apsarases, enjoying the clarified butter, go forth together mightily—svāhā.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
I have overcome you with the mind; I have overcome you with the heart. I have overcome you with all my limbs—for thus the abandonment-spell has been performed.
You women who rejoice to greet the man who pursues you—all of you, gather together and declare: in the sharpening-rite, the abandonment has been performed.
Heaven and Earth have established abandonment for me; the god Savitṛ and Bṛhaspati have established abandonment. And Agni and Sūrya—in the sharpening-rite, the abandonment has been performed for you.
From the sky, from the earth, from the wind, from the rivers—Indra brought the saṃskanda plant together. It came here; it has come to this place.
Saṃskanda-strength, with its strength—the name has been assigned to you by the gods. Your name is golden-name; you are the Saṃskanda herb.
The ocean is united with the rivers; both heaven and earth are united. Wife and husband are united in the womb—you are the Saṃskanda herb.
We breathe together the skull-plates of your head, we breathe together the womb, the two saṃgavinī veins. We breathe all your limbs together—we breathe them together through the Skanda-herb.
O Dhātṛ, establish splendor in me; through splendor make me a lord. May Indra, the bountiful one who rules over the people, lead me with fame.
May that great Indra-power reside in me, and skill and resolve in me. May the hot-milk vessel shine forth three times in me; may I win the milk of it—of the Gāyatrī meter, of the Virāj-light.
The two who dwell in the Arka plant's abode, the two poets Mātariśvan—Yama and the Aṅgirases: may the gods make me glorious, possessed of fame—svāhā.
We merchants call upon Indra; may he come before us as our knowing protector. Slaying the grudging foe who lurks along the path like a beast, may he who is sovereign be the giver of wealth to me.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
May our trading thrive, our selling, and our resale; may the counter-trade make us wealthy. May the gods, rejoicing together, accept the oblation; may our going forth and our return be auspicious.
When I go about trading and counter-trading, seeking wealth through my own means, O gods — may Indra, Bṛhaspati, Savitā, Soma, and Agni place brilliance in that enterprise for me.
The many god-traveled paths of yours that pass along heaven and earth — upon those I place myself in radiance, so that having purchased goods I may carry wealth home.
The nooses of Nirṛti that have been fastened to the tattered garment — from those the one who wears armor is freed, as he approaches, laying the joint-evil to rest.
That is truly no garment in which they pierce a man; the form is smeared together with blood. Therefore that must be stripped off.
Rising up, the unknowing one became disliked, one who was to share in much. He does not attain a good path, he who travels along with that one.
This, to be received by a brahmin — through it he makes that auspicious. Through it the giver is freed from the noose of the arka plant and sees clearly.
Those two teeth, like two descended tigers pointing downward, that seek to devour both the father and the mother — those two teeth, O Bṛhaspati, O Jātavedas, make auspicious here through the sacred word.
Eat the rice, eat the barley, eat the black beans, and also the sesame. That is your portion laid out as the holding of a jewel — harm not the father and the mother.
Non-fierce, yoked together, in agreement, gentle — be these teeth of good omen. Harm not the father and the mother; let what is terrible in your nature be elsewhere.
By this let Indra and Agni be yoked, together with King Soma the ally. May Indra, attended by the Maruts, make the seizure against my enemies for me.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
I have performed this seizure, sharpened by Indra through austerity. Wherever my enemies are, those who hate me — I seize them.
With seizing and with binding we crush the enemies. Their out-breaths and their in-breaths — their vital forces one by one I have cut off.
Svāhā to the swift-rushing one, the one accompanied by Maruts!
Svāhā to the victory-hero, the one who overwhelms his foes!
Svāhā to Bṛhaspati, who has all the gods with him!
Heaven stirs forth, earth stirs forth, the mid-space stirs forth, each into its own realm. Forward — the oceanic waters have shaken the thorn loose.
May the wind shake you forth, may the earth with its might. Forward — the oceanic waters have shaken the thorn loose.
May the sun shake you forth, together with the nourishing lunar mansions. Forward — the oceanic waters have shaken the thorn loose.
The amulet pautudruva that has come to me, the universal medicine — may it strike away from us all evil dreaming and whatever darkness there is.
Away from us all evil dreaming, and away the evil omen. Now, O amulet, make me always golden-splendored.
Always let me be one possessed of fortune, full of vigor, capable of enduring all. The pautudruva amulet that has mounted me together with wealth, has mounted together with Indra.
A male horse, wealth, property; a male golden ornament — O herb, place a male son in this woman.
Just as when a male is born there is rejoicing and no one says a word against it — in just that way, O herb, place a son in this woman.
You, O herb, are purchased with a horse, with an antelope, with a cow. A white horse is your wealth, gold and greenery are yours. Given by King Soma, be here an agent of male offspring.
Whatever manly strength, wealth, sacred lore, and whatever learning and jewel I bear — may the guardian of the deposit protect this here for us while I go traversing the womens' way beyond.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Whatever manly strength, wealth, sacred knowledge, and whatever bold fires belong to me — may Hariścandra protect that here for us while I go beyond, having traveled through the village.
Here I go, having traveled beyond the village, toward manly strength, wealth, and sacred lore. Whatever is pure here in you — this I take to myself.
For indeed the Sun yoked first the thousand dappled ones for slaying the dasyu, O powerful and bounteous one; subduing the dāsa color for the Ārya, yoking the two arms and the vajra, O much-invoked one.
Come swiftly for the slaying of the dasyu; O Indra, shatter their strong joints. Being fierce of purpose and faith, those who are unyoked — smash many of them together with the stroke.
For now they have seen Indra, of bright purifying might, many falling together like arrows. Those who battle against our bold and bounteous one — fearlessly the wise ones have turned against them.
To the current year, to the passing year, to the full year — we make known this. Whatever wrongdoing we have fallen into in our vows, by that fault of evil-heartedness we have become besmirched.
O lord of vows, whatever vow of mine has gone astray — may day and night together settle this for me. May the moon, rising in the east, be the healer; may the sun with his rays approve this.
Whatever vow I have transgressed by thought, by mind, by heart — may the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus kindle that aright in me.
I bring the vows to Agni, the lord of vows. May he make for me great brilliance, vast fame, and long life.
May the well-being-bringing wind blow upon us; may the radiant, vigor-bearing herbs come nigh. O Rudra, grant bliss to the footed creature — the fat-filled, life-giving, well-being-bringing ones — for his refuge.
Those cows of one form, of all forms, of equal form — those whose birth and udder Agni knows — those that the Aṅgirasas made here for austerity: to them may Parjanya extend great shelter.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Those cows that have spread their bodies among the gods, whose forms and names Soma knows — may those, swelling in numbers, rich in offspring, be pointed out for us, O Indra, in the cowpen.
Prajāpati, delighting in me, has driven many true ones here into my cowpen. May we dwell together with their offspring, living long through many autumns.
Mounted and churning about is the tawny one, the much-churner. The grain-smut was born from the straw-chaff, from rice, from black beans, and also from barley.
Just as the rump of the straw-chaff does not come together in the grain-smut — in just that way, O plow-attendant, drive the grain-smut out from the villages, drive it out to the directions.
Just as a donkey, of contracted appearance, breaks wind at its neighbor — in just that way let your rump fart, O straw-chaff leaf; O Vṛtra-slayer, O Śāki, make it fart.
Pointed like a spike, pleasant, thirsty for Soma — the plow draws up the fat cow, the ewe, the spirited mare, and the draft animal of the chariot.
Draw taut the harness for good fortune; brandish the goad for good fortune. Strike the right side of the yoked draft animal with the goad for good fortune.
Hold down the honey-sweet plowshare in the fields at all times; may Parjanya rain upon it for abundance, to make the grain.
These very ones were seen coming toward the vedi. Agni sent forward the offering to the gods; the sacred formula is the hotr, the lord of oblations.
These well-being-bringing ones have come, bearing udders full of sweetness. Learn from those that are milking inexhaustible milk.
You are the iḍā offerings, honey-mixed, of all forms — enter me, together with breath, with radiance, with ardor, with strength.
The bright cloud of the sky, milking out its waters — it is the navel of cosmic order (ṛta), and it reveals the immortal nectar.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Milking out clarified butter drunk in from all sides, milking out nourishing strength unceasingly — may the pious worship her with their offerings.
Seek the ghee in this swelling womb; approach it! Those libations you have made while living — may they drip with sweetness for you.
May the essences of plants and their powers bow together toward me. I have followed the hand of the earth, full of strength and full of sap.
You are the guide of the path of the hand; you are the guide. Thus do we lead away all evil dreams around the post.
May my field be rich in sap; may my grain too be rich in sap. My agriculture shall be full of sap — may I myself be full of sap.
I bring a white offering to Agni the powerful, the mighty, the finder of the heavenly light, the radiant one. May he make us firm and strong, and grant that we live long.
I know your name, O Agni — you are named through the waters; you are the triple-shielded one. May the threefold nourishment, the threefold sacrifice, attend us.
Growing strong on the milk of Prajāpati, long-lived and radiant with splendor — may we who live long sit down near you.
Those two wide-nostriled, life-consuming, ficus-dark messengers of Yama who roam among men — I know them; the sun knows them. What are these two? What will they do?
No deceiver has beguiled me; I am not to be overcome by the deceitful; I am not naive by birth, nor a disciple still learning. I am the conqueror, the all-conqueror, the vanquisher of armies, the knower of heaven — I am all this universe of beings.
He has stood up, he has risen, the inspired sage was born; he measured out the breadth of the earth. He took his seat as sovereign over all the worlds; he knows by insight the ordinances of Varuṇa.
Prajāpati is rich in offspring; he is rich in offspring — may he make me rich in offspring.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The sun is full of radiant splendor; he is full of splendor — may he make me full of splendor.
Soma is full of milky sap; he is full of sap — may he make me full of sap.
Thirty testicles has the kābava plant; ten testicles the owl-plant has. Four are yours, O muddy one.
O fierce-shining one, cut them off at the root! You are demonic by birth — we drive that away from here.
You are born of Indra, born of Soma — we send that away from here. O wide fish of sweet waters, you guard its passage — free from discharge, free from disease.
You are swift and you are nimble. You are the kindling-wood of Prajāpati, hairy in name, called Saṃsiti. Prajāpati, desiring to become established through you, rose up and became established. Just as Prajāpati, desiring to become established through you, became established, even so may I, desiring to become established through you, become established. May good fortune come to me; may the students of sacred knowledge come to me. Svāhā!
You are prosperity and you are firm establishment. [Prajāpati, desiring to become established through you, rose up and became established. Just as Prajāpati desiring to become established through you became established, even so may I become established. May good fortune come to me; may the students of sacred knowledge] come to me. Svāhā!
You are sleeplessness and you are restlessness. [Prajāpati... may the students of sacred knowledge] come to me. Svāhā!
You are brilliance and you are a wondrous being. [Prajāpati... may the students of sacred knowledge] come to me. Svāhā!
You are fame and you are glory. [Prajāpati... may the students of sacred knowledge] come to me. Svāhā!
You are water and you are greatness. [Prajāpati... may the students of sacred knowledge] come to me. Svāhā!
You are food and you are the eating of food. [Prajāpati... may the students of sacred knowledge] come to me. Svāhā!

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
You are the one that proffers and the one that bestows freely. [Prajāpati... may the students of sacred knowledge] come to me. Svāhā!
You are the fulfiller of desires and the milker of desires. [Prajāpati... may the students of sacred knowledge] come to me. Svāhā!
You are the one that brings and the one that gathers together. [Prajāpati... may the students of sacred knowledge] come to me. Svāhā!
You are the one that points the way and the one that points it forth. [Prajāpati... may the students of sacred knowledge] come to me. Svāhā!
You are approval and you are the one who grants approval. [Prajāpati... may the students of sacred knowledge] come to me. Svāhā!
You are conquest and you are victory. [Prajāpati... may the students of sacred knowledge] come to me. Svāhā!
You are complete conquest and you are what is won by joining together. [Prajāpati... may the students of sacred knowledge] come to me. Svāhā!
Agni is the lord of the earth; may Soma protect you. We know you; know us. You are the overlord — make me the overlord of cattle, horses, men, students of sacred knowledge, of prosperity and the eating of food.
Vāyu is the lord of the atmosphere; [may Soma protect you. We know you; know us. You are the overlord — make me the overlord of cattle, horses, men, students of sacred knowledge, of prosperity and the eating] of food.
The sun is the lord of the sky; may Soma protect you. We know you; know us. You are the overlord — make me the overlord of cattle, horses, men, students of sacred knowledge, of prosperity and the eating of food.
O Vasu who finds — may the Vasus find for me: houses, progeny, cattle, wealth, prosperity, and firm establishment.
O Vasu who brings hither — may there come to me: houses, progeny, cattle, wealth, prosperity, and firm establishment.
O Vasus who unite — may there come together to me: houses, progeny, cattle, wealth, prosperity, and firm establishment.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
You are conquest — may I conquer; may I conquer the earthly armies.
You are victory — may I be victorious; may I conquer the human armies.
You are complete conquest — may I conquer completely; may I conquer all armies.
Awaken him, fully awaken him; do not think him fit for sleeping. Let him stand upright, thinking only of me — let him not even mention other women.
Turn him toward me, turn him back, bring him around fully — do this. With the god of love, we conquer all his thoughts.
The Maruts heat up love-longing in the kindled Jātavedas. May his mind fly upward and come to rest in me.
O lord of the troop, make me lord of the troop; do not take me away from it like barley.
O one who is joined to the troop, join me to the troop; do not cut me off from it.
O one who has a troop, make me one who has a troop; may I not be lost from it.
O increaser of the troop, increase my troop of cattle, horses, men, students of sacred knowledge, of prosperity and the eating of food.
O abundant increaser of the troop, increase my troop abundantly — [cattle, horses, men, students of sacred knowledge, of prosperity and the eating] of food.
O great increaser of the troop, greatly increase my troop of cattle, horses, men, students of sacred knowledge, of prosperity and the eating of food.
Whatever poison is dug up and whatever is not dug up — all that poison is rendered tasteless.
Whatever poison is ground up and whatever is not ground up — all that poison is rendered tasteless.
Whatever poison is smeared on and whatever is not smeared on — all that poison is rendered tasteless.
As a she-wolf whose cubs have been devoured, or a tigress, would become frenzied with distress — even so become frenzied, sent by my anxious longing.
As the blazing tuft of autumn grass would be set wildly afire — even so become wildly agitated, sent by my anxious longing.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Cause him to cry out, become frenzied; wither with desire for me. Sent by my anxious longing.
In whose two powers all this universe is fixed — the existent and the moving, the blinking and the stirring — let those two seize the speaker here as witness; may he not sleep wrongly in this place, O Prajāpati.
Whoever would rob me as I speak — with heart, with speech, with speech, with ear, with mind — let divine Indra, Varuṇa, Bṛhaspati, the lordly god, come upon him, and Death, so that he may not live to see the third dawn.
Whoever would rob me, thinking himself learned in sacred lore, though I am thus the knower, the Pramati among thinkers — let divine Indra, Varuṇa, Bṛhaspati, the lordly god, come upon him, and Death, so that he may not live to see the third dawn.
I lay back his very breath upon him with a blow turned inward — do not give recognition to the one who would rob me. Let him cut off his own life-span as with an axe upon a tree, so that he may not live to see the third dawn.
Of that Speech whose one syllable stands beyond thousands, and whose branches are ten thousand — let whoever would rob me as I speak in the assembly of that Speech now come to distress.
Dawn kindled the Sun; kindled by Dawn he rose; rising, he shone upon the creatures; he smote away darkness; he gained the eating of food. When darkness is smitten, he becomes an eater of food — whoever knows this.
Wind kindled Fire; kindled by Wind he blazed; he flamed up; he smote away darkness; he gained the eating of food. When darkness is smitten, he becomes an eater of food — whoever knows this.
The mind-formed one kindled the Brahmin student; kindled, he dwelt in brahmacarya; he spoke the Veda in succession; he smote away darkness; he gained the eating of food. When darkness is smitten, he becomes an eater of food — whoever knows this.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
By the oblation, O Prajāpati, I surround this husband and wife for their flourishing and extension. Bestow upon them abundance of wealth, O Savitṛ; grant them death in old age, both fully heroic.
May this oblation go forth increasing the husband and wife — rich in offspring, rich in cattle, of fine heroism. Bestow upon them abundance of wealth, O Savitṛ; grant them death in old age, both fully heroic.
I pour this oblation rich in cattle, rich in livestock, rich in horses for the husband and wife. Bestow upon them abundance of wealth, O Savitṛ; grant them death in old age, both fully heroic.
You are life-giving; may I live; may I live out my full lifespan.
You are sustaining life; may I live upon it; may I live out my full lifespan.
You are conjointly life-giving; may I live altogether; may I live out my full lifespan.
You are the vital ones; may I live; may I live out my full lifespan.
You are the intention of Prajāpati, a thousandfold nourishment. Through the intention of Prajāpati, through the thousandfold nourishment, may I nourish a thousand cattle.
You are the intention of Bṛhaspati, a thousandfold nourishment. Through the intention of Bṛhaspati, through the thousandfold nourishment, may I nourish a thousand cattle.
You are the intention of Brahman, a thousandfold nourishment. Through the intention of Brahman, through the thousandfold nourishment, may I nourish a thousand cattle.
You are Virāj; make me brilliant as Virāj. Of you who are such, may I partake of the glory.
You are Svarāj; make me self-sovereign as Svarāj. Of you who are such, may I partake of the sweetness.
You are Samrāj; make me universally sovereign as Samrāj. Of you who are such, may I partake of the food.
I pour for you the oblation rich in vitality — for life, not for death. I have brought you good strength and fortune; I drive away disease.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
I pour for you the oblation rich in heroic offspring — for life, not for death. I have brought you good strength and fortune; I drive away disease.
I pour for you the oblation rich in fine heroes — for life, not for death. I have brought you good strength and fortune; I drive away disease.
I pour for you the oblation rich in all heroes — for life, not for death. I have brought you good strength and fortune; I drive away disease.
I pour for you the oblation rich in offspring — receive the embryo in the womb. May it be born again in due time, in the tenth month for delivery.
I pour for you the oblation rich in good offspring — receive the embryo in the womb. May it be born again in due time, in the tenth month for delivery.
I pour for you the oblation rich in fine sons — receive the embryo in the womb. May it be born again in due time, in the tenth month for delivery.
I pour for you the oblation for prosperity — O gods, direct your blessing toward this one. May the cattle enter into him, both the four-footed and those that are two-footed.
I pour for you the oblation for wealth — O gods, direct your blessing toward this one. May the cattle enter into him, both the four-footed and those that are two-footed.
I pour for you the oblation with good increase — O gods, direct your blessing toward this one. May the cattle enter into him, both the four-footed and those that are two-footed.
I pour for you the oblation with complete prosperity — O gods, direct your blessing toward this one. May the cattle enter into him, both the four-footed and those that are two-footed.
I pour for you the oblation for peaceful security; may you be settled in security with cattle and heroes. May Indra and Agni, yoked together as companions, together bestow you along with all the gods.
I pour for you the oblation with firm establishment; may you stand firm with cattle and heroes. May Indra and Agni, yoked together as companions, together bestow you along with all the gods.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
I pour for you the oblation with complete becoming; may you come together fully with cattle and heroes. May Indra and Agni, yoked together as companions, together bestow you along with all the gods.
I pour for you the oblation with abundant being; may you excel with cattle and heroes. May Indra and Agni, yoked together as companions, together bestow you along with all the gods.
Those who by thought led speech to its summit, or who by mind declared the truths — waxing great through the third sacred utterance, by the fourth they perceived the name of the milch-cow.
He, the son, came to know his father; he, the son, came to know his mother; he became a son, he became again a munificent one. He disclosed the sky, he the atmosphere, he the sun; he became all the worlds — he came into being.
The Atharvan as father, all-divine; the embryo of the mother, the father bringing together — he who discerned the abode of immortality, who saw the boundaries of eternal wealth.
Some of your forms are auspicious, some are inauspicious — you bear them all without anger. Three forms of speech are hidden in the secret place; from one of them all this world has spread forth.
Aditi is the sky, Aditi the atmosphere, Aditi is the mother, he the father, he the son; all the gods are Aditi, the five peoples are Aditi; Aditi is what has been born, Aditi is what shall be born.
I have made praise for the sons of Aditi, the great sheltering ones, the great and unharmed ones. Their abode indeed is fathomless, reaching the sea; beyond their trembling power there is nothing whatsoever.
At the starting of the vigorous race we shall invoke by speech the great mother, Aditi by name, in whom all this universe has entered — may that goddess, easy to invoke, bestow shelter upon us.
The great mother of those of excellent vows, the wife of cosmic order — we would invoke her for aid: Aditi, of mighty dominion, ever-young, wide-reaching, granting fine shelter, of good guidance.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
The well-protecting earth, the sinless sky, Aditi of fine shelter and good guidance — may we ascend the divine boat, well-oared, faultless and never leaking, for our well-being.
O Vāyu, well-invoked, you travel with one and with ten, with two and twenty for the sacrifice, with three and thirty — unyoke those here, release them now.
By this pervasion he generated glorious deeds; for that radiance is broad for choosing a path. Varuṇa rose up toward the summit of sweetness when he set his own body in motion within himself.
The gods worshipped sacrifice with sacrifice — those were the first cosmic laws. Those great ones attend the vault of heaven where the ancient Sādhya gods abide.
The sacrifice came into being; it fully came into being; it became lord over the earth. It was born, it grew again — may it establish wealth in us.
When the immortal gods worshipped the immortal gods with an oblation, worshipped the deathless with a deathless mind — let us speak of that in the highest heaven, let us utter it at the rising of the sun.
The enchanted gods also worshipped with a dog, and worshipped with the limbs of a cow in many ways. He who by mind discovered this sacrifice — may he proclaim it to us; let us speak of him here and now.
When the gods extended the sacrifice with the primordial being as the oblation — who indeed today could tell us of that, if the oblation-offerers were actually set in motion?
May Indra, the good protector, self-strong, with his aids, gracious and all-knowing, be favorable; may he thrust away enmity and make us fearless — may we be lords of heroic strength.
May that good-protecting, self-strong Indra keep enmity far away from us, away into the distance. May we be in the favor of that worshipful one, abiding in his auspicious goodwill.
Your broad thunder, your towering form, your divine banner that adorns all this world — be merciful to us, O god, with lightning for the crops, and do not strike us down with the rays of the sun.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
That breast of yours, O Sarasvatī, that is richly nourishing, that brings delight, that is grace-giving, easy to invoke and full of skill — the one with which you win all desirable things, set that here for giving nourishment.
This oblation of yours, O Sarasvatī, mixed with ghee — this is the mouth-offering belonging to the ancestors. These most beneficent utterances of yours that have been proclaimed — by these may we become wealthy patrons.
Pūṣan was born on the foremost of paths, on the foremost path of heaven, on the foremost path of earth. Knowing the way, he travels to and fro between both most beloved abodes.
Pūṣan knows all these directions; may he lead us by the most fearless path. A giver of well-being, shining bright, with all heroic power, never neglectful, may he go before us, ever knowing.
May Pūṣan follow our cattle; may Pūṣan protect our horses; may Pūṣan win strength for us.
O Pūṣan, under your vow may we never come to harm at any time. We are your praisers here.
One of your forms is bright, another is worthy of worship; you have two forms of different appearance — you are like the sky. For you protect all creative powers, O self-powerful one. May your bountiful gift be here, O Pūṣan.
May Dhātṛ bestow on the pious man an undiminished, forward-moving life. May we hold in mind the good favor of that god whose law is truth.
May Dhātṛ bestow all things upon the pious man, upon the pious man desiring offspring, in his house. May immortal offspring clothe themselves about him; may all the gods and Aditi, with one accord, be favorable.
May Dhātṛ, Rāti, and Savitṛ be pleased with this; may Prajāpati, lord of treasures, our Agni — may Tvaṣṭṛ, delighting in offspring together with Pūṣan, bestow wealth upon the sacrificer.
Dhātṛ rules over offspring and over wealth; Dhātṛ generated this entire universe. May abundant nourishment be conveyed to the pious man — to that god let us offer homage with an oblation.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
For you, O god, have set forth for the primal Father his full stature and his breadth. Now, O Savitṛ, press out for us desirable gifts twofold, along with abundant cattle.
Go forward from the good to the better; let Bṛhaspati be your forerunner. Then make this man, in the choicest part of this earth, one who has driven off enemies, possessed of all heroic men.
The god Savitṛ, dwelling in the house, most excellent, bestowing wealth, vigor, and long lives upon the fathers — may he drink soma, may he exhilarate this man at the sacrifice; even the wide-roaming one delights in his holy ordinance.
That brilliant gift of Savitṛ of true might, of the god, at his impulsion, do we win — that which Kaṇva milked for the great bull, the full-uddered cow of thousandfold streams, for the sustaining.
Who among the nobles, desiring better fortune, will lead us out of this blameworthy hostility? Who desires the fulfillment of vows? Who desires sacrifice? Who wins long life among the gods?
Who, milking by friendship with Bṛhaspati the dappled cow given by Varuṇa to the Atharvan — easy to milk, ever with her calf — shall make the body prosper according to his will?
Heat has not scorched him, nor has cold struck him down; the earth, the swift-flowing, streams forth for him. Even the waters flow for him unceasingly; where soma is, there is blessing evermore.
In whose quarter of the sky this shines forth, toward Anumati do the descendants adorn themselves; whose lap is the wide atmosphere — may she grant us abundant shelter.
May Anumati today guide our sacrifice to the gods; may Agni, the carrier of oblations, be a source of joy for the one who has given.
For truly, O Anumati, you will consent; bring welfare to us. Bestow nourishment upon our offspring; extend our lifespans for us.
May the consenting Anumati consent — the nourishment rich in progeny, never diminishing. May we not fall into her wrath; may that goddess, easy to invoke, grant us shelter.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
O Anumati, consent to those deeds of ours — whatever we have done with our bodies; whatever has been done regarding offspring, regarding bodies, regarding progeny, among cattle, among herbs, within the waters.
May divine Anumati, well-born, possessed of good dominion and heroic power, come to us. For her guidance has been benevolent; may she protect this sacrifice beloved by the gods.
Anumati begot all this — whatever trembles, whatever moves, and whatever stands still. May I be in the good grace of her, O goddess Anumati; for you, O Anumati, will indeed consent to us.
By that name of yours which is easy to invoke, O well-guiding Anumati, agreed upon and good to bestow — by that name, O goddess, swell nourishment for us, all-desired and rich in heroes, with benevolent thought.
I consecrate you for progeny; may progeny breathe after you; breathe life into the progeny. I buy your brightness with brightness, your radiance with radiance, your immortality with immortality.
You are the body of austerity, the color of Prajāpati. You are purchased with the supreme sacrificial animal.
I praise that god Savitṛ, of poet-wisdom, hidden within the two woolen strands, of true impulse, the bestower of gems, with a beloved thought.
He whose upward-shooting thought blazed with light at his impulsion — golden-handed and of excellent resolve, he measured out the sky with grace.
This one, the thought of seers, measuring out a thousand, the light in the ordinance — may the radiant one drive together the meeting dawns.
Sinless, like-minded, on the day of Svā, most full of spirit — at the recognition of the cow.
Come together, all, with might toward the lord of heaven, who alone has truly been the guest of peoples. That ancient one, making the new shine forth — the track has turned back around him alone, everywhere.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
I call with repeated invocation the divine Kuhū, the immortal, the skilled in work, the easy to invoke, in this sacrifice. She who gives us the hearing of the ancestors — to you, O goddess, we render worship with oblation.
May Kuhū, consort of immortality among the gods, hear our oblation of this offering. Abundantly nourished, may she pour forth blessings upon the one who gives; may she bestow flourishing of riches upon the wise one.
Come to agreement together; come to union together; let your minds know one another. May Mitra unite all of you together; may there be concord among you with me.
Whatever Agni has granted us, whatever Indra, whatever all the gods, the Maruts bright with light — may Savitā of true ordinance, Sarasvatī, and Anumati bestow that upon us.
O gods, for the sake of both kinds of welfare, grant shelter to our two-footed and four-footed creatures. One who eats, who drinks, who is nourished with strength and is well-fed — establish for us that state of well-being and ease, free from affliction.
O Bṛhaspati, O Savitā, awaken him; though already sharpened, whet him yet more keenly. Make him grow for great good fortune; may all the gods rejoice after him.
May he thrive yonder beyond what Yama holds; Bṛhaspati has released him from the accusation. May those two Aśvins, the healers of the gods, push back death from him, O Agni, with their skills.
O Indra and Varuṇa, you two who are drinkers of the pressed, drink this pressed, intoxicating soma, you who hold firm to your vows. Your chariot comes to the rite for the delight of the gods, comes at daybreak for the drinking.
O Indra and Varuṇa, you two bulls, drink your fill of the most sweetly intoxicating, vigorous soma. This drink has been poured out for you two among us; be seated on this sacred grass and be exhilarated.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Step wide, O Viṣṇu; make a broad dwelling space. Drink the ghee, O you born from ghee; lead forward, forward the lord of the sacrifice.
From the sky, O Viṣṇu, or from the earth, or from the wide, great middle-space — fill both your hands with sweetness; reach them out, from the right and from the left.
Now let me proclaim the heroic deeds of Viṣṇu, who measured out the earthly realms, who propped up the upper abode as he strode forth — the wide-pacing one who strides in three ways.
Viṣṇu proclaims those heroic deeds: like a fearsome wild beast that roams and dwells on the mountains — in whose three wide strides all the worlds abide.
O Agni and Viṣṇu, great is your dear abode; guard the secret names of ghee. Bearing the seven treasures in house after house, may the tongue move toward you laden with ghee.
O Agni and Viṣṇu, great is that greatness of yours; enjoy the secret gifts of ghee. Growing with excellent praise in house after house, may the tongue rise up to you with ghee.
Raise up the earth; pierce open this heavenly cloud. O Dhātṛ, lord and sovereign of the heavenly udder, open wide the aperture for us.
Moving away from the human realm, praising the divine might — turn back toward our leadings, O god, enjoying the friendship of the gods.
I worship the lord of nourishment through nourishment — Dhātṛ, the ordainer, in these worlds. By the half-measure be sweet for me here; by the half-measure be the equator now for that one yonder.
This nourishing one has been brought with nourishment beyond; let this one hear what I say. By the half-measure be sweet for me here; by the half-measure be the equator now for that one yonder.
Here seize him, O Nirṛti; here destroy him, O Nirṛti; here cut him entirely away. By the half-measure be sweet for me here; by the half-measure be the equator now for that one yonder.

title: Atharvaveda (Paippalāda)
text:
Whatever I invoke of you, O Nourishment, hear that for me; be one to be invoked in this call of mine. Nirṛti, conspiring together with the gods, severs that one yonder from the snare of Varuṇa.
Whatever sin we have committed through forgetfulness, whatever we have come upon with our steps, O Jātavedas — from that protect us, O wise one, for good fortune; lead us and our friends to immortality.
O Agni, overseer, come to us; protect us from misfortune, protect us from evil dreams. Protect us from disease of the mouth and from all other afflictions.
You are radiance; may we become full of radiance — possessed of vision, rich in cattle, rich in progeny, and full of splendor.
The milk you collect by day, the milk you carry in your udders — that milk of yours, O all-formed ones, I take away with a herb.
The sweetness you cows gather from herbs, from waters — that milk of yours, O all-formed ones, I take away with a plant.
You who press down upon one — seek out a sleeping man, one who lies there listless. May Varuṇa enfold us with armor of iron, with armor of stone.
